sections.text:
General-purpose embodied manipulation hinges on a unified action representation that generalizes across embodiments and scales readily. Yet existing policies rely on embodiment-specific action spaces, making cross-embodiment demonstrations difficult to leverage at scale and limiting transfer to new embodiments and spatial variations.

To this end, we introduce Universal Manipulation Representation (UMR), a unified action representation that enables zero-shot skill transfer from human demonstrations to heterogeneous robots.

UMR decomposes manipulation into two functionally distinct yet geometrically linked components: embodiment-agnostic World Flow, which describes task-relevant object motion in the world frame, and Ego Trajectory, which represents end-effector motion relative to the current pose.

We instantiate UMR as World--Ego Point VLA (WEPVLA), a compact 0.5B-parameter policy that learns in the unified geometric action space through a dual-stream Point Action Adapter and a unified Point Action Expert, with an $SE（3）$ conjugation coupling the two components.

To improve data efficiency, we complement UMR with a Data-Efficient Strategy (DES) that diversifies object configurations through stage-aware point-cloud editing while preserving demonstrated contact geometry. In simulation, WEPVLA achieves average success rates of 97.5\% on LIBERO and 85.7\% on the 10-task RLBench benchmark.

In real-world experiments, a single policy trained on human demonstrations augmented by DES transfers zero-shot to diverse deployment conditions. With about 10 minutes of collected human demonstrations per task and no robot demonstrations, it achieves 91.7\% average success across six evaluation settings, compared with 60.8\% for HumanEgo.

Code and additional materials are available at https://umr-wepvla.github.io/.

summary.en: The paper introduces Universal Manipulation Representation (UMR), separating task-relevant object motion in world coordinates from end-effector motion relative to its current pose, to support zero-shot transfer from human demonstrations to heterogeneous robots. Its WEPVLA implementation is paired with a data-efficient strategy that diversifies object configurations through stage-aware point-cloud editing while preserving demonstrated contact geometry. The authors report benchmark success rates in simulation and real-world results in which one policy trained on human demonstrations transfers across deployment conditions and outperforms the comparison method.
summary.zh: 论文提出通用操作表示 UMR，将操作分为描述任务相关物体世界坐标运动的 World Flow，以及描述末端执行器相对当前姿态运动的 Ego Trajectory，并以此支持从人类演示向不同机器人零样本迁移。作者将其实现为 WEPVLA，并配套使用通过阶段感知点云编辑扩展物体配置、同时保留演示接触几何的数据高效策略。在仿真基准上报告了成功率；真实实验中，单一策略仅用人类演示训练并迁移至多种部署条件，表现优于所比较方法。

items.title: UMR: Universal Manipulation Representation

sections.text:
Open-set task execution can significantly benefit from seamlessly switching between coarse and fine scene representations depending on the context and the evolving information as the robot explores the environment.

For example, it is often sufficient to start with a coarse scene representation initially and only employ a finer, more granular scene representation when the robot encounters regions which are likely to contain the task relevant objects. Hence, in this work, we propose BiMoSG, a bimodal 3D scene graph generation approach for open-set tasks.

BiMoSG employs a "fast" mode by default to efficiently generate a coarse 3D scene graph and can switch to a "slow" mode for generating a finer open vocabulary 3D scene graph of task relevant objects. We demonstrate that our proposed 3D scene graph generation approach is significantly faster than the open-source state-of-the-art approaches.

This allows us to integrate the scene graph generation process with task execution for real-time deployment.

summary.en: The paper proposes BiMoSG, a bimodal 3D scene graph generation approach for open-set tasks. It uses a fast mode by default to create a coarse graph and can switch to a slow mode that generates a finer, open-vocabulary graph when exploration reaches regions likely to contain task-relevant objects. The authors state that their approach is significantly faster than open-source state-of-the-art approaches, enabling integration of scene graph generation with task execution for real-time deployment. The abstract gives no specific test setting or quantitative speed results.
summary.zh: 论文提出 BiMoSG，一种面向开放集任务的双模态三维场景图生成方法。它默认采用“快”模式生成粗略场景图，并可在机器人探索到可能包含任务相关物体的区域时切换到“慢”模式，生成更精细的开放词汇场景图。作者称，该方法比开源先进方法显著更快，并据此将场景图生成与任务执行结合，以支持实时部署。摘要未说明具体实验场景或量化速度数据。

items.title: Seeing Fast and Slow: Bimodal 3D Scene Graphs for Open-set Tasks

sections.text:
Contrastive Reinforcement Learning (CRL) learns representations that estimate goal reachability, yet its policy remains conditioned on raw goals and therefore does not directly exploit the geometry encoded by its critic.

We introduce Direction-Conditioned Policies (DCP), a method built around a small modification to CRL: DCP selects previously visited states as waypoints during online training and conditions the policy on their direction and distance in representation space.

At deployment, DCP applies the same interface directly to the final goal, requiring neither waypoint selection nor planning. Across nine navigation and manipulation tasks, DCP attains higher final success rates than CRL on seven tasks and spends more time near the goal on seven.

Controlled maze experiments further show that DCP captures shortest-path geometry more accurately and that the supplied direction causally influences the actor's behavior. We identify waypoint coverage and ranking as limits to exploration, and show that learned candidate generation improves goal reaching in two controlled mazes.

summary.en: The paper presents Direction-Conditioned Policies (DCP), which use previously visited states as training waypoints and condition the policy on their direction and distance in representation space. At deployment, the same interface is applied directly to the final goal, without waypoint selection or planning. Across nine navigation and manipulation tasks, DCP has higher final success rates than CRL on seven and spends more time near the goal on seven. Controlled maze experiments indicate more accurate shortest-path geometry and a causal effect of supplied direction on behavior. The authors identify waypoint coverage and ranking as exploration limits and report improved goal reaching from learned candidate generation in two controlled mazes.
summary.zh: 论文提出方向条件策略 DCP，用已访问状态作为在线训练中的航点，并让策略以这些航点在表征空间中的方向和距离为条件；部署时则直接对最终目标使用相同接口，无需选取航点或规划。在九项导航与操作任务中，DCP 在七项任务上的最终成功率高于 CRL，并在七项任务中有更多时间接近目标。受控迷宫实验显示其更准确地捕捉最短路径几何，且方向输入会因果性地影响行为。作者还指出航点覆盖和排序会限制探索，并报告候选生成改善了两个受控迷宫中的目标到达。

items.title: Direction-Conditioned Policies for Online Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning

sections.text:
Both Remotely Operated underwater Vehicles (ROVs) and Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) are frequently deployed to acquire geometric bathymetric data. However, it is often discovered post-survey that the acquired data coverage is incomplete.

Given the high operational cost associated with underwater deployments, it is essential to incrementally visualize surface coverage in real-time to support informed decision-making by both the operators of ROVs and the AUVs during data collection.

In addition, traditional incremental surface reconstruction methods, such as Digital Terrain Models (DTMs), are inherently limited in expressiveness: they represent surfaces as height fields, allows only one elevation value per $(x, y)$ coordinate and thus cannot capture overhangs or vertical structures.

To overcome these limitations, we adapt the original Ball Pivoting Algorithm (BPA) into an incremental, real-time, and free-form surface reconstruction method, referred to as Incremental BPA (IBPA).

Our method incrementally constructs an orientable, manifold mesh from streaming point cloud data without imposing assumptions regarding point cloud overlap or spatial distribution. Furthermore, we introduce a hole detection mechanism that identifies and highlights incomplete mesh regions.

Compared to existing approaches, our method supports more complex surface topologies without prior structural assumptions. The source code of our reference implementation is available: https://github.com/Mauhing/Incremental-BPA

summary.en: The paper presents Incremental BPA (IBPA), a method for real-time free-form surface mesh reconstruction from streaming point clouds, motivated by incomplete underwater survey coverage and the limits of height-field models in representing overhangs or vertical structures. It incrementally constructs an orientable manifold mesh without assumptions about point-cloud overlap or spatial distribution, and adds hole detection to identify and highlight incomplete regions. The authors state that, compared with existing approaches, IBPA supports more complex surface topologies without prior structural assumptions. The abstract provides no quantitative comparison results.
summary.zh: 论文提出增量球旋转算法 IBPA，用于从流式点云实时重建自由形状表面网格，以应对水下测绘数据覆盖不完整及高度场模型无法表达悬垂或垂直结构的局限。该方法逐步构建可定向的流形网格，不对点云重叠或空间分布作假设，并加入孔洞检测机制以识别和突出显示不完整区域。作者称，与现有方法相比，IBPA 支持更复杂的表面拓扑，且不需要预先设定结构假设。摘要未提供定量比较结果。

items.title: IBPA: Real-time Free-form Manifold Mesh Reconstruction via Incremental Ball Pivoting with Integrated Hole Detection

sections.text:
When a team of robots delegates planning and mutual trust to LLM agents, a single compromised robot can corrupt the shared outcome. We study this threat in a grounded task: a multi-robot survey in which measurements can be verified against the physical world, but every verification costs budget that would otherwise advance the mission.

We treat the compromised robot as a stealthy adversary in the system-theoretic sense: it is limited not by an energy bound but by the team's own detectors. We then derive two bounds. First, the probability that the adversary's reports are verified is bounded below in terms of the degrees in the communication graph and the verification budget.

Second, the map error caused by any stealthy adversary is bounded above by the value of a linear program over the adversary's bias distributions; its solution is an exchange rate between stealth budget and damage: below a critical verification level the worst stealthy attack tells rare, full-magnitude lies on the records least likely to be verified, and above it the better purchase is small biases hidden in the noise.

In experiments where the honest robots are LLM agents, both bounds hold at the budget the attack actually spent. The experiments also show that which records an LLM robot re-checks is unbiased, but how much it re-checks is unpredictable.

summary.en: The paper studies stealthy corruption by one compromised robot in an LLM-coordinated multi-robot surveying task where measurements can be checked against the physical world. It derives a lower bound on report verification probability based on communication-graph degrees and verification budget, and an upper bound on map error through a linear program over attack biases. The authors claim that low verification favors rare, full-scale lies, while higher verification favors small biases hidden in noise. LLM-robot experiments support both bounds at the budget spent.
summary.zh: 论文研究由 LLM 智能体协调的多机器人测绘任务中，单个受损机器人如何隐蔽地篡改共享结果。作者给出两项界限：通信图结构和核验预算共同约束虚假报告被核验的概率；隐蔽攻击造成的地图误差受一个关于偏差分布的线性规划上界约束。作者声称，核验不足时最有利的攻击是对较少被核验的记录偶尔撒大谎，核验较充分时则以小偏差隐藏在噪声中。LLM 机器人实验显示，在攻击实际使用的预算下两项界限成立；重查哪些记录没有偏向，但重查多少不可预测。

items.title: Lie Rarely, Lie Big: Stealthy Insider Attacks on LLM Robot Teams

sections.text:
World models learn to predict how their environment will evolve, making them an important foundation for general-purpose robotic control. Yet world action models depend on camera inputs whose manipulation can corrupt the visual representations used across tasks and action policies.

Existing attacks on these models optimize against the victim's actions or predicted futures and therefore require access to target-model outputs. In this paper, we propose an attack, TAPDreamer, against world action models that instead uses a public encoder alone to construct a fixed local perturbation that transfers across tasks and action architectures.

TAPDreamer requires no target-policy queries. Our key insight is that interactions between patch-induced changes in attention weights and value vectors broadcast a nearly identical representation shift far beyond the patch footprint, and this shift remains stable across task observations.

Guided by this insight, TAPDreamer uses six frames from one source task to maximize the global L1 distance between clean and patched encoder representations.

In closed-loop evaluation, one frozen patch per benchmark, covering about 6.5% of the input, reduces FastWAM's success rate from 97.7% to 0.0% across 40 LIBERO tasks and from 90.86% to 0.0% across 50 RoboTwin tasks; matched random patches retain 81.5% and 79.2% success.

The same patches reduce success to 1.45% and 1.00% on two DreamWAM configurations and to 10.60% on Motus. These results show that protecting downstream action generation alone is insufficient: defenses for world action models must also secure shared visual encoders against persistent local perturbations.

summary.en: The paper proposes TAPDreamer, an attack on world action models that uses only a public encoder to create a fixed adversarial patch and requires no target-policy queries. The authors attribute transfer to a stable representation shift caused by patch-induced changes in attention weights and value vectors. They optimize using six frames from one source task. In closed-loop evaluations, patches covering about 6.5% of the input sharply reduced success rates across reported models and tasks; these findings are limited to the stated evaluation settings.
summary.zh: 论文提出 TAPDreamer，一种仅使用公开编码器构造对抗补丁、无需查询目标策略的世界动作模型攻击方法。作者认为，补丁改变注意力权重和值向量后，会在补丁区域之外造成近似一致且跨任务稳定的表征偏移；方法用单一源任务的六帧优化全局表征距离。闭环评估中，每个基准使用一个覆盖约6.5%输入的固定补丁，在多个模型与任务上显著降低成功率；结果限于所报告的评估设置。

items.title: TAPDreamer: Transferable Adversarial Patches for World Action Models

sections.text:
Embodied world models predict the visual consequences of candidate actions before execution. However, existing action-conditioned world models often adopt uniformly weighted visual generation objectives that can be misaligned with embodied prediction needs.

Even with explicit motion conditioning, these objectives can underemphasize spatially sparse changes that are critical to interaction. We propose KineWorld, a transport-aware world-modeling framework that extends robot kinematics from motion conditioning to the spatial allocation of generative supervision.

Kinematic Transport Lifting (KTL) constructs renderer-derived, camera-aligned transport fields from commanded robot motion. Transport-Aware World Diffusion (TAWD) calibrates their motion support on the video-latent grid and reweights future-RGB flow matching through a normalized mixture of uniform and transport-focused distributions.

We train KineWorld using ALOHA-AgileX bimanual manipulation data from RoboTwin 2.0.KineWorld achieves an EWMScore-P of 68.95 in single-view evaluation and a TWB-Score of 54.82 in multi-view evaluation. These results support a shift from appearance fitting toward action-consequence modeling for embodied decision-making.

summary.en: The paper presents KineWorld, an embodied world-modeling framework that uses robot kinematics to allocate spatial generative supervision. Kinematic Transport Lifting builds camera-aligned transport fields from commanded motion; Transport-Aware World Diffusion calibrates motion support on the video-latent grid and reweights future-RGB flow matching with a mixture of uniform and transport-focused distributions. The model is trained on ALOHA-AgileX bimanual manipulation data from RoboTwin 2.0. The authors report an EWMScore-P of 68.95 in single-view evaluation and a TWB-Score of 54.82 in multi-view evaluation.
summary.zh: 论文提出 KineWorld，一种将机器人运动学用于空间生成监督分配的具身世界模型框架。其运动学传输提升模块根据指令运动构建与相机对齐的传输场；传输感知世界扩散模块在视频潜在网格上校准运动支持，并通过均匀与聚焦传输场的混合分布重加权未来 RGB 流匹配。模型使用 RoboTwin 2.0 的 ALOHA-AgileX 双臂操作数据训练。作者报告，单视角评估的 EWMScore-P 为 68.95，多视角评估的 TWB-Score 为 54.82，并认为结果支持从外观拟合转向动作后果建模。

items.title: KineWorld: Action-Induced Transport Fields for Embodied World Modeling

sections.text:
Transferring visual representations pretrained on human videos to robot manipulation requires learning reliable correspondences between human and robot demonstrations. However, paired demonstrations can differ in execution rate and in the proportion of non-key frames that do not directly reflect task progress.

Frames at the same relative timestamp may therefore represent different task stages, which can cause correspondence learning to fail. To address these issues, we propose Frame-Level Temporal Alignment (FLTA), a framework that uses two temporal priors to adapt visual encoders pretrained on human videos for robot manipulation.

It learns shared task-progress representations without frame-level correspondence annotations, allowing frames at different relative temporal positions to match. A global progress prior combines normalized temporal positions with visual similarity to construct a soft correspondence target.

A local temporal order prior penalizes backward transitions while allowing stays and varying forward rates to accommodate execution-rate differences.

With ResNet-50 and ViT encoders, our method achieves relative improvements of 46.93% and 65.96%, respectively, over the best baselines in average simulation success rates and achieves higher task success rates on real-world manipulation tasks.

These results also suggest that effective human-robot adaptation depends less on the number of parameters updated than on which parameters are selected. Our project page is available at https://rtx5090ultra.github.io/FLTA-Project-Page/.

summary.en: The paper introduces Frame-Level Temporal Alignment (FLTA) to adapt visual encoders pretrained on human videos for robot manipulation. Without frame-level correspondence labels, it matches demonstrations at different relative time positions using a global task-progress prior and a local temporal-order prior that permits stays and varying forward rates. With ResNet-50 and ViT encoders, the authors report relative improvements of 46.93% and 65.96% over the best baselines in average simulation success rates, and higher success on real-world manipulation tasks. They suggest parameter selection matters more than the number updated.
summary.zh: 论文提出帧级时间对齐（FLTA），用于将在人类视频上预训练的视觉编码器适配到机器人操作。该方法通过全局任务进度先验和局部时间顺序先验，在无需帧级对应标注的情况下，匹配相对时间位置不同的演示帧，并允许停留及不同的前进速度。使用 ResNet-50 和 ViT 编码器时，作者报告仿真平均成功率较最佳基线分别相对提升 46.93% 和 65.96%，真实操作任务成功率也更高。作者还指出，适配效果可能更取决于选择更新哪些参数，而非更新参数数量。

items.title: Frame-Level Temporal Alignment for Human-to-Robot Visual Adaptation

sections.text:
Learning from human demonstrations is a reliable way to teach robots new tasks, but the gains from each additional demonstration shrink as the policy improves. Continued improvement can instead come from supervised deployment, where an operator places the objects and intervenes when the policy fails.

We ask how to maximize improvement from a fixed budget of supervised episodes on high-precision manipulation tasks with wide ranges of object placements. We observe that failures can concentrate in a small subset of initial states, so uniform collection spends much of the operator's time on states the policy already handles.

Mulligan makes the initial-state distribution a decision, starting each round's episodes at observed failures and untried states. To further improve data efficiency, we augment interactive imitation learning with a value function trained on all data, including failures that imitation discards.

Across three real-world tasks evaluated on 2,550 held-out, blinded episodes and two simulated tasks, Mulligan outperforms uniform initial-state sampling at matched collection budgets, and combined with value-based action selection, HiL-IDQL+Mulligan, improves final real-task success by 10-34 percentage points.

With operator interventions, the human-robot team completes 98% of collection episodes, remaining productive while the policy learns. Videos, code, and data are available at https://mulligan.page/.

summary.en: Mulligan targets efficient data collection for high-precision manipulation under a fixed budget of supervised episodes. It selects initial states from observed failures and untried states, and trains a value function using all collected data, including failures omitted by imitation learning. Across three real-world tasks evaluated in held-out, blinded episodes and two simulated tasks, the authors report better performance than uniform sampling at matched budgets. Combined with value-based action selection, it improves final real-task success by 10–34 percentage points; operator interventions enable completion of 98% of collection episodes.
summary.zh: Mulligan针对高精度操作任务，研究如何在固定监督回合预算下更有效地收集机器人学习数据。该方法根据观察到的失败状态和未尝试状态选择每轮初始状态，并利用包括失败数据在内的全部数据训练价值函数。在三项真实任务的留出盲测回合及两项仿真任务中，作者报告其在相同采集预算下优于均匀采样；结合基于价值的动作选择后，真实任务最终成功率提高10至34个百分点。操作员介入时，采集回合完成率为98%。

items.title: Mulligan: Performance-Guided Data Collection for Efficient On-Robot Learning

sections.text:
Learning robot policies directly on physical systems remains difficult because data collection is costly and policy exploration can be unsafe. We introduce Visual and Motor Policies from Sampling-Based Planning (VAMPS), a framework that uses Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control to train reusable policies without human demonstrations.

VAMPS supports two training modes. For one-step proprioceptive policies, it operates iteratively in simulation: the policy warm-starts MPPI, and the refined trajectories provide new supervision as the policy changes. A learned terminal value improves short-horizon planning, while an Implicit Q-Learning (IQL) critic guides the policy update.

Iterative refinement outperforms training once on frozen MPPI data, and we transfer the learned locomotion policy to a Unitree Go2.For visuomotor policies, VAMPS operates directly from real-robot data. MPPI uses task-specific state estimates to plan and execute trajectories while recording RGB and sensor observations on a Flexiv Rizon 10S.

Action Chunking with Transformers predicts action chunks, reducing the effective prediction horizon, and is trained offline on this fixed dataset. We demonstrate visuomotor pick-and-place and force-aware whiteboard erasing. In the latter task, the policy additionally observes the measured $6$-D wrench and desired normal force.

These results show that VAMPS can learn policies either in simulation followed by hardware transfer or directly from autonomously collected real-robot data.

summary.en: VAMPS uses sampling-based planning to train robot policies without human demonstrations, through either simulation followed by hardware transfer or direct collection of real-robot data. For proprioceptive policies, the method iteratively uses the policy to warm-start MPPI and obtains supervision from refined trajectories, with a learned terminal value and an IQL critic supporting policy updates. The authors report that iterative refinement outperforms training once on frozen MPPI data and transfer a locomotion policy to hardware. For visuomotor policies, autonomous MPPI data collection supports offline training for pick-and-place and force-aware whiteboard erasing.
summary.zh: VAMPS利用基于采样的规划训练无需人工示范的机器人策略，涵盖仿真训练后迁移和直接使用真实机器人数据两种方式。对于本体感觉策略，方法迭代地以策略初始化MPPI规划，并用改进轨迹提供监督，同时结合学习到的终端价值和IQL评论器更新策略；作者称迭代优化优于一次性使用固定MPPI数据训练，并将运动策略迁移至硬件。对于视觉运动策略，MPPI在Flexiv机器人上自主规划并采集图像与传感器数据，再离线训练动作分块模型；展示任务包括视觉抓放和感知力的白板擦除。

items.title: VAMPS: Visual and Motor Policies from Sampling-Based Planning

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action models (WAMs) often degrade under out-of-distribution task variations despite retaining partial task capability.

To recover such capability, we propose RoboIRS, an inference-time internal representation steering method that uses successful and failed rollouts to train linear classifiers, select outcome-relevant intervention locations, and derive task-specific steering directions without updating policy parameters.

On 15 simulation tasks with a frozen $\pi 0.5$ policy, RoboIRS improves the average success rate from 44.4% to 66.2%, outperforming alternative inference-time intervention baselines while adding little inference time.

We further validate RoboIRS on real-robot manipulation using the same $\pi 0.5$ policy and demonstrate its applicability to a world-action model Cosmos Policy, where the average success rate improves from 35.4% to 55.4%.

These results show that directly steering internal robot-policy representations can improve the performance of robot policies at inference time. Project website is available at https://rollingoat.github.io/roboirs/.

summary.en: RoboIRS is an inference-time representation-steering method intended to recover capabilities that vision-language-action and world-action models retain under out-of-distribution task variations. It uses successful and failed rollouts to train linear classifiers, identify outcome-relevant intervention locations, and derive task-specific steering directions without changing policy parameters. On simulation tasks with a frozen π0.5 policy, the reported average success rate rises from 44.4% to 66.2%. The authors also report real-robot manipulation validation and an improvement with Cosmos Policy, supporting the method’s use for inference-time policy enhancement.
summary.zh: RoboIRS是一种推理时内部表征引导方法，旨在恢复视觉语言动作模型和世界动作模型在分布外任务变化下保留的部分能力。它使用成功与失败的运行轨迹训练线性分类器，选择与结果相关的干预位置并生成任务特定的引导方向，而不更新策略参数。在冻结的π0.5策略上，仿真任务平均成功率由44.4%升至66.2%；作者还报告了真实机器人操作验证，并在Cosmos Policy上观察到平均成功率提升。结果支持该方法可在推理阶段改善机器人策略表现。

items.title: RoboIRS: Inference-Time Internal Representation Steering for Generalist Robot Policies

While this method was primarily investigated for legged robot locomotion in the past, it can be more generally applicable to other types of robotic systems. sections.text:
Virtual Model Control (VMC) is an approach to design a controller for force-controlled robots in complex uncertain environments. While this method was primarily investigated for legged robot locomotion in the past, it can be more generally applicable to other types of robotic systems.

This paper investigates the VMC framework for reaching tasks in a force-controlled robotic arm. We propose six different approaches to designing virtual models in order to achieve reaching tasks in environments with obstacles and uncertainties. A force-controlled 8 degree-of-freedom humanoid robot was used to validate the proposed approach in the real world.

We conducted three experiments to test the performance of VMC controllers in terms of predictability, sensitivity to external force, and adaptability against known and unknown obstacles.

Experimental analyses show that, even though the proposed approach needs to sacrifice accuracy and trajectory optimality, it enables us to design complex reaching motions under uncertainties, in an intuitive and extendable manner.

summary.en: This paper investigates Virtual Model Control (VMC) for reaching tasks with a force-controlled robotic arm in uncertain environments, and proposes six approaches to designing virtual models. The approach is validated in the real world using an eight-degree-of-freedom force-controlled humanoid robot. Three experiments examine controller predictability, sensitivity to external forces, and adaptability to known and unknown obstacles. The experimental analysis indicates a trade-off: the approach sacrifices some accuracy and trajectory optimality, while enabling intuitive and extensible design of complex reaching motions under uncertainty.
summary.zh: 本文研究虚拟模型控制（VMC）在力控机械臂不确定环境下执行到达任务的应用，并提出六种虚拟模型设计方法。研究使用一台八自由度力控人形机器人进行真实环境验证，通过三项实验考察控制器的可预测性、对外力的敏感性，以及对已知和未知障碍物的适应能力。实验分析表明，该方法需要牺牲一定精度和轨迹最优性，但作者认为它能够以直观且可扩展的方式设计不确定条件下的复杂到达运动。

items.title: Virtual model control for compliant reaching under uncertainties

sections.text:
This paper presents sparse calibration-based personalization for kernel-based gait phase and walking speed co-estimation from wearable inertial measurement units (IMUs).A 28-speed reference library was constructed from bilateral thigh and shank trajectories in a 20-subject locomotion dataset.

Rather than directly applying population-average kernels, the method combines a user-specific baseline estimated from three calibration speeds with a principal-component (PC) model of baseline-centered kinematic deviations. Offline validation showed that personalized kernels reduced phase error relative to the population kernel.

In a single-participant online pilot evaluation, the personalized kernels produced numerically lower mean phase and speed errors and ran in real time on embedded hardware. However, the speed effect was not significant, and pairwise phase differences did not remain significant after multiple-comparison correction.

The pilot evaluation establishes wearable implementation feasibility while indicating reference-to-online dataset mismatch and the need for larger-cohort validation.

summary.en: The paper presents sparse calibration-based personalization for estimating gait phase and walking speed from wearable IMUs. It estimates a user-specific baseline from three calibration speeds and models baseline-centered kinematic deviations with principal components. Offline validation found lower phase error than with a population kernel. In a single-participant online pilot, personalized kernels had numerically lower mean phase and speed errors and ran in real time on embedded hardware. The speed effect was not significant, and phase differences did not remain significant after multiple-comparison correction. The authors note dataset mismatch and the need for larger-cohort validation.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种基于稀疏校准的个性化方法，用可穿戴惯性测量单元同时估计步态相位和行走速度。方法以三种校准速度估计个人基线，并结合基线中心化运动学偏差的主成分模型。离线验证显示，个性化核的相位误差低于总体核。单参与者在线试点中，相位和速度平均误差数值较低，并可在嵌入式硬件实时运行；但速度效果不显著，经过多重比较校正后相位差异也未保持显著。作者指出数据集不匹配，并认为仍需更大队列验证。

items.title: Sparse Calibration-Based Personalization of Kernel-Based Gait Phase and Speed Estimation Using Wearable IMUs

sections.text:
Imitation learning, also known as learning from demonstrations, is a popular approach to train AI models; however, the vulnerability of these models to adversarial attacks remains underexplored.

We present the first systematic study of adversarial attacks, across a range of both classic and recently proposed imitation learning algorithms, including Vanilla Behavior Cloning (Vanilla BC), LSTM-GMM, Implicit Behavior Cloning (IBC), Diffusion Policy (DP), and Vector-Quantized Behavior Transformer (VQ-BET).

We study the vulnerability of these methods to white-box, grey-box and black-box adversarial perturbations. Our experiments reveal that most existing methods are highly vulnerable to these attacks, including black-box transfer attacks that transfer across algorithms.

White-box attacks cause at least a 65% reduction in average task success across all evaluated tasks and algorithms, while the black-box transfer attacks reduce task success by up to 88% on Lift, 99% on Can, and 100% on Square.

To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to study and compare the vulnerabilities of different popular imitation learning algorithms to both white-box and black-box attacks. Our findings highlight the vulnerabilities of modern imitation learning algorithms, paving the way for future work in addressing such limitations.

Videos and code are available at https://sites.google.com/view/uap-attacks-on-bc.

summary.en: The paper systematically studies adversarial vulnerabilities across several imitation learning methods, including Vanilla BC, LSTM-GMM, IBC, Diffusion Policy, and VQ-BET. It evaluates white-box, grey-box, and black-box perturbations. Experiments show that most evaluated methods are highly vulnerable, including to black-box transfer attacks across algorithms. White-box attacks reduce average task success by at least 65% across all evaluated tasks and algorithms. Black-box transfer attacks reduce success by up to 88% on Lift, 99% on Can, and 100% on Square. The authors describe this as the first comparison of these vulnerabilities across popular methods.
summary.zh: 论文系统比较多种模仿学习策略对对抗扰动的脆弱性，涵盖白盒、灰盒和黑盒攻击，以及 Vanilla BC、LSTM-GMM、IBC、Diffusion Policy 和 VQ-BET。实验显示，多数受评估方法容易受到攻击，包括跨算法迁移的黑盒攻击。白盒攻击在所有评估任务和算法中使平均任务成功率至少下降65%；黑盒迁移攻击在 Lift、Can 和 Square 任务中的成功率降幅分别最高达88%、99%和100%。作者称这是对这些常用策略相关脆弱性的首次研究和比较。

items.title: How Vulnerable Is My Learned Policy? Universal Adversarial Perturbation Attacks On Modern Behavior Cloning Policies

sections.text:
Human--robot co-transportation of deformable objects requires predicting object deformation during motion, since obstacle clearance depends on both the grasp points and the unactuated interior. We present a hierarchical planning framework that combines a learned cloth model with a reduced-order whole-body model of a dual-arm mobile manipulator.

A physics-residual conditional recurrent variational autoencoder (p-cRVAE) predicts the full cloth configuration from grasp-point observations by learning a residual correction to a computationally efficient linearized physics model, limiting error accumulation over 40-step planning horizon.

The predicted cloth dynamics are embedded in a model predictive path integral (MPPI) planner using a reduced-order representation of a dual-arm mobile manipulator that preserves the non-holonomic base constraint and arm workspace limits. An MPC layer subsequently refines the sampled motion into smooth, executable references for whole-body control.

The reduced-order formulation achieves tracking performance comparable to the full 17-DoF model while reducing computation time by approximately 80%.

Across four co-transportation scenarios and two carrying speeds, the proposed framework maintains cloth-obstacle clearance where a corner-following baseline results in collisions, while whole-body refinement reduces final cloth deformation from 0.93\,m to 0.28\,m.

summary.en: The paper proposes hierarchical planning for human-robot cloth co-transport, combining a learned cloth model with a reduced-order whole-body model of a dual-arm mobile manipulator. A physics-residual recurrent variational autoencoder predicts cloth configuration from grasp-point observations, and its predictions feed an MPPI planner followed by MPC refinement. The authors report tracking comparable to a full 17-DoF model with about 80% less computation time. Across four scenarios and two carrying speeds, the framework maintained cloth-obstacle clearance where a corner-following baseline collided; whole-body refinement also reduced final cloth deformation.
summary.zh: 论文提出用于人机协同搬运布料的分层规划框架，将学习得到的布料模型与双臂移动操作机器人的降阶全身模型结合。物理残差条件循环变分自编码器根据抓取点观测预测布料构型，并修正线性化物理模型；预测结果进入模型预测路径积分规划器，再由模型预测控制层细化运动。作者报告，降阶模型的跟踪表现与17自由度模型相当，计算时间约减少80%。在四种场景和两种搬运速度下，该框架保持布料与障碍物间隙，而拐角跟随基线发生碰撞；全身细化也降低了最终布料变形。

items.title: Physics Residual Dynamics and Reduced Order Whole-Body Planning for Obstacle Aware Human Robot Cloth CoTransportation

We introduce the Jar Jar ROV, a low-cost, open-source Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) platform designed for citizen science-based water quality monitoring by middle school students. This paper presents the design of the platform and the results of a large-scale deployment with over 100 students across a US state who built, programmed, and deployed

sections.text:
Engaging K-12 students in authentic scientific research remains a significant challenge, particularly at the intersection of environmental science and robotics. We introduce the Jar Jar ROV, a low-cost, open-source Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) platform designed for citizen science-based water quality monitoring by middle school students.

This paper presents the design of the platform and the results of a large-scale deployment with over 100 students across a US state who built, programmed, and deployed the ROVs in local lakes. The educational framework yielded high student engagement in hands-on activities, with ROV construction earning a perfect average score from mentors.

Scientifically, the program established a grassroots monitoring network, generating nearly eleven thousand validated measurements of temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, and turbidity. However, our evaluation identified a critical "engagement gap," with student interest declining sharply during more complex tasks such as electronics assembly and data uploading.

This paper contributes both a validated, scalable model for integrating robotics into environmental education and a data-driven roadmap for future improvements.

These enhancements focus on lowering technical barriers and creating a more intuitive link between data collection and scientific discovery, addressing a key challenge in empowering the next generation of citizen scientists.

summary.en: The paper introduces Jar Jar ROV, a low-cost, open-source remotely operated vehicle for middle school water-quality monitoring through citizen science. In a deployment involving over 100 students across one US state, students built, programmed, and used the ROVs in local lakes. Mentors gave ROV construction a perfect average score. The program generated nearly 11,000 validated measurements of temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, and turbidity. The evaluation also found a sharp decline in student interest during more complex tasks such as electronics assembly and data uploading. The authors propose lowering technical barriers and making the link between data collection and scientific discovery more intuitive.
summary.zh: 论文介绍低成本开源遥控水下机器人 Jar Jar ROV，供中学生开展基于公民科学的水质监测，并报告其在美国一个州、超过100名学生中的部署。学生参与了机器人的制作、编程和湖泊部署；导师对机器人搭建活动的平均评分为满分。该项目建立了基层监测网络，产生近1.1万条经验证的温度、pH、溶解氧和浊度测量数据。评估还发现，学生在电子装配和数据上传等复杂任务中的兴趣明显下降。作者据此提出降低技术门槛、改善数据采集与科学发现联系的后续方向。

items.title: Leveraging Cost-effective Robotics for K-12 STEM Education through Water Quality Monitoring Tasks

The robots are opaque, so if three robots are collinear, the middle robot obstructs the visibility between the other two. Each robot is assigned a finite movement budget, reflecting its limited energy, that bounds the total distance it may traverse during the execution. Moreover, an arbitrary number of robots may become permanently

sections.text:
We investigate the mutual visibility problem for a swarm of $n\ge3$ autonomous mobile robots under the budget-constrained mobility fault model. The robots are opaque, so if three robots are collinear, the middle robot obstructs the visibility between the other two.

Each robot is assigned a finite movement budget, reflecting its limited energy, that bounds the total distance it may traverse during the execution. Moreover, an arbitrary number of robots may become permanently immobile due to mobility faults.

The objective is to design a distributed algorithm that enables the non-faulty robots to coordinate their movements so that, within a finite time, every non-faulty robot attains unobstructed visibility of all robots in the system, including the faulty ones, while respecting the prescribed movement budget.

We consider luminous robots operating under the $\mathsf{SSYNC}$ model with non-rigid movements, without any agreement on their local coordinate systems, and equipped only with a {\it common fixed reference point}.We present a deterministic distributed algorithm that solves the problem despite an arbitrary number of mobility faults.

The algorithm guarantees mutual visibility for the non-faulty robots, respects the movement budget of every robot, provides collision-free movements for the robots, and uses only 12 light colors.

summary.en: The paper studies mutual visibility for opaque autonomous robots with finite movement budgets, where any number may become permanently immobile. Under the SSYNC model with non-rigid movement, no agreement on local coordinate systems, and a common fixed reference point, the authors present a deterministic distributed algorithm. They claim it enables non-faulty robots to see every robot in finite time, respects each robot’s movement budget, and avoids collisions, using 12 light colors.
summary.zh: 论文研究预算受限移动故障模型下，至少三台不透明自主机器人的互相可见问题：机器人移动总距离受预算限制，任意数量的机器人可能永久失去移动能力。作者在 SSYNC、非刚性移动且无局部坐标系共识的设定下，提出确定性分布式算法，使非故障机器人在有限时间内看见系统中所有机器人，同时遵守预算并避免碰撞。算法使用12种灯光颜色，且仅依赖共同固定参考点。

items.title: Budget-Constrained Fault-Tolerant Mutual Visibility for Autonomous Robots under the Mobility Fault Model

items.intro: arXiv:2607.15579v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Equipping humanoid robots with coherent and adaptable personas is crucial for fostering natural, engaging, and trustworthy human-robot interaction (HRI). However, existing approaches often rely on static, hard-coded identities that lack the flexibility to adapt to individual user contexts. In this paper, we present PACE (Persona Adaptation through Conversational Elicitation), a novel framework for the interactive generation and deployment of structured personas on the Ameca humanoid robot. Our system introduces an Interactive Persona Elicitation

sections.text:
Equipping humanoid robots with coherent and adaptable personas is crucial for fostering natural, engaging, and trustworthy human-robot interaction (HRI).However, existing approaches often rely on static, hard-coded identities that lack the flexibility to adapt to individual user contexts.

In this paper, we present PACE (Persona Adaptation through Conversational Elicitation), a novel framework for the interactive generation and deployment of structured personas on the Ameca humanoid robot.

Our system introduces an Interactive Persona Elicitation Pipeline, enabling the robot to dynamically synthesize a tailored, psychologically grounded identity through user Q&A. This elicitation process feeds into a persona prompt compilation phase, generating a structured persona prompt built upon multi-perspective dimensions.

We detail the Embodied System Integration required to translate this structured specification into expressive, multimodal humanoid behaviors.

Through a comprehensive empirical HRI evaluation, we assess the impact of dynamically generated personas on user trust, perceived anthropomorphism, persona consistency, personal relevance, and interaction quality compared to a generic baseline.

These contributions establish a scalable pathway for deploying personalized, interactive, and reliable identities in embodied humanoid assistants. Video demo is available at: https://lipzh5.github.io/PACE/

summary.en: The paper presents PACE, a framework for interactively generating and deploying structured personas on the Ameca humanoid robot. User question-and-answer exchanges inform a tailored identity, which is compiled into a multi-perspective persona prompt and translated into expressive multimodal behavior. The authors describe the embodied system integration and an empirical HRI evaluation comparing dynamically generated personas with a generic baseline on trust, perceived anthropomorphism, persona consistency, personal relevance, and interaction quality. The abstract does not report evaluation outcomes.
summary.zh: 论文提出 PACE，用于在 Ameca 人形机器人上交互式生成和部署结构化 persona。系统通过用户问答合成个性化身份，再将其编译为包含多视角维度的 persona 提示，并将规格转化为富有表现力的多模态行为。作者介绍了具身系统集成，并报告开展了实证人机交互评估，比较动态生成 persona 与通用基线在用户信任、感知拟人性、身份一致性、个人相关性和交互质量方面的表现；摘要未给出评估结果。

items.title: PACE: Persona Adaptation through Conversational Elicitation in Human-Robot Interaction

items.intro: arXiv:2607.22877v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Physical intelligence refers to intelligence systems that understand, reason about, and act in accordance with the physical world and its underlying laws, dynamics, and constraints. Unlike conventional AI systems, physical intelligence interacts continuously with uncertain physical environments, and its actions produce consequences that are physically irreversible. As existing trustworthy AI frameworks have been developed primarily for digital AI systems, they do not fully capture the distinctive challenges of Physical Intelligence, such as physical

sections.text:
Physical intelligence refers to intelligence systems that understand, reason about, and act in accordance with the physical world and its underlying laws, dynamics, and constraints.

Unlike conventional AI systems, physical intelligence interacts continuously with uncertain physical environments, and its actions produce consequences that are physically irreversible.

As existing trustworthy AI frameworks have been developed primarily for digital AI systems, they do not fully capture the distinctive challenges of Physical Intelligence, such as physical safety, cyber-physical security, and physical manufacturing process. To address this gap, we present a survey of trustworthy physical intelligence principles.

First, we characterize the core capabilities and challenges of physical intelligence. Second, we examine the role of physics in AI. Third, we trace the end-to-end physical intelligence life cycle across five core stages and introduce Trustworthy Physical Intelligence Operationalization (T-PAIO).

Fourth, we develop the Trustworthy Physical Intelligence (T-PAI) framework, a theoretical framework that organizes key trustworthiness principles and provides a foundation for governing trustworthy physical intelligence systems.

summary.en: This survey argues that trustworthy AI frameworks designed mainly for digital systems do not fully address physical intelligence challenges, including physical safety, cyber-physical security, and manufacturing processes. The authors characterize physical intelligence capabilities and challenges, examine the role of physics in AI, and describe a life cycle with five core stages. They introduce Trustworthy Physical Intelligence Operationalization (T-PAIO) and develop the theoretical T-PAI framework to organize trustworthiness principles and provide a foundation for governance.
summary.zh: 这篇综述指出，物理智能持续与不确定的物理环境交互，行动可能造成不可逆后果；现有可信人工智能框架主要面向数字系统，未充分覆盖物理安全、网络物理安全和制造过程等挑战。作者概述物理智能的核心能力与挑战，考察物理学在人工智能中的作用，并沿五个核心阶段梳理其全生命周期，提出可信物理智能运行化方案 T-PAIO。文中还构建理论框架 T-PAI，用于组织可信原则并为系统治理提供基础。

items.title: Towards Trustworthy Physical Intelligence: From Theory to Practice Across Life Cycle

However, imitation-learned policies inherit the execution speed of their demonstrations, and test-time speed modification can introduce unrecoverable out-of-distribution observations, reducing task success. We observe that the directional inconsistency of action chunks reflects task-phase criticality, indicating how aggressively action step

sections.text:
Online control of execution speed is essential for deploying robot policies in real-world scenarios, as robots may need to speed up under time constraints or slow down to facilitate human interaction and improve safety.

However, imitation-learned policies inherit the execution speed of their demonstrations, and test-time speed modification can introduce unrecoverable out-of-distribution observations, reducing task success.

We observe that the directional inconsistency of action chunks reflects task-phase criticality, indicating how aggressively action step lengths can be modified while preserving task success. Based on this observation, we introduce FreeSpeed, a training-free module that post-processes action chunks from pretrained policies.

FreeSpeed resamples each predicted chunk at the requested rate, then uses directional inconsistency between adjacent actions as the primary signal for rescaling. This signal adaptively determines how closely the execution speed can approach the requested speed, allowing flexible speed adjustment within the evaluated limits without compromising task success.

Across three policy families and 50 simulated tasks, FreeSpeed supports online speed changes, with realized execution rates spanning 0.22x to 2.53x among settings that preserve per-task success.

Across four real-world manipulation tasks, FreeSpeed achieves an average success rate of 94.0%, matching the frozen policy's 93.8%, while realizing execution rates from 0.38x to 1.97x.

summary.en: FreeSpeed is a training-free module that post-processes action chunks from pretrained robot policies to adjust execution speed online. It resamples chunks at the requested rate and uses directional inconsistency between adjacent actions to guide speed rescaling, aiming to preserve task success. The authors evaluate it across three policy families and 50 simulated tasks. In four real-world manipulation tasks, they report a 94.0% average success rate, compared with 93.8% for the frozen policy; reported speed ranges apply to settings that preserve per-task success.
summary.zh: FreeSpeed 是一种无需训练的模块，用于后处理预训练机器人策略的动作片段，以在线调整执行速度。它先按请求速率重采样动作，再依据相邻动作的方向不一致程度调节速度，以适应任务阶段并尽量维持成功率。作者在三类策略和50项仿真任务中评估在线速度变化；在四项真实操作任务中，报告其平均成功率为94.0%，与冻结策略的93.8%相当。摘要给出的速度范围仅适用于各任务成功率得以保持的设置。

items.title: FreeSpeed: Training-Free Speed Control for Generative Robot Policies

sections.text:
The For\^et Montmorency (FoMo) dataset is a comprehensive multi-season data collection, recorded over the span of one year in a boreal forest. Featuring a unique combination of on- and off-pavement environments with significant environmental changes, the dataset challenges established odometry and SLAM pipelines.

Some highlights of the data include the accumulation of snow exceeding 1 m, significant vegetation growth in front of sensors, and operations at the traction limits of the platform. In total, the FoMo dataset includes over 64 km of six diverse trajectories, repeated during 12 deployments throughout the year.

The dataset features data from one rotating and one hybrid solid-state lidar, a Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar, full-HD images from a stereo camera and a wide lens monocular camera, as well as data from two IMUs.

Ground Truth is calculated by post-processing three GNSS receivers mounted on the Uncrewed Ground Vehicle (UGV) and a static GNSS base station. Additional metadata, such as one measurement per minute from an on-site weather station, camera calibration intrinsics, and vehicle power consumption, is available for all sequences.

To highlight the relevance of the dataset, we performed a preliminary evaluation of the robustness of a lidar-inertial, radar-gyro, and a visual-inertial localization and mapping techniques to seasonal changes. We show that seasonal changes have serious effects on the re-localization capabilities of the state-of-the-art methods.

The dataset and development kit are available at https://fomo.norlab.ulaval.ca.

summary.en: FoMo is a multi-season robot navigation dataset collected over one year in a boreal forest, covering paved and off-pavement environments with substantial seasonal changes. It contains more than 64 km across six diverse trajectories, repeated over 12 deployments, with data from lidar, FMCW radar, cameras, and two IMUs. Ground truth is post-processed from vehicle-mounted GNSS receivers and a static base station; weather, camera calibration, and power metadata are also provided. A preliminary evaluation reports serious seasonal effects on relocalization by three localization and mapping approaches.
summary.zh: FoMo 是一套在北方针叶林历时一年的多季节机器人导航数据集，涵盖铺装与非铺装环境及显著季节变化。数据包含六条轨迹、超过64公里的记录，并在全年12次部署中重复采集，使用多种激光雷达、雷达、相机和IMU。真值由车载GNSS接收机及静态基站后处理获得，另提供天气、相机标定和车辆能耗等元数据。作者初步评估了三类定位建图方法，称季节变化严重影响其重定位能力。

items.title: FoMo: A Multi-Season Dataset for Robot Navigation in For\^et Montmorency

sections.text:
For ground robots operating in outdoor environments, understanding the properties of the underlying terrain is essential for ensuring reliable operation. In most perception-based studies, this problem is formulated as categorical classification with a fixed number of classes defined during training.

We propose an approach that enables new surface classes to be added as trainable vectors, which can subsequently be used to address higher-level tasks.

By employing a learning paradigm based on predicting the robot's next state in time and using attention blocks, we improved classification accuracy to 98.56% on the Belyaev-Kushnarev dataset and 94.8% on BorealTC.

summary.en: The paper addresses terrain understanding for ground robots operating outdoors, noting that perception studies commonly treat it as classification over a fixed set of training classes. The authors propose a surface representation approach in which new surface classes can be added as trainable vectors for use in higher-level tasks. The learning method predicts the robot’s next state in time and uses attention blocks. The reported classification accuracy is 98.56% on the Belyaev-Kushnarev dataset and 94.8% on BorealTC.
summary.zh: 本文针对户外地面机器人的地形理解问题，指出常见感知研究将其设定为训练阶段固定类别数的分类任务。作者提出一种表面表示学习方法，可将新的表面类别作为可训练向量加入，并用于更高层任务。该方法通过预测机器人下一时刻状态并采用注意力模块进行学习；在 Belyaev-Kushnarev 数据集上的分类准确率为98.56%，在 BorealTC 上为94.8%。

items.title: Attention-Based Surface Representation Learning for Robot State Prediction and Open-Ended Surface Classification

sections.text:
In this paper, we present a distributed cascade force control system (DCFC) for multiple robots with the aim of pushing a rigid object towards a desired moving target without their inter-robot communication. These mobile robots are equipped with 360-degree vision-based soft tactile sensors utilized to determine contact location and resultant impact force.

By investigating the dynamics of moving rigid objects on the flat, we proposed a distributed cascade control. The inner loop control incorporates contact force and positioning, ensuring the robots' pushing contact and application of the desired force to the object.

The outer loop control coordinates the robots to push the object in a desired direction without inter-robot communication, regardless of the unknown object mass. The stability and convergence of the system are verified using the Lyapunov stability theory.

We also conducted simulation and real-word experiments to validate the performance of the proposed control method, and the experimental results showcase the successful coordination of multiple robots in pushing an object towards a moving desired direction.

summary.en: The paper presents a distributed cascade force control system for multiple robots pushing a rigid object toward a moving target without inter-robot communication. The robots use 360-degree vision-based soft tactile sensors to determine contact locations and impact forces. An inner loop controls contact force and positioning, while an outer loop coordinates the pushing direction and is described as independent of unknown object mass. Stability and convergence are verified using Lyapunov stability theory. Simulations and real-world experiments are reported, with results showing coordinated pushing toward a moving desired direction.
summary.zh: 本文提出分布式级联力控制系统，使多个机器人在不进行机器人间通信的情况下，将刚性物体推向移动目标。机器人利用360度视觉软触觉传感器确定接触位置和冲击力；内环控制接触力与位置，外环协调推送方向，并声称可应对未知物体质量。作者通过李雅普诺夫稳定性理论验证系统稳定性与收敛性，并开展仿真和真实实验，报告多机器人成功协调推动物体朝目标移动方向运动。

items.title: Distributed Cascade Force Control of Soft-Tactile-Based Multi-robot System for Object Transportation

sections.text:
Self driving vehicles have emerged as a reliable technology that has the capability to transform transportation and mobility. The development of self driving cars requires significant advances in a number of areas, including perception, localization, decision making, and control.

This research paper is based on the project implementation of the combination of object detection using YOLO (You Only Look Once), depth sensing using MiDaS for the localization and perception of obstacles, perspective transform, and decision making for path planning in self driving cars.

The contemporary state of the technology for object detection, depth sensing, localization, and path planning evaluates the performance of the combined system through simulations and experiments. The results show that the combination of YOLO and MiDaS provides a new robust system for object detection and depth sensing.

This research paper contributes to the advancement of self driving car technology and provides new and innovative approaches to the perception and localization of obstacles in the environment. Keywords: YOLO, MiDaS, perception, localization, decision making

summary.en: The paper describes a self-driving vehicle project combining YOLO object detection, MiDaS depth sensing, perspective transformation, and decision making for obstacle perception, localization, and path planning. The authors evaluate the combined system through simulations and experiments. They report that combining YOLO and MiDaS provides a new robust system for object detection and depth sensing. The abstract does not specify experimental conditions or provide quantitative results.
summary.zh: 本文描述一项自动驾驶项目实现，将 YOLO 用于物体检测、MiDaS 用于深度感知，并结合透视变换和决策方法进行障碍物定位、感知及路径规划。作者通过仿真和实验评估组合系统，报告 YOLO 与 MiDaS 的结合形成了用于物体检测和深度感知的新型稳健系统。摘要未提供具体实验条件或量化结果。

items.title: AUTOPILOT An Advanced Perception, Localization and Path Planning Techniques for Autonomous Vehicles Using YOLOv7 and MiDaS

Urban relay placement is difficult because line-of-sight blockage, communication range, altitude, and three-dimensional obstacles must be considered jointly. Arm2Air transfers obstacle-avoidance skeletons from robot arms to UAV relay placement through cross-embodiment transfer. Source-domain robot-arm motions from a pretrained Neural MP model are converted into ordered skeletons that pretrain a transformer-based transfer platform, which is then adapted to the UAV

sections.text:
Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) relay networks can restore connectivity after communication infrastructure is damaged. Urban relay placement is difficult because line-of-sight blockage, communication range, altitude, and three-dimensional obstacles must be considered jointly.

Arm2Air transfers obstacle-avoidance skeletons from robot arms to UAV relay placement through cross-embodiment transfer.

Source-domain robot-arm motions from a pretrained Neural MP model are converted into ordered skeletons that pretrain a transformer-based transfer platform, which is then adapted to the UAV domain using limited target data and Low-Rank Adaptation.

The transferred skeleton initializes a relay chain that is refined for connectivity, bottleneck capacity, delay, and movement cost. On nine held-out high-clutter 3D urban maps, Arm2Air reduced median end-to-end planning runtime by 64.9 percent relative to the fastest conventional planner.

On the high-obstruction group of a separate 30-map dense urban holdout, it increased bottleneck capacity by 32.6 percent, reduced capacity variance by 74.7 percent, reduced maximum hop distance by 13.2 percent, reduced hop-distance variance by 75.2 percent, and reduced relay displacement by 16.9 percent relative to IMPC-MD.

With only three target-domain training maps, Arm2Air reduced relay-position root mean square error by 53.6 percent relative to training from scratch while updating 0.134 million parameters, compared with 1.383 million for Scratch and Full Fine-tuning.

These results demonstrate computationally and data-efficient UAV relay placement and suggest a broader principle for transferring ordered structural priors across heterogeneous embodied tasks.

summary.en: Arm2Air transfers ordered obstacle-avoidance skeletons from pretrained robot-arm motions to UAV relay placement, then refines relay chains for connectivity, capacity, delay, and movement cost. On nine held-out high-clutter 3D maps, it reduced median planning runtime by 64.9% relative to the fastest conventional planner. On a separate 30-map holdout, results for the high-obstruction group showed gains over IMPC-MD in bottleneck capacity and several distance and displacement measures. With three target-domain training maps, the authors also report a 53.6% reduction in relay-position error versus training from scratch.
summary.zh: Arm2Air将预训练神经运动规划模型中的机械臂避障动作转为有序骨架，用少量无人机目标域数据和低秩适配迁移到三维中继布置，再据此优化连通性、瓶颈容量、时延和移动成本。在九张高复杂度留出地图上，其端到端规划中位运行时间较最快传统规划器降低64.9%。在另一个30张密集城市地图留出集的高遮挡组中，相较IMPC-MD，瓶颈容量提高32.6%，中继位移降低16.9%等。作者还报告，仅用三张目标域训练地图时，位置均方根误差较从头训练降低53.6%。

items.title: Arm2Air: Cross-Embodiment Skeleton Transfer for 3D Relay Formation

However, most of them use fixed pruning schedules, such as pruning once at a

sections.text:
Visual token pruning is an effective way to accelerate vision-language models and is especially useful for vision-language-action (VLA) inference, where many visual tokens must be processed before predicting robot actions.

Existing pruning methods usually estimate which tokens can be pruned based on attention scores or feature diversity, retaining tokens that are either highly attended or visually different from others. However, most of them use fixed pruning schedules, such as pruning once at a preset layer or pruning at uniformly spaced layers.

Such schedules can be risky for VLA models, because the model may not know which visual regions matter for the action in early layers. Tokens that look unimportant at first may become useful after the model combines visual observations with the language instruction.

In this work, we propose SAPrune, a training-free visual token pruning framework for efficient VLA inference. Instead of pruning at fixed layers, SAPrune uses a small calibration set to observe how action-to-visual attention changes across layers, and chooses pruning layers only after the attention pattern becomes more reliable.

At each selected layer, SAPrune applies a dual-path pruning rule: one path protects strongly attended visual tokens from pruning, while the other prevents useful surrounding context from being discarded.

Experiments on LIBERO, SIMPLER, and real-world robotic tasks show that SAPrune prunes 87.5% of visual tokens and achieves up to 1.718x inference speedup while maintaining competitive task success rates.

summary.en: SAPrune is a training-free visual token pruning framework for vision-language-action inference. Using a small calibration set, it tracks how action-to-visual attention changes across layers and selects pruning layers after the pattern becomes more reliable. At each selected layer, a dual-path rule protects strongly attended tokens and preserves useful surrounding context. Experiments on LIBERO, SIMPLER, and real-world robotic tasks report pruning 87.5% of visual tokens and up to 1.718x inference speedup while maintaining competitive task success rates.
summary.zh: SAPrune是一种无需训练的视觉令牌剪枝方法，面向视觉-语言-动作模型推理。它利用小型校准集观察各层动作到视觉的注意力变化，在注意力模式更可靠后才选择剪枝层；每层采用双路径规则，保护高注意力令牌，并保留有用的周边上下文。摘要指出，过早剪枝可能丢弃之后结合语言指令才显得重要的视觉区域。在LIBERO、SIMPLER及真实机器人任务上的实验中，该方法剪去87.5%的视觉令牌，最高达到1.718倍推理加速，同时保持有竞争力的任务成功率。

items.title: When and What to Prune? Stage-Aware Visual Token Pruning for Efficient VLA

items.intro: arXiv:2610.05969v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diffusion policies provide expressive action distributions for continuous-control reinforcement learning. However, safety-aware online diffusion policy optimization remains underexplored, particularly methods that use predictive reachability information without an explicit dynamics model. We propose Reachability-Aware Diffusion Policy Optimization (RADPO), a model-free method that combines predictive first-hit safety estimation with cumulative-cost budget feedback. RADPO learns a discounted first-hit reachability value that captures the discounted risk of a cost event, assigns larger weight to events that occur

sections.text:
Diffusion policies provide expressive action distributions for continuous-control reinforcement learning. However, safety-aware online diffusion policy optimization remains underexplored, particularly methods that use predictive reachability information without an explicit dynamics model.

We propose Reachability-Aware Diffusion Policy Optimization (RADPO), a model-free method that combines predictive first-hit safety estimation with cumulative-cost budget feedback.

RADPO learns a discounted first-hit reachability value that captures the discounted risk of a cost event, assigns larger weight to events that occur sooner, and uses this signal to shape the reward. A separate dual-like multiplier adjusts the shaping strength according to realized episodic costs relative to a prescribed budget.

The diffusion actor improves through weighted denoising regression on candidate actions scored by the reward critic. Our approach requires neither a learned dynamics model, action gradients through the critics, nor differentiation through the reverse diffusion sampler.

We establish theoretical properties of the reachability value and show that accumulated reachability penalty provides a conservative surrogate for future discounted cumulative cost.

Across ten continuous-control safety tasks, RADPO achieves competitive reward-cost trade-offs, with substantial reductions in constraint violations on several tasks relative to the compared baselines.

Our theoretical and empirical analysis supports that combining reachability with cumulative budget feedback is a viable approach to safety-aware diffusion policies.

summary.en: RADPO is a model-free method for safety-aware diffusion policy optimization in continuous-control reinforcement learning. It combines predictive first-hit reachability estimates with feedback from a cumulative-cost budget: earlier cost events receive greater weight, and a multiplier adjusts reward shaping based on realized episodic costs. The diffusion actor improves through weighted denoising regression on candidate actions scored by a reward critic. The authors establish theoretical properties and characterize accumulated reachability penalty as a conservative surrogate for future discounted cost. Across ten safety tasks, RADPO achieved competitive reward-cost trade-offs and reduced constraint violations on several tasks relative to the compared baselines.
summary.zh: RADPO是一种面向连续控制强化学习的无模型扩散策略优化方法，将预测式首次触发安全估计与累积成本预算反馈结合。它学习折扣首次触发可达性值，以较高权重处理更早发生的成本事件，并用该信号塑造奖励；另以乘子根据实际回合成本相对预设预算调整塑造强度。策略通过对奖励评论器评分的候选动作进行加权去噪回归来改进。作者证明了可达性值的理论性质，并指出累积可达性惩罚可保守近似未来折扣成本。在十项连续控制安全任务中，实验显示其奖励与成本权衡有竞争力，且若干任务的约束违规显著减少。

items.title: Reachability-Aware Diffusion Policy Optimization

items.intro: arXiv:2610.03898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model-based control of an aquatic robotic platform depends on a hydrodynamic model that is costly to identify and specific to the hull, payload, and conditions it was measured in. Here, we present MOSAIC-SV, a deployable real-time adaptive dynamics identification and control system that identifies a control-sufficient dynamics model from a spec-sheet engineering prior, without dedicated identification trials, and re-estimates it at every control step of a closed-loop mission while the controller plans on

sections.text:
Model-based control of an aquatic robotic platform depends on a hydrodynamic model that is costly to identify and specific to the hull, payload, and conditions it was measured in.

Here, we present MOSAIC-SV, a deployable real-time adaptive dynamics identification and control system that identifies a control-sufficient dynamics model from a spec-sheet engineering prior, without dedicated identification trials, and re-estimates it at every control step of a closed-loop mission while the controller plans on it.

A physically admissible unscented Kalman filter re-estimates hydrodynamic, disturbance, and actuator parameters at every control step of the closed-loop mission; while a command-dependent consider projection withholds corrections the current command cannot attribute between actuator effectiveness and external force; and a model predictive path integral controller plans on the current estimate.

In simulation on a CyberShip II plant, MOSAIC-SV recovers the transit performance of the calibrated model under static mismatch and transient changes, and stays within 20% of its own transit time at the unscaled prior when its inertia or damping prior is wrong by an order of magnitude.

In on-water field trials on the Blue Robotics BlueBoat, a twin-thruster catamaran, MOSAIC-SV transits at least 25% faster and predicts its own motion with at least 56% less error than its frozen engineering prior, including under an unmodeled payload. The same MOSAIC-SV system concept was also feasibly deployed on a 6.3-tonne dual outboard monohull.

summary.en: MOSAIC-SV identifies a control-sufficient aquatic-robot dynamics model from a spec-sheet engineering prior without dedicated identification trials, then re-estimates parameters at every control step for closed-loop planning. Its components include a physically admissible unscented Kalman filter, a command-dependent consider projection, and a model predictive path integral controller. CyberShip II simulations report recovery of calibrated-model transit performance under mismatch and transient changes, with transit time within 20% of the unscaled prior when inertia or damping is wrong by an order of magnitude. BlueBoat field trials report at least 25% faster transit and 56% less motion-prediction error than the frozen prior, including with an unmodeled payload.
summary.zh: MOSAIC-SV从规格表工程先验识别水上机器人的控制所需动力学模型，无需专门辨识试验，并在闭环任务中每个控制步重新估计参数供控制器规划。系统结合物理可行的无迹卡尔曼滤波、命令相关的考虑投影和模型预测路径积分控制器。CyberShip II仿真显示，它能在静态模型失配和瞬态变化下恢复经校准模型的航行表现；先验惯性或阻尼误差达一个数量级时，航行时间仍在未缩放先验的20%以内。BlueBoat水上试验中，相较冻结工程先验，航行至少快25%，运动预测误差至少低56%，包括未建模载荷情形。该系统概念也在6.3吨双舷外机单体船上实现可行部署。

items.title: MOSAIC-SV: Real-Time Adaptive Identification of Vessel Dynamics for the Control and Deployment of Aquatic Robots

sections.text:
In recent years, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) or drones have been increasingly adopted in urban environments for applications such as parcel delivery, infrastructure inspection, emergency response, and drone light shows.

A non-negligible issue is how to manage the increasing number of drones operated by different entities, to enable them to cooperatively avoid potential collisions and determine conflict-free short-term flight paths in urban airspace.

This paper presents a Prediction-Based Short-Term Decentralized Greedy (PB-STDG) guidance algorithm for a structured Drone Road System (DRS).

PB-STDG extends the original STDG algorithm by introducing a prediction mechanism that enables drones to anticipate the decisions of neighboring drones using additional information shared in beacon packets, aiming to address the over-conservative behavior observed in the STDG algorithm.

Several simulation scenarios are conducted to evaluate and compare the proposed algorithm with STDG. The results show that PB-STDG improves traffic efficiency while maintaining a safety level comparable to that of STDG.

summary.en: The paper presents PB-STDG, a prediction-based short-term decentralized greedy guidance algorithm for structured drone road systems. Extending STDG, it uses additional information in beacon packets to anticipate neighboring drones’ decisions, with the aim of reducing the original algorithm’s over-conservative behavior. In several simulation scenarios, comparisons show improved traffic efficiency while maintaining a safety level comparable to STDG.
summary.zh: 论文提出面向结构化无人机道路系统的预测型短期分散贪心引导算法 PB-STDG，在原 STDG 基础上利用信标包中的额外信息预测邻近无人机的决策，旨在缓解原算法过于保守的问题。多个仿真场景的比较结果显示，该算法提高了交通效率，同时保持与 STDG 相当的安全水平。

items.title: PB-STDG: A Prediction-Based Short-Term Decentralized Greedy Guidance Algorithm for a Drone Road System
