Reinforcement learning's standard scalar reward carries far less information than the directional task error that defines the task. Random exploration further discards whatever information each rollout returns. Through residual learning with directional task-error supervision and a task error model that drives sample selection, we achieve stable

sections.text:
For residual learning that refines existing behavior, sample efficiency depends on two things: how much information each rollout returns, and how efficiently the learner uses that information. Reinforcement learning's standard scalar reward carries far less information than the directional task error that defines the task.

Random exploration further discards whatever information each rollout returns. Through residual learning with directional task-error supervision and a task error model that drives sample selection, we achieve stable three-, four-, and five-ball juggling on anthropomorphic Barrett WAM arms.

Despite planning and controlling through a simple, idealized stack, the system converges from the second attempt. The first attempt drops, after which task error decreases monotonically without further failures. In comparison, five-ball juggling typically takes humans years of practice.

We compare residual learners across two ternary axes, the directional information in the learning feedback and the commitment of the analytic prior, spanning Newton-style Jacobian updates, Composite Bayesian Optimization, and stochastic search methods.

Both axes prove necessary for fast convergence: neither directional feedback nor an informative prior alone matches their combination, and the simplest method that combines them, a fixed-Jacobian Newton update, is the fastest and fully reliable.

The learned residual tolerates substantial prior misalignment and degraded joint tracking, affecting mainly convergence speed. The bottleneck for residual learning on real robots is therefore the information content of the supervision signal and how the learner uses it, not the accuracy of the surrounding stack.

Video documentation of all experiments is available at https://kai-ploeger.com/residual-juggling.

summary.en: The paper studies residual learning for real-robot juggling, arguing that directional task-error supervision carries more information than scalar reward and that a task-error model can guide sample selection. The authors report stable three-, four-, and five-ball juggling on anthropomorphic Barrett WAM arms. After a failed first attempt, the system converges from the second attempt, with task error decreasing monotonically and no further failures. Comparisons indicate that fast convergence requires both directional feedback and an informative analytic prior; a fixed-Jacobian Newton update is reported as fastest and reliable. The learned residual tolerates prior misalignment and degraded joint tracking, mainly affecting convergence speed.
summary.zh: 本文研究用于真实机器人任务的残差学习，主张方向性任务误差监督比标量奖励包含更多学习信息，并用任务误差模型指导样本选择。作者报告，该方法使拟人化 Barrett WAM 机械臂实现稳定的三球、四球和五球杂耍：首次尝试失败后，系统从第二次尝试开始收敛，任务误差随后单调下降且不再失败。对比分析显示，方向性反馈与有信息量的解析先验结合才能快速收敛；其中固定雅可比牛顿更新最快且可靠。作者称残差可容忍显著先验偏差和关节跟踪退化，主要影响收敛速度。

items.title: Task-Error Residual Learning for Real-Robot Five-Ball Juggling

items.intro: arXiv:2610.04767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Latent world models enable robots to plan by predicting the consequences of actions. Planning long tasks with control-rate actions requires many prediction steps, which enlarges the search space and accumulates error. Skill-level actions shorten these sequences, but a symbolic skill vocabulary requires domain knowledge and labeled demonstrations. We construct skill-level actions from the inputs of a flow-matching policy trained on demonstrations segmented into complete skills. The policy maps a noise seed and an

sections.text:
Latent world models enable robots to plan by predicting the consequences of actions. Planning long tasks with control-rate actions requires many prediction steps, which enlarges the search space and accumulates error. Skill-level actions shorten these sequences, but a symbolic skill vocabulary requires domain knowledge and labeled demonstrations.

We construct skill-level actions from the inputs of a flow-matching policy trained on demonstrations segmented into complete skills. The policy maps a noise seed and an observation, optionally with a code or label, to a complete skill execution, so one execution is one world-model transition.

On this mechanism we propose four action abstractions with increasing task knowledge: a compressed seed, two discrete codes learned from the demonstrations, and a symbolic label. We evaluate them with a common world-model training procedure and planning framework on simulated block rearrangement tasks that require up to 14 sequential skills.

The symbolic label succeeds in over 90% of the tasks that require up to six skills and degrades beyond. Without any label, an object-centric learned code matches it on single-skill tasks and retains half to three quarters of its success on tasks of two to five skills.

Ablations attribute much of the label's advantage to its planner knowing which actions are applicable, rather than to the label itself. Beyond six skills the search, not the world model, limits success. Project page: https://andreumatoses.github.io/research/flow-skill-wm

summary.en: The authors construct skill-level actions from the inputs to a flow-matching policy trained on demonstrations of complete skills, then compare four abstractions in simulated block rearrangement tasks requiring up to 14 sequential skills. Symbolic labels achieve over 90% success on tasks requiring up to six skills, with performance declining on longer tasks. Without labels, an object-centric learned code matches the label on single-skill tasks and retains half to three quarters of its success on tasks of two to five skills. Ablations attribute much of the label advantage to planner knowledge of action applicability; beyond six skills, search is the limiting factor.
summary.zh: 本文从基于示范训练、并将完整技能作为输出的流匹配策略输入中构造技能级动作，用于长时程规划。作者比较压缩噪声种子、两种学习得到的离散码和符号标签四种抽象，并在最多需要14个连续技能的模拟积木重排任务中评估。符号标签在最多六技能的任务中成功率超过90%，更长任务表现下降；无标签的物体中心学习码在单技能任务上与其相当，在二至五技能任务中保留其一半至四分之三的成功率。消融结果表明，标签优势很大程度来自规划器知道动作适用条件；超过六技能后，搜索成为限制因素。

items.title: Flow Policies as Actions of Skill-Level World Models: Learned and Symbolic Abstractions for Long-Horizon Planning

items.intro: arXiv:2610.05571v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In safety-critical domains such as autonomous driving, systems must be evaluated across a large number of environment conditions, often represented as composite scenarios built from primitive scenarios. Existing statistical model checking (SMC) approaches analyze each composite scenario independently, requiring many expensive simulations and resulting in substantial redundant computation when scenarios share common structure. This work introduces a scenario-based compositional SMC framework for safety and co-safety specifications, enabling efficient analysis of composite scenarios. Our

sections.text:
In safety-critical domains such as autonomous driving, systems must be evaluated across a large number of environment conditions, often represented as composite scenarios built from primitive scenarios.

Existing statistical model checking (SMC) approaches analyze each composite scenario independently, requiring many expensive simulations and resulting in substantial redundant computation when scenarios share common structure.

This work introduces a scenario-based compositional SMC framework for safety and co-safety specifications, enabling efficient analysis of composite scenarios.

Our approach decomposes scenarios into primitives and specifications into sub-specifications, verifies each primitive independently, and composes the resulting statistical estimates using importance sampling and kernel density estimation.

Our empirical evaluation shows that the proposed framework can accurately answer verification queries for previously unseen composite scenarios while reducing simulation cost through parallelization and trace reuse.

summary.en: The paper presents a compositional statistical model checking framework for safety and co-safety specifications over composite scenarios. It decomposes scenarios into primitives and specifications into sub-specifications, verifies primitives independently, and combines statistical estimates using importance sampling and kernel density estimation. The empirical evaluation reports that the method accurately answers verification queries for previously unseen composite scenarios and reduces simulation cost through parallelization and trace reuse. The abstract does not give quantitative cost reductions or further details about the evaluation conditions.
summary.zh: 本文提出面向安全与余安全规格的场景组合式统计模型检查框架，以减少独立分析复合场景所需的重复仿真。方法将场景分解为基本场景、将规格分解为子规格，分别验证各基本场景，再通过重要性采样和核密度估计组合统计估计。经验评估显示，该框架能够准确回答此前未见复合场景的验证查询，并通过并行化和轨迹复用降低仿真成本。摘要未说明具体领域外的实验条件或量化降幅。

items.title: Scenario-Based Compositional Statistical Model Checking for Safety Specifications

items.intro: arXiv:2610.04255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robotic manipulation often requires inferring task-relevant states from past interactions when the current observation alone is insufficient to determine the appropriate action. Despite progress in benchmarking memory-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) models, application-oriented tasks requiring history-dependent semantic inference remain underrepresented. We introduce GiT (Grounded in Time), a dataset and benchmark for grounding manipulation decisions in past events across biolaboratory, household, and industrial scenarios. sections.text:
Robotic manipulation often requires inferring task-relevant states from past interactions when the current observation alone is insufficient to determine the appropriate action.

Despite progress in benchmarking memory-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) models, application-oriented tasks requiring history-dependent semantic inference remain underrepresented. We introduce GiT (Grounded in Time), a dataset and benchmark for grounding manipulation decisions in past events across biolaboratory, household, and industrial scenarios.

It includes real-robot and Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) style demonstrations covering 18 bimanual tasks, together with simulation data and a ManiSkill-based evaluation suite covering nine tasks.

Fine-grained subtask annotations and annotated counterfactual task pairs, in which similar current observations require different actions depending on prior events, support policy learning and targeted evaluation of history use.

Evaluations of representative end-to-end VLA models in simulation and on selected real-world tasks reveal substantial room for improvement in history-dependent manipulation. The dataset and benchmark are available at the project page.

summary.en: The authors introduce GiT, a dataset and benchmark for grounding robotic manipulation decisions in past events across biolaboratory, household, and industrial settings. It contains real-robot and UMI-style demonstrations for 18 bimanual tasks, simulation data, and a ManiSkill-based evaluation suite covering nine tasks. Fine-grained subtask annotations and counterfactual task pairs support policy learning and targeted assessment of whether models use history. Evaluations of representative end-to-end vision-language-action models in simulation and on selected real-world tasks indicate substantial room for improvement in history-dependent manipulation.
summary.zh: 本文介绍GiT（Grounded in Time），一个用于机器人操作中基于过去事件进行时间定位的数据集与基准，覆盖生物实验室、家庭和工业场景。数据包含真实机器人及UMI风格示范，涉及18项双臂任务，并提供仿真数据和基于ManiSkill、覆盖九项任务的评测套件。细粒度子任务标注和反事实任务对可用于策略学习及定向评估历史信息的使用。对代表性端到端视觉语言动作模型的仿真评测及部分真实任务评测显示，依赖历史的操作仍有较大改进空间。

items.title: Grounded in Time: A Multi-Source Dataset and Benchmark for Temporal Grounding in Robotic Manipulation

sections.text:
Ultrasound visual servoing is essential for autonomous robotic ultrasound, yet 6-DoF probe control from 2D B-mode images remains challenging due to limited and ambiguous out-of-plane motion cues. Existing methods typically rely on anatomical priors or handcrafted visual features, limiting their generalizability across imaging targets.

Inspired by trackerless 3D ultrasound reconstruction, we propose Recon2Servo, a visual servoing framework that learns image-to-motion inference directly from B-mode images for 6-DoF probe control.

A DINOv3 encoder with low-rank adaptation and a bidirectional relation module estimate the relative probe pose between current and target images to guide iterative closed-loop target-view alignment.

The framework combines supervised relative-pose learning, reconstruction-guided closed-loop adaptation, and bounded residual pose correction to improve motion inference during servoing.

Evaluations on a public dataset and an in-house dataset collected from 12 healthy volunteers using different ultrasound systems demonstrate its effectiveness in reconstructed-volume servoing.

Additional real-robot demonstrations of target-view alignment and dynamic tracking on a human forearm are provided in the supplementary video: https://youtu.be/qwsOdI-GMYk.

summary.en: Recon2Servo learns image-to-motion inference from 2D B-mode ultrasound images for six-degree-of-freedom probe visual servoing. It uses a low-rank-adapted DINOv3 encoder and a bidirectional relation module to estimate relative probe pose between current and target images and guide iterative closed-loop alignment. The framework also combines supervised relative-pose learning, reconstruction-guided adaptation, and bounded residual pose correction. Evaluations on a public dataset and an in-house dataset collected from 12 healthy volunteers using different ultrasound systems demonstrate reconstructed-volume servoing. Supplementary video shows real-robot target alignment and dynamic tracking on a human forearm.
summary.zh: 本文提出Recon2Servo，通过直接从二维B模式超声图像学习图像到运动的推断，实现六自由度探头视觉伺服。框架使用经低秩适配的DINOv3编码器和双向关系模块估计当前图像与目标图像间的相对探头位姿，以迭代闭环对齐目标视图；方法还结合监督式相对位姿学习、重建引导的闭环适配及有界残差位姿校正。作者在公开数据集和来自12名健康志愿者、使用不同超声系统采集的自建数据集上评估，并报告重建体积伺服效果；补充视频展示了人体前臂上的真实机器人对齐和动态跟踪。

items.title: Recon2Servo: Robotic Ultrasound Visual Servoing via Learned Image-to-Motion Inference

Verifier-guided test-time scaling offers an efficient alternative by sampling multiple action candidates and selecting the one most likely to lead to task success at inference time. sections.text:
Scaling robot data and model capacity has improved Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, but further progress is constrained by the high cost of robotic data. Verifier-guided test-time scaling offers an efficient alternative by sampling multiple action candidates and selecting the one most likely to lead to task success at inference time.

Existing classification-based verifiers learn from trajectory-level outcomes but treat all visited states equally, even though their value for candidate discrimination can vary across a trajectory.

At many states, plausible actions are similar and provide limited discrimination signal, while only a sparse set of decision-critical states admits meaningfully different actions that can substantially affect downstream outcomes. To address this, we propose DiVeR, which estimates decision criticality from the dispersion of sampled action representations.

DiVeR then uses this signal to reweight verifier learning toward states where action selection is most consequential, without requiring step-level annotations or additional environment interaction.

Across LIBERO, RoboCasa, and real-world experiments on a Franka Research 3 robot, DiVeR consistently improves task success through more effective verifier-guided action selection, while adding negligible verifier inference overhead.

summary.en: The paper presents DiVeR, a verifier-learning method for test-time scaling of vision-language-action policies. It estimates how decision-critical a state is from the dispersion of sampled action representations, then gives such states greater weight during verifier learning without step-level annotations or additional environment interaction. The authors report improved task success through verifier-guided action selection across LIBERO, RoboCasa, and real-world experiments with a Franka Research 3 robot, with negligible verifier inference overhead.
summary.zh: 论文提出 DiVeR，一种用于视觉—语言—动作策略测试时扩展的验证器学习方法。它根据采样动作表示的离散程度估计状态的决策关键性，并据此提高验证器对关键状态的学习权重，无需逐步标注或额外环境交互。作者报告，DiVeR 在 LIBERO、RoboCasa 和 Franka Research 3 机器人真实环境实验中，通过改进验证器引导的动作选择提升任务成功率，同时验证器推理开销可忽略。

items.title: DiVeR: Decision-Critical Verifier Learning for VLA Test-Time Scaling

WAMJET

sections.text:
World Action Models (WAMs) leverage pretrained video foundation models for robot manipulation, but their large backbones and video-action co-prediction are expensive. Although existing acceleration techniques offer many ways to reduce this cost, selecting and composing them requires substantial engineering for each model and hardware platform.

To tackle this bottleneck, we present WAMJET, an agentic harness that accelerates WAM inference by equipping coding agents with reusable optimization guidance and measurement and validation tools.

WAMJET follows a bottleneck-driven workflow where the agent profiles inference, modifies targeted code, validates effects, and iteratively refines the acceleration stack as bottlenecks shift, while preserving action quality. Experiments span six WAMs, three coding agents, and two GPU architectures.

WAMJET achieves up to 9.95x lossless speedup over upstream implementations. Approximation and hardware-aware optimization yield additional latency reductions, with comparable success rates. The results show that WAMJET can produce effective acceleration stacks for WAM deployment.

summary.en: The paper introduces WAMJET, an agentic harness for accelerating world action model inference. It gives coding agents reusable optimization guidance and tools for measurement and validation. Agents profile bottlenecks, modify targeted code, validate changes, and refine the optimization stack while preserving action quality. Experiments cover six world action models, three coding agents, and two GPU architectures. The authors report up to 9.95× lossless speedup over upstream implementations, with further latency reductions from approximation and hardware-aware optimization at comparable success rates.
summary.zh: 论文提出 WAMJET，用代理式框架加速世界动作模型推理。该框架为编码代理提供可复用的优化指导，以及测量和验证工具；代理按瓶颈分析、修改代码、验证效果并迭代优化，同时保持动作质量。实验涉及六种世界动作模型、三种编码代理和两种 GPU 架构。作者报告，相较上游实现，最高可实现9.95倍无损加速；近似计算和硬件感知优化还能进一步降低延迟，且成功率相近。

items.title: WAMJET: A Harness for World Action Model Acceleration

We build and evaluate such a system. People are detected, lifted onto the floor by ray-plane intersection, tracked in a gravity-aligned metric frame, and forecast as per-step probability maps by a small

sections.text:
A pedestrian with a phone could be shown where nearby people will be in the next few seconds, if the forecast stays on the ground while the phone moves, is calibrated, and needs only a monocular camera and visual-inertial odometry (VIO).We build and evaluate such a system.

People are detected, lifted onto the floor by ray-plane intersection, tracked in a gravity-aligned metric frame, and forecast as per-step probability maps by a small U-Net trained with a negative log-likelihood (NLL) loss on bird's-eye (SDD) and first-person (EgoTraj-Bench) trajectories.

On handheld ADVIO recordings, vertical VIO drift and the user's own changes of level silently rescale monocular ground positions (by 87% within 90 s on one clip; on another, all tracks are lost for the last 31% of the clip); keeping the camera's height above the floor constant under a low-pass-filtered altitude avoids this, though it lags on escalators.

On the SDD and EgoTraj-Bench test splits, the final forecaster lowers the NLL at 4.8 s by 1.51 and 1.37 nats relative to a fitted constant-velocity Gaussian. Lacking ground truth for people in handheld video, we score forecasts against the tracker's own later raw measurements.

In an internally pre-registered evaluation on seven held-out clips, the final forecaster's NLL is lower than the benchmark-fitted baseline's at 1.2, 2.4 and 4.8 s (by 0.17, 0.23 and 0.47 nats; 95% intervals over people exclude zero), but by less than half as much as on the development clips.

Exploratory analyses cut both ways: resampling clips instead of people widens the intervals to include zero at 1.2 and 2.4 s, and once both forecasters are recalibrated on the development clips the network is significantly better only at 1.2 s; but two clips run with ADVIO's reference poses favour the network much more when re-run with the phone's own poses.

We discuss what such self-consistency scores can and cannot show.

summary.en: The paper builds a system that forecasts pedestrian locations as probability maps using a phone’s monocular camera and visual-inertial odometry. It detects people, projects them onto the floor, tracks them in a gravity-aligned metric frame, and uses a small U-Net for forecasting. The authors report that vertical VIO drift and changes in user height can rescale ground positions; low-pass-filtered altitude helps maintain camera height above the floor but lags on escalators. Because handheld video lacks pedestrian ground truth, forecasts are scored against later tracker measurements. A preregistered evaluation on seven held-out clips shows lower NLL than the baseline, with smaller gains than on development clips and exploratory results that vary by evaluation setup.
summary.zh: 论文构建了一套用手机单目相机和视觉惯性里程计预测行人位置概率图的系统：检测行人，将其投影到地面并在重力对齐的度量坐标系中跟踪，再用小型 U-Net 预测。作者指出，手持视频中的垂直漂移和高度变化会使地面位置缩放，因此以低通滤波后的高度维持相机离地高度，可避免该问题但在自动扶梯上有滞后。由于缺少手持视频行人真值，评估使用跟踪器之后的原始测量；七段留出视频的预注册评估显示，相较基线，预测 NLL 有所降低，但幅度低于开发集，探索性分析也显示结果随评估设定而异。

items.title: Probabilistic Pedestrian Forecasts from a Handheld Phone: World-Frame Heat Maps, Visual-Inertial Height Drift, and Evaluation without Ground Truth

We introduce Closed-Loop Refinement and Execution (CLRE), a hierarchical receding-horizon control framework designed to mitigate these failure modes while leaving the upstream planner frozen and adding no new learned model. sections.text:
Learning-based driving planners are usually trained and evaluated in open loop against logged trajectories. In closed loop, a trajectory with small displacement error can still stall the vehicle, steer it into a conflict with surrounding agents, or be executed with abrupt braking.

We introduce Closed-Loop Refinement and Execution (CLRE), a hierarchical receding-horizon control framework designed to mitigate these failure modes while leaving the upstream planner frozen and adding no new learned model.

The upper layer treats the nominal trajectory as a reference and solves a finite-horizon optimal control problem that trades route progress against interaction with predicted agents.

Solving it from several initializations gives a candidate set, and a prediction-conditioned oriented-bounding-box (OBB) feasibility test retains only candidates whose minimum predicted OBB clearance over the horizon meets a threshold.

The lower layer executes the lowest-cost survivor, or a route-centerline backup when none remains, through the tracking controller supplied with the planner, augmented by a range-based speed bound and a saturated proportional braking law.

In closed-loop simulation on the 220-route Bench2Drive validation set with VAD as the upstream planner, CLRE raises the driving score from 42.26 to 55.89 and route completion from 55.69 to 71.51, and reduces collision events from 117 to 97.

summary.en: The paper introduces Closed-Loop Refinement and Execution (CLRE), a framework intended to improve learned driving planners in closed-loop settings while keeping the upstream planner frozen and adding no learned model. Its upper layer treats the nominal trajectory as a reference and uses finite-horizon optimal control to balance route progress and interaction with predicted agents. A prediction-conditioned oriented bounding box test filters candidate trajectories. The lower layer executes the lowest-cost survivor, or a route-centerline backup if none passes, with speed bounds and braking control. In closed-loop simulation on the 220-route Bench2Drive validation set using VAD, the authors report higher driving score and route completion, and fewer collision events.
summary.zh: 论文提出闭环细化与执行框架 CLRE，用于改进学习型驾驶规划器的闭环表现，同时冻结上游规划器且不增加新学习模型。上层将名义轨迹作为参考，通过有限时域最优控制权衡路线进度与周围交通参与者的交互，并以预测条件下的有向包围盒可行性测试筛选候选轨迹。下层执行成本最低的可行候选；若无候选通过，则使用路线中心线备用方案，并结合速度约束和制动控制。在使用 VAD 规划器的 Bench2Drive 220 条路线验证集闭环仿真中，作者报告驾驶分数和路线完成率提高，碰撞事件减少。

items.title: Closed-Loop Refinement and Execution for Learned Driving Planners

Whether someone is injured on a battlefield, in a natural disaster, or in an athletic event, great care is always taken with the cervical spine when transporting, rolling, or moving the patient. In this work, we present an algorithm and adaptations for bi-manual robots to stabilize the cervical spine during

sections.text:
The neck, specifically the cervical spine, is a highly fragile and mobile part of the body with a high risk of catastrophic injury. Whether someone is injured on a battlefield, in a natural disaster, or in an athletic event, great care is always taken with the cervical spine when transporting, rolling, or moving the patient.

In this work, we present an algorithm and adaptations for bi-manual robots to stabilize the cervical spine during rolling maneuvers. We investigate techniques to maximize grip strength within safety bounds and present a control approach for proper neck rotation.

We found that with our approach, a bi-manual robot is capable of achieving human-level performance in maintaining target rotational alignments. The axial alignment for the robot with prediction was within .21 degrees of human novices.

summary.en: The paper presents an algorithm and adaptations for bimanual robots to stabilize the cervical spine during rolling maneuvers. It investigates maximizing grip strength within safety bounds and controlling neck rotation. The authors report human-level performance in maintaining target rotational alignments. With prediction, the robot’s axial alignment was within 0.21 degrees of that of human novices. The abstract does not specify the evaluation setting.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种双臂机器人算法及适配方案，用于患者滚动操作时稳定颈椎，并研究安全约束下增强抓握力和控制颈部旋转的方法。作者称，该方法使机器人在保持目标旋转对齐方面达到与人类相当的表现；带预测时，机器人轴向对齐误差在文中报告为与人类新手相差0.21度。摘要未说明这些结果的具体实验环境。

items.title: Bi-manual Stabilization of the Cervical Spine for Safe Physical Human-Robot Interaction in Rolling Maneuvers

However, existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies that predict future observations from shared features leave the forecast decoupled from the actions the policy will actually execute, and impose no physical constraints on how the scene may evolve. sections.text:
Robots need to anticipate how their actions will change the world, since manipulation success hinges on the resulting contacts and object motions.

However, existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies that predict future observations from shared features leave the forecast decoupled from the actions the policy will actually execute, and impose no physical constraints on how the scene may evolve. We introduce ForeAct3D, a framework for policy-grounded future world modeling within VLA policies.

Learnable geometric queries decode depth, semantic segmentation, and camera pose from the policy representation into current and future semantic 3D scene states, and the future queries are conditioned on the policy-generated action chunk to ground the forecast in the planned interaction.

A physical-consistency closure relates the two states through background staticity and instance-level rigidity, and anchors the wrist-camera pose to end-effector kinematics. These objectives shape the shared representation used for action generation during training, and no future prediction is required at inference.

Without robot pretraining, ForeAct3D achieves 98.3\% average success on LIBERO and an average task length of 3.73 on CALVIN, outperforming its base policy on every suite.

Ablations show that semantic 3D supervision, physical consistency, and action conditioning each improve manipulation performance, and that action conditioning substantially improves future object localization.

Real-world experiments on spatial placement, object insertion, and sequential manipulation further raise average success from 6.7\% to 37.8\% over the base policy. The project page and code are available at https://github.com/anthonytao80-crypto/ForeAct3D.

summary.en: ForeAct3D grounds future scene predictions in action chunks generated by a vision-language-action policy. Geometric queries predict current and future semantic 3D states, with physical-consistency objectives based on static backgrounds, rigid objects, and wrist-camera and end-effector kinematics. These objectives shape the shared representation during training; future prediction is not needed at inference. The authors report improvements over the base policy on LIBERO and CALVIN without robot pretraining, and higher average success in real-world trials involving placement, insertion, and sequential manipulation.
summary.zh: ForeAct3D将未来场景预测与视觉语言动作策略生成的动作序列关联，并用几何查询预测当前和未来的语义三维场景状态，以背景静止、物体刚性及手腕相机与末端运动学关系施加物理一致性约束。训练时这些目标塑造共享表征，推理时不需预测未来。作者报告，在无机器人预训练时，该方法在LIBERO和CALVIN上优于基础策略；消融显示各组成部分有助于操作表现，真实机器人实验涵盖空间放置、物体插入和序列操作，平均成功率较基础策略提高。

items.title: ForeAct3D: Policy-Grounded Future World Modeling for VLA Policies

Generative planners trained on demonstration produce both in one pass, requiring neither a symbolic domain nor search. To date, however, they have relied on thousands of scripted demonstrations of fixed-base arms and executed open loop. sections.text:
Long-horizon mobile manipulation requires a task plan and the motion that executes it. Generative planners trained on demonstration produce both in one pass, requiring neither a symbolic domain nor search. To date, however, they have relied on thousands of scripted demonstrations of fixed-base arms and executed open loop.

This paper presents a hybrid flow matching planner: a single network generates the symbolic plan with masked discrete flow matching and the motion trajectory with continuous flow matching. Unlike prior generative planners, we aim to learn from a much smaller set of demonstrations and to execute the plan in closed loop.

Two properties of the data compensate for the small dataset. A demonstration resumed from any of its intermediate actions is itself a demonstration, which multiplies the training samples and enables replanning after every action. Objects of the same kind are interchangeable, which turns demonstrations of one goal into demonstrations of every permuted goal.

Our base implementation produces valid plans on 68% of held-out scenes; a training and generation scheme for the discrete plan raises this to 76%, and replanning after every action raises the task completion rate from 40% to 53% in a kinematic simulation.

The planner matches the task completion rate of motion-only flow matching policies while additionally providing the symbolic plan, and it outperforms previous hybrid diffusion formulations on both task completion and plan validity. We validate the planner on a real mobile manipulator.

Videos and project page: https://andreumatoses.github.io/research/hybrid-flow-planning

summary.en: The paper introduces a hybrid flow-matching planner that generates a symbolic task plan with masked discrete flow matching and a motion trajectory with continuous flow matching. It aims to learn from fewer demonstrations and execute closed-loop. The method uses demonstrations resumed from intermediate actions and interchangeable objects to expand training examples and support replanning. In kinematic simulation, valid plans increased from 68% to 76% of held-out scenes with a revised discrete-plan scheme, while replanning raised task completion from 40% to 53%. The authors also report validation on a real mobile manipulator.
summary.zh: 论文提出混合流匹配规划器，由单一网络以离散流匹配生成符号任务计划、以连续流匹配生成运动轨迹，目标是用较少真实演示进行闭环规划。作者利用演示可从中间动作继续、同类物体可互换这两种性质扩充训练样本并支持重规划。运动学仿真中，基础实现对68%的留出场景生成有效计划，改进离散计划训练与生成方案后为76%；逐动作重规划使任务完成率从40%升至53%。论文还称在真实移动操作机器人上进行了验证。

items.title: Learning Task and Motion Plans from Real Demonstrations with Hybrid Flow Matching

items.intro: arXiv:2610.00731v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Simulated evaluation is increasingly used alongside real-world evaluation of robot policies because it is cheaper and easier to repeat; however, its value depends on how closely its outcomes track the real robot's. We test whether our reconstruction pipeline, combining metrically scaled object geometry, authored physical parameters and scene reconstruction, reduces disagreement between simulated and real robot scores relative to a default open-source recipe. We constructed two simulated versions of one bimanual robot cell

sections.text:
Simulated evaluation is increasingly used alongside real-world evaluation of robot policies because it is cheaper and easier to repeat; however, its value depends on how closely its outcomes track the real robot's.

We test whether our reconstruction pipeline, combining metrically scaled object geometry, authored physical parameters and scene reconstruction, reduces disagreement between simulated and real robot scores relative to a default open-source recipe.

We constructed two simulated versions of one bimanual robot cell: an authored reconstruction, using object geometry at estimated metric scale, projected textures, authored physics and our own scene splat; and a baseline, referred to as the default reconstruction, using the open-source recipe of a generative single-image mesh, engine-default physics and a Gaussian-splat scene.

Both reconstructions use the same object photographs and scene video. Two policies ran five tasks each, giving ten task-policy pairs, which we call cells; each cell was run twenty times in each reconstruction with all other settings held fixed. Both reconstructions were scored against the same real trials, graded by a third-party evaluator.

Pearson correlation between the ten simulated and real cell means is r = 0.90 for the authored reconstruction and 0.51 for the default. Mean score error is 6.97 percentage points for the authored reconstruction and 17.54 for the default, a reduction of 10.56 percentage points.

These results show that improving the quality of the environment reconstruction through higher visual fidelity, authored physics and metric scale makes the simulation more faithful to the real world and narrows the sim-to-real gap.

We release the harness, the per-trial scores, every reported run's configuration, and the assets and scenes of both reconstructions.

summary.en: The study compares two simulated reconstructions of one bimanual robot cell: an authored version with metrically scaled object geometry, authored physics, and a reconstructed scene, and a baseline using an open-source recipe. Both use the same photographs and scene video. Two policies perform five tasks each; each task-policy pair is run twenty times per reconstruction and compared with the same real trials. The authors report simulated-to-real mean-score correlations of 0.90 and 0.51, and mean score errors of 6.97 and 17.54 percentage points, respectively. They conclude that higher-quality reconstruction narrows the sim-to-real gap.
summary.zh: 研究比较同一双臂机器人工作单元的两种仿真重建：一种采用估计公制尺度的物体几何、定制物理参数和场景重建，另一种采用开源默认方案。两种重建使用相同照片与场景视频；两项策略各执行五项任务，每个任务—策略组合在每种重建中运行二十次，并与相同真实试验评分比较。作者报告，定制重建的仿真与真实均分相关系数为0.90，默认重建为0.51；均分误差分别为6.97和17.54个百分点。作者认为提高环境重建质量可缩小仿真与现实的差距。

items.title: Measuring Asset and Scene Reconstruction Effects in Real-to-Sim Robot Evaluation

For example, a policy trained on diverse handover demonstrations may learn to pass a knife blade-first. To address this gap, we propose MoRE(Mode Redirection), which redirects policy rollouts

sections.text:
Behavior-cloned policies often learn multiple behavior modes from demonstration datasets, including modes that are unsafe or otherwise undesired at deployment. For example, a policy trained on diverse handover demonstrations may learn to pass a knife blade-first.

Standard remedies such as data curation and inference-time steering either require access to the original demonstrations for full retraining or add substantial inference-time overhead. To address this gap, we propose MoRE(Mode Redirection), which redirects policy rollouts toward desired behavior modes through a short "uncloning" step.

Specifically, MoRE distills the redirection signal from a temporary mode classifier into the policy weights to steer behavior. A retain loss balances this edit by preserving desired-mode competence, allowing the standalone policy to suppress unwanted modes with zero inference-time overhead.

Across eight simulated and real-world tasks, MoRE improves the average deployment success rate (SR) by 44 percentage points over the original mixed-mode policy. Among all compared adaptation and steering baselines, MoRE achieves the strongest SR and approaches the filtered-data retraining reference, while preserving task competence and inference speed.

MoRE also generalizes across robot policy backbones, including Diffusion Policy and the Pi0.5 VLA, diverse task categories, and real-world deployments.

summary.en: The paper proposes MoRE, a short “uncloning” step that distills redirection signals from a temporary mode classifier into policy weights. A retain loss is used to preserve competence in desired behavior modes, so the standalone policy can suppress unwanted modes without inference-time overhead. Across eight simulated and real-world tasks, the authors report a 44-percentage-point average deployment success-rate gain over the original mixed-mode policy. They say MoRE outperforms the compared adaptation and steering baselines and approaches filtered-data retraining.
summary.zh: 论文提出 MoRE，通过短暂的“反克隆”步骤，将临时模式分类器提供的重定向信号蒸馏到策略权重中，并以保留损失维持期望行为模式的能力，使独立策略抑制不希望出现的模式而无需推理时额外开销。作者报告，在八项仿真及现实任务中，其平均部署成功率较原混合模式策略提高44个百分点，并称其优于所比较的适配与引导基线，接近过滤数据重训参考；评估涵盖 Diffusion Policy、Pi0.5 VLA 及现实部署。

items.title: Behavior Uncloning: Distilling Mode Redirection into Policy Weights without Inference-Time Steering

Reinforcement Learning (RL) methods provide a viable and effective solution but often rely on unrealistic assumptions, such as the knowledge of humans' position and velocity. In this paper, we introduce JESSI (JAX-based E2E Safe Social Interpretable navigation), a lightweight end-to-end RL framework that maps raw LiDAR scans directly to kinematically feasible control commands. JESSI enhances safety via Dirichlet-parameterized continuous action spaces and

sections.text:
Autonomous social navigation requires balancing efficiency, physical safety, and social compliance. Reinforcement Learning (RL) methods provide a viable and effective solution but often rely on unrealistic assumptions, such as the knowledge of humans' position and velocity.

In this paper, we introduce JESSI (JAX-based E2E Safe Social Interpretable navigation), a lightweight end-to-end RL framework that maps raw LiDAR scans directly to kinematically feasible control commands.

JESSI enhances safety via Dirichlet-parameterized continuous action spaces and deterministic bounding, while an integrated attention-based perception module extracts probabilistic human states for interpretable, socially aware decision-making.

Through extensive simulations and real-world deployment on a differential-drive robot, we demonstrate that jointly optimizing the RL policy with a supervised perception signal in a multi-task paradigm enhances social behavior.

Ultimately, JESSI is able to balance high navigation success rates and superior social behaviors compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

items.title: End-to-End Safe Social Navigation via Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning and Probabilistic Perception

items.intro: arXiv:2610.05011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Floorplans provide compact and widely available geometric maps for indoor localization, but existing high-performing floorplan-based methods still convert them into dense scene-specific offline databases, tying accuracy, storage, and runtime to the sampling resolution of the discretized pose space. FreeLoc introduces an efficient online geometric querying and diffusion-aided refinement scheme, which retrieves plausible pose anchors

sections.text:
Floorplans provide compact and widely available geometric maps for indoor localization, but existing high-performing floorplan-based methods still convert them into dense scene-specific offline databases, tying accuracy, storage, and runtime to the sampling resolution of the discretized pose space.

We present FreeLoc, an online RGB-based floorplan localization framework that treats the floorplan as a directly queryable geometric map.

FreeLoc introduces an efficient online geometric querying and diffusion-aided refinement scheme, which retrieves plausible pose anchors through on-the-fly floorplan ray querying and refines them into accurate continuous pose estimates.

For sequential localization, FreeLoc develops an online likelihood construction strategy that bridges single-frame localization and probabilistic temporal fusion by constructing likelihoods from coarse-sampled candidates and refined pose hypotheses, enabling histogram-filter-based temporal fusion without offline databases.

Experiments demonstrate real-time online inference and state-of-the-art performance in both single-frame and sequential localization, while real-world results validate practical deployability in indoor robotic localization scenarios.

summary.en: The paper presents FreeLoc, an online RGB indoor localization framework that treats a floorplan as a directly queryable geometric map, without an offline dense scene database. It retrieves plausible pose anchors through online ray queries and refines them into continuous estimates with diffusion assistance. For sequential localization, it builds likelihoods from coarse candidates and refined hypotheses for histogram-filter temporal fusion. The authors report real-time online inference and state-of-the-art performance in single-frame and sequential localization experiments; real-world results are presented as evidence of practical deployability for indoor robots.
summary.zh: 论文提出 FreeLoc，一种在线 RGB 室内定位框架，将平面图作为可直接查询的几何地图，避免依赖离线密集场景数据库。它通过在线射线查询获取候选位姿锚点，再以扩散辅助方法细化为连续位姿估计；序列定位则从粗采样候选和细化假设构造似然，并用直方图滤波进行时序融合。作者报告实验实现实时在线推理，并在单帧与序列定位中达到先进性能；现实结果用于验证其在室内机器人定位中的实际可部署性。

items.title: FreeLoc: Online Floorplan Localization via Diffusion-Aided Pose Refinement

In most practical systems, the process noise and measurement noise covariances are defined globally and shared across object classes, presuming identical uncertainty characteristics across heterogeneous traffic participants. sections.text:
Kalman filter (KF)-based multi-object tracking (MOT) remains a strong baseline for autonomous driving due to its strong performance, computational efficiency and interpretability.

In most practical systems, the process noise and measurement noise covariances are defined globally and shared across object classes, presuming identical uncertainty characteristics across heterogeneous traffic participants. This work revisits this assumption and proposes CANMOT, a class-aware and object-aligned noise modeling framework for KF-based 3D MOT.

Class-specific diagonal process and measurement covariance matrices are introduced and optionally expressed in the object coordinate frame to preserve longitudinal-lateral anisotropy.

Systematic experiments on the nuScenes benchmark show that class-aware and object-aligned noise modeling improves tracking performance and substantially reduces identity switches compared to state-of-the-art (SotA).

In addition, the consistency of the estimated uncertainty is analyzed using the Average Normalized Estimation Error Squared (ANEES) and $\chi^2$-based violation tests. The results reveal severe overconfidence in standard KF-based MOT baselines.

While the proposed formulation improves calibration without modifying the underlying filtering framework, it still exhibits substantial inconsistency, highlighting the need for further research in this area. Code is available at https://github.com/rst-tu-dortmund/CANMOT

summary.en: The paper proposes CANMOT, a class-aware noise modeling framework for Kalman-filter-based 3D multi-object tracking. It assigns class-specific diagonal process and measurement covariance matrices, optionally expressed in object coordinates to preserve longitudinal-lateral anisotropy. Experiments on nuScenes show improved tracking performance and fewer identity switches. The authors assess uncertainty consistency with ANEES and chi-squared violation tests, finding severe overconfidence in standard KF-based MOT baselines. CANMOT improves calibration without changing the filtering framework, but substantial inconsistency remains.
summary.zh: 论文提出 CANMOT，针对自动驾驶三维多目标跟踪中的卡尔曼滤波器，按类别建模过程噪声与测量噪声协方差，并可在目标坐标系中表达以保留纵横向差异。在 nuScenes 基准上的实验显示，该建模提升跟踪表现并减少身份切换。作者还用 ANEES 与基于卡方的违例检验分析不确定性，发现标准卡尔曼跟踪基线存在严重过度自信。尽管该方法改善校准且不改变滤波框架，估计仍明显不一致。

items.title: CANMOT: Class-Aware Noise Modeling for Multi-Object Tracking in Autonomous Driving

LightVLN compresses

sections.text:
Aerial vision-and-language navigation (VLN) enables unmanned aerial vehicles to execute long-horizon natural-language instructions from visual observations in complex three-dimensional environments.

However, recent aerial VLN models often rely on large-scale vision-language backbones and dense visual histories, imposing substantial computation and memory costs that hinder onboard deployment.

We propose LightVLN, a lightweight history-aware aerial VLN framework that combines a compact 0.5B language backbone with compact representations of both historical and current observations. LightVLN compresses each historical frame into a single token using visual features already computed by the policy.

It further introduces history- and instruction-conditioned local aggregation to reduce the current observation from 256 to 32 visual tokens while preserving navigation-relevant spatial information. With up to 16 historical frames, the policy uses at most 48 observation-derived tokens.

On the public OpenFly dataset, LightVLN achieves 50.93% Test-Seen and 36.14% Test-Unseen success rates (SR), outperforming the evaluated 7B language-backbone baselines on most reported metrics. It also achieves 25.83% SR on AerialVLN-S Val-Seen.

In a reconstructed unseen campus, we deploy LightVLN on a DJI M350 RTK with an external Jetson Orin NX 16 GB for closed-loop onboard-compute real-to-sim hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) evaluation, achieving 14.61 Hz model inference and 11.13 Hz end-to-end decision updates.

These results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of LightVLN for aerial navigation.

summary.en: The paper proposes LightVLN, a lightweight aerial vision-and-language navigation framework with a compact language backbone. It compresses each historical frame into one token and uses history- and instruction-conditioned local aggregation to reduce current-observation tokens. The authors report success rates on OpenFly and AerialVLN-S, with LightVLN outperforming evaluated 7B-backbone baselines on most reported metrics. They also conduct closed-loop, onboard-compute real-to-sim hardware-in-the-loop evaluation in a reconstructed unseen campus and report inference and decision-update rates.
summary.zh: 论文提出轻量级空中视觉语言导航框架 LightVLN，采用紧凑语言骨干网络，并将历史帧压缩为单个视觉令牌；通过历史和指令条件下的局部聚合，将当前观测令牌由256个减至32个。在 OpenFly 和 AerialVLN-S 数据集上报告了导航成功率，并称其在多数已报告指标上优于所评估的7B语言骨干基线。作者还在重建的未见校园中开展闭环机载计算实虚结合硬件在环评估，报告了模型推理和端到端决策更新频率。

items.title: LightVLN: Efficient Aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation with Compact Memory and History-Guided Local Aggregation

While two-wheeled platforms are highly manoeuvrable, their constant balancing adjustments make onboard odometry highly unreliable for precise navigation. Furthermore, the addition of a side-mounted robotic arm introduces unactuated lateral roll moments when a payload is lifted, a challenge heavily compounded on uneven terrain. To solve these

sections.text:
We propose a hierarchical control framework to address severe dynamic instabilities and navigational drift that arise when a two-wheeled inverted pendulum (TWIP) robot attempts asymmetric object manipulation.

While two-wheeled platforms are highly manoeuvrable, their constant balancing adjustments make onboard odometry highly unreliable for precise navigation. Furthermore, the addition of a side-mounted robotic arm introduces unactuated lateral roll moments when a payload is lifted, a challenge heavily compounded on uneven terrain.

To solve these coupled problems, our architecture divides the workload. An offboard vision system tracks overhead ArUco markers to provide high-latency global waypoint navigation, bypassing odometry drift. Simultaneously, a low-latency onboard control loop rejects active physical disturbances using inertial and encoder data.

In our physical experiments, this dual-loop approach enabled the custom-built robot to navigate accurately, reject transient impacts from speed bumps, adapt to a dynamic seesaw ramp, and carry a payload securely without falling over its narrow wheelbase.

summary.en: The paper proposes a hierarchical control framework for navigation and asymmetric manipulation by a two-wheeled inverted pendulum robot. An offboard vision system tracks overhead ArUco markers to provide global waypoint navigation, while a low-latency onboard loop uses inertial and encoder data to reject physical disturbances. In physical experiments, the authors report accurate navigation, rejection of transient speed-bump impacts, adaptation to a dynamic seesaw ramp, and secure payload carrying without the robot falling over.
summary.zh: 论文提出用于两轮倒立摆机器人导航和非对称操作的分层控制框架，针对负载搬运时的导航漂移、动态不稳定和侧向滚转力矩问题。系统由两部分组成：机外视觉系统跟踪顶部 ArUco 标记，提供全局航点导航；机载低延迟控制回路利用惯性与编码器数据抑制物理扰动。作者报告称，在实体机器人实验中，该方法支持机器人准确导航、抵抗减速带的瞬态冲击、适应动态跷跷板坡道，并在不倾倒的情况下稳定搬运负载。

items.title: LQR-ArUco Fusion: Robust Hierarchical Control for Navigation and Asymmetric Manipulation in Two-Wheeled Robots

Construction sites, however, differ fundamentally from public roads and challenge many assumptions underlying conventional autonomous driving systems. They are characterized by unstructured terrain, airborne dust, continuously evolving site conditions, and construction-specific objects

sections.text:
Autoware is an open-source autonomous driving software platform widely adopted by researchers and industry developers. Originally developed primarily for public-road applications, including passenger vehicles, taxis, and buses, Autoware is increasingly being extended to off-road environments such as construction and agricultural sites.

Construction sites, however, differ fundamentally from public roads and challenge many assumptions underlying conventional autonomous driving systems. They are characterized by unstructured terrain, airborne dust, continuously evolving site conditions, and construction-specific objects.

This paper presents lessons learned from ongoing efforts to extend an Autoware-based autonomous driving system to large dump trucks operating at construction sites. We identify gaps between public-road and off-road construction applications across the sensing, mapping, localization, perception, planning, and control modules of the Autoware stack.

We then discuss potential solutions for addressing these gaps, with particular emphasis on ongoing LiDAR-based perception pipeline development and findings from field testing. Finally, we propose a roadmap toward end-to-end autonomous driving for construction vehicles.

summary.en: The paper describes ongoing efforts to extend Autoware to large dump trucks at construction sites, where unstructured terrain, airborne dust, changing conditions, and construction-specific objects challenge public-road assumptions. It identifies gaps between road and construction applications across sensing, mapping, localization, perception, planning, and control. The authors discuss potential solutions, focusing on development of a LiDAR perception pipeline and findings from field testing, and propose a roadmap toward end-to-end autonomous driving for construction vehicles.
summary.zh: 论文总结将 Autoware 扩展至建筑工地大型自卸卡车自动驾驶的持续工作，指出非结构化地形、扬尘、场地持续变化及专用目标等因素，使工地环境不同于公共道路。作者从感知、地图、定位、感知、规划和控制模块分析道路与越野施工应用间的差距，并讨论可能的解决方向，重点介绍正在开发的激光雷达感知流程及现场测试发现。论文最后提出面向工程车辆端到端自动驾驶的路线图；摘要未声称该路线图已实现。

items.title: Autoware in Construction: Gap Analysis and LiDAR Perception Toward Off-Road Autonomous Driving

items.intro: arXiv:2610.03773v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Soft tactile sensors elevate robotic touch through enhanced flexibility and adaptability, yet most existing designs depend on embedded electronics that are susceptible to interference and environmental limitations. In this work, we leverage fluid-solid interactions to develop a class of soft tactile sensors that operate entirely without electronics at the sensing site. The sensor comprises a fluid-filled elastomeric channel connected to only two external pressure sensors. Touching different regions of the elastomeric surface displaces

sections.text:
Soft tactile sensors elevate robotic touch through enhanced flexibility and adaptability, yet most existing designs depend on embedded electronics that are susceptible to interference and environmental limitations.

In this work, we leverage fluid-solid interactions to develop a class of soft tactile sensors that operate entirely without electronics at the sensing site. The sensor comprises a fluid-filled elastomeric channel connected to only two external pressure sensors.

Touching different regions of the elastomeric surface displaces the viscous fluid, producing distinct pressure patterns that encode both touch position and force.

These signals are decoded through a machine learning framework that integrates feature extraction, soft clustering, and adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference to achieve accurate localization and force estimation.

We validate this concept through single-point touch localization and force estimation in a linear (1D) sensor and extend the same sensing principle to 2D tactile mapping by routing the channel across the surface using space-filling curves, while maintaining the same minimal hardware setup.

This simple approach remains effective in environments where conventional electronic sensors often fail, such as underwater or in the presence of magnetic interference.

summary.en: The paper presents soft tactile sensors based on fluid-solid interaction, with no electronics at the sensing site. A fluid-filled elastomeric channel connects to two external pressure sensors; touch produces pressure patterns that encode location and force. A machine-learning framework combines feature extraction, soft clustering, and adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference for localization and force estimation. The authors demonstrate single-point localization and force estimation with a one-dimensional sensor, then extend the principle to two-dimensional tactile mapping using space-filling channel paths and the same minimal hardware.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种利用流固相互作用的软触觉传感器，在传感位置无需电子元件：充液弹性通道连接两个外部压力传感器，触碰表面不同区域会产生可表征位置和作用力的压力模式。机器学习框架结合特征提取、软聚类和自适应神经模糊推理，用于定位与力估计。作者通过一维传感器的单点触摸定位和力估计验证该方法，并以空间填充曲线路由通道扩展到二维触觉映射，保持相同的精简硬件配置。

items.title: Tactile Perception through Fluid-Solid Interaction

items.intro: arXiv:2610.05062v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models translate multimodal observations into low-level robot actions. During robot operation, each control period sets an inference deadline, and overruns leave the robot acting on stale observations, reducing task success. Meeting this deadline motivates on-device or nearby edge execution, where a single robot requires batch-1 inference outside the design point of LLM serving systems. Although VLA architectures combine familiar vision-language, autoregressive, and diffusion-style components, their runtime behavior in this batch-1 control

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models translate multimodal observations into low-level robot actions. During robot operation, each control period sets an inference deadline, and overruns leave the robot acting on stale observations, reducing task success.

Meeting this deadline motivates on-device or nearby edge execution, where a single robot requires batch-1 inference outside the design point of LLM serving systems. Although VLA architectures combine familiar vision-language, autoregressive, and diffusion-style components, their runtime behavior in this batch-1 control setting remains uncharacterized.

We characterize four representative VLA models on an edge GPU server and two onboard SoCs, using single-inference profiling and 43,200 closed-loop episodes.

Action tensor dimensionality determines whether a stage is memory- or compute-bound, platform balance can shift that bottleneck, and GPU frequency scaling yields a platform-dependent energy-latency sweet spot.

In closed-loop operation, overlapping inference with action execution creates an accuracy-speed-energy tradeoff, and no configuration is Pareto-dominant across deployment SLOs. These results guide joint design of VLA model architectures, hardware, and runtime policies.

summary.en: This work characterizes four vision-language-action models in batch-one, deadline-driven robot control. The authors profile single inferences on an edge GPU server and two onboard SoCs, and evaluate closed-loop operation. They report that action tensor dimensionality and platform balance affect whether stages are memory- or compute-bound, while frequency scaling produces platform-dependent energy-latency tradeoffs. Overlapping inference and action execution also trades accuracy, speed, and energy, with no configuration dominating across deployment service objectives.
summary.zh: 本文分析视觉—语言—动作模型在具身机器人单批次、周期性控制场景中的运行特征。作者在边缘GPU服务器和两种机载SoC上，对四种代表性模型进行单次推理剖析，并开展闭环评估。结果显示，动作张量维度及平台配置会影响计算或内存瓶颈，频率调节带来的能耗—时延折中因平台而异；推理与动作执行重叠则形成准确性、速度和能耗权衡，没有一种配置在所有部署服务目标下占优。

items.title: Beyond LLM Serving: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Workloads for Embodied AI System Design

items.intro: arXiv:2610.06280v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World action models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation. They act by first predicting how a task should be performed and then decoding the actions from that future. However, the remaining actions are invalid once execution drifts from the prediction. Simply replanning from the already out of distribution state rarely restores what the task still requires; existing execution monitors decide when to stop, but not what to restore. We

sections.text:
World action models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation. They act by first predicting how a task should be performed and then decoding the actions from that future. However, the remaining actions are invalid once execution drifts from the prediction.

Simply replanning from the already out of distribution state rarely restores what the task still requires; existing execution monitors decide when to stop, but not what to restore. We observe that the answer is already in hand: the future the WAM predicted before acting depicts exactly the states it intended to pass through.

We introduce FAVOR (Future Anchored Verification and Online Recovery), a lightweight framework that keeps these predicted frames as anchors and uses them for verification and recovery. An Anchor Verifier compares each observation with its anchor, together with the executed actions, to flag deviations that break the task.

Anchor-Guided Recovery uses a vision-language model to turn the flagged anchor into a short corrective instruction. Under strengthened instruction guidance, the WAM executes this instruction to return to the intended future. It then resumes the task.

FAVOR raises the task success of the base WAM from 97.85% to 98.10% on LIBERO and from 72.60% to 72.98% on LIBERO-Plus without modifying the policy.

summary.en: The paper introduces FAVOR, a framework for verifying and recovering world action models during robotic manipulation. It retains predicted future frames as anchors; an Anchor Verifier compares observations and executed actions with these anchors to flag task-breaking deviations. A vision-language model converts a flagged anchor into a short corrective instruction, which the WAM follows under strengthened instruction guidance before resuming the task. The authors report improved base-model task success on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus without modifying the policy.
summary.zh: 本文提出FAVOR，用于在世界动作模型执行机器人操作任务时，借助模型行动前预测的未来画面进行验证和在线恢复。锚点验证器结合观测与已执行动作识别可能破坏任务的偏差；恢复模块通过视觉—语言模型生成简短纠正指令，并在强化指令引导下让模型回到预期状态后继续任务。摘要报告，FAVOR在LIBERO和LIBERO-Plus上提高了基础模型的任务成功率，且无需修改策略。

items.title: Future Anchored Verification and Online Recovery for World Action Models

By modeling the robot as a first-order system, they generate a feedback-based desired velocity field that guides the robot toward a target while avoiding obstacles. However, extending such feedback planners to systems with higher-order dynamics, while preserving safety and stability properties, is not a straightforward task. In the present work, we propose an approach that adapts existing feedback-based kinematic

sections.text:
Kinematic motion planners are among the most widely used control approaches in robotic applications. By modeling the robot as a first-order system, they generate a feedback-based desired velocity field that guides the robot toward a target while avoiding obstacles.

However, extending such feedback planners to systems with higher-order dynamics, while preserving safety and stability properties, is not a straightforward task.

In the present work, we propose an approach that adapts existing feedback-based kinematic motion planners to second-order autonomous systems while retaining their safety and almost global asymptotic stability guarantees.

We consider two general classes of kinematic motion planners: those derived from navigation functions and those defined directly through desired velocity fields without relying on an underlying navigation function.

To validate the proposed methodology, two feedback-based kinematic motion planners are adapted to second-order systems and evaluated both in simulations and experimentally.

summary.en: This work proposes adapting feedback-based kinematic motion planners to autonomous systems with second-order dynamics, while retaining safety and almost-global asymptotic stability guarantees. It considers planners derived from navigation functions and planners defined directly through desired velocity fields. The authors adapt two feedback-based kinematic planners to second-order systems and evaluate them in simulations and experiments. The abstract does not specify quantitative outcomes or detailed experimental results.
summary.zh: 本文提出一种方法，将基于反馈的运动学运动规划器扩展到具有二阶动力学的自主系统，并声称保留安全性和几乎全局渐近稳定性保证。研究涵盖两类规划器：基于导航函数的规划器，以及直接定义期望速度场的规划器。作者将两个反馈式运动学规划器改造为二阶系统，并通过仿真和实验进行评估。摘要未给出具体实验结果或量化性能数据。

items.title: From Kinematic Motion Planners to Dynamic Autonomous Navigation with Obstacle Avoidance (Extended version)

However, sensing robustness does not necessarily translate into robust downstream planning, while existing 4D radar benchmarks focus primarily on perception rather than trajectory planning. sections.text:
Adverse weather and poor illumination remain major challenges for robust ego-trajectory planning in mobile autonomy. 4D radar offers reliable sensing under adverse conditions and direct radial-velocity measurements.

However, sensing robustness does not necessarily translate into robust downstream planning, while existing 4D radar benchmarks focus primarily on perception rather than trajectory planning. We present Radar2Plan, a modular benchmark for open-loop ego-trajectory planning using real-world 4D radar data.

Radar2Plan connects sensor encoders, scene representations, and planning heads through common interfaces, enabling controlled comparisons between different sensor and planner configurations.

Using DSERT-RoLL and MAN TruckScenes, we evaluated seven combinations of camera, 4D radar, and LiDAR in four representative planning baselines and 12 weather and illumination conditions under a unified protocol. To our knowledge, Radar2Plan is the first benchmark dedicated to evaluating real-world 4D radars for autonomous driving planning.

Experiments show that 4D radar alone supports competitive ego-trajectory planning and robust performance under adverse conditions. Sensor-configuration comparisons further demonstrate its complementary value to other modalities, while revealing dependencies on sensor combination and planning architecture.

The modular design also supports additional datasets, sensing modalities, and planners, providing a flexible foundation for future research on radar-based autonomous driving planning.

summary.en: The paper presents Radar2Plan, a modular benchmark for open-loop ego-trajectory planning with real-world 4D radar data. Common interfaces connect sensor encoders, scene representations, and planning heads for controlled comparisons. The authors evaluate seven camera, radar, and LiDAR configurations across four planning baselines and varied weather and illumination conditions using two datasets. They report that 4D radar alone supports competitive planning and robust performance in adverse conditions; its complementary value depends on sensor combinations and planning architecture.
summary.zh: 本文介绍Radar2Plan，这是一个使用真实4D雷达数据评估开环自车轨迹规划的模块化基准。它通过统一接口连接传感器编码器、场景表示和规划器，支持比较不同传感器与规划配置。作者基于两个数据集，评估相机、4D雷达和激光雷达的七种组合、四种规划基线及多种天气和光照条件。实验显示，单独使用4D雷达可实现有竞争力的规划表现，并在恶劣条件下保持稳健；其与其他模态的互补效果取决于传感器组合和规划架构。

items.title: Radar2Plan: Benchmarking 4D Radar for End-to-End Open-Loop Ego-Trajectory Planning

sections.text:
Balanced discrete optimal transport between n sources and n targets of unit mass is exactly the minimum-cost assignment problem-a bipartite perfect matching-and is therefore solvable exactly by industrial matching engines in milliseconds to seconds.

We ask when the exact approach beats the standard approximate alternatives, entropic Sinkhorn and its accelerated variant Greenkhorn, and make the sparse-exact side certified by a textbook LP dual-feasibility clip.

Three contributions. (i) Measurement: on dense 2-D instances, exact matching (Jonker-Volgenant) is faster and strictly more accurate than either approximate method throughout the moderate-n regime (0.01 s at n=500 to 11.5 s at n=8000); reaching a 1% quality target on the same hardware requires roughly 10-80 min for Greenkhorn (factors 4e2-6e4 over exact; plain Sinkhorn is 20-650x slower still), a rough power-law projection beyond the measured range.

Greenkhorn's measured speedup over plain Sinkhorn is only 1.0-1.5x on most converged cells. (ii) A simple kNN-pool gap certificate: given a pool matching and its Blossom dual, a one-pass O(n^2) clip produces a dense-feasible lower bound; combined with the Sinkhorn dual potential (valid at every iterate, not just at convergence), the bound is valid on all 45 measured configurations and tightens monotonically with k. (iii) A multi-robot task-allocation sanity check where the discrete plan is the deliverable: per-round exact assignment costs 0.1-68 ms, while a Sinkhorn-plus-hardening pipeline costs 0.12-15.9 s and accumulates 6-27% extra travel over 15 rounds.

The Sinkhorn family's large-n dense regime is acknowledged and left untouched. Code, data, and results under MIT: https://github.com/dimkadimon/OT-Blossom.

summary.en: The paper compares exact matching with Sinkhorn and Greenkhorn approximations for balanced discrete optimal transport. The authors report that Jonker-Volgenant matching is faster and more accurate on measured moderate-size dense 2-D instances. They introduce a lower-bound certificate combining a k-nearest-neighbor matching pool with a dual-feasibility clip, valid on all 45 measured configurations and tightening with k. In a multi-robot allocation check, exact assignment is faster, while Sinkhorn plus hardening adds travel over 15 rounds. The large-n dense regime is left unaddressed.
summary.zh: 论文比较离散平衡最优传输中的精确匹配与 Sinkhorn、Greenkhorn 近似方法。作者报告，在测量的中等规模稠密二维实例上，Jonker-Volgenant 匹配更快且精度更高，并提出结合 k 近邻匹配池与对偶可行性裁剪的下界证书，在全部 45 个测量配置上有效且随 k 收紧。多机器人任务分配检验中，精确分配耗时较短，Sinkhorn 加硬化方案在 15 轮中产生额外行程。作者未处理 Sinkhorn 在超大规模稠密情形的表现。

items.title: Exact Optimal Transport by Matching

sections.text:
World-action models (WAMs) augment robot policies with action-conditioned environment dynamics, yet existing approaches largely rely on future observation reconstruction or generic latent prediction and lack structured, control-oriented world representations tightly coupled with action generation.

We introduce Magic-W0, a world-action foundation model that jointly models structured physical state evolution and continuous actions. Magic-W0 represents interaction as a Structured World Transition consisting of Current State, Transition, and Future State.

Current State combines vision-language context with Current 3D Geometry; Transition is represented by 3D Motion capturing action-induced three-dimensional changes; and Future State is represented by Future Semantics describing task-relevant outcomes.

To couple prediction and control, we propose a layer-aligned world-action interaction architecture in which evolving action hypotheses condition world-transition prediction, while predicted world representations continuously inform action generation.

Magic-W0 is pre-trained on large-scale egocentric human manipulation, UMI, real-robot, and simulation data, with latent supervision for geometry, 3D motion, and future semantics from pre-trained visual models.

Inference-time interventions show that structured world representations respond systematically to changes in candidate actions and that action-related information propagates through shared 3D representations into future semantic predictions. On RoboDojo-Sim, Magic-W0 achieves an average Score of 27.10, the highest among the compared WAMs.

Across multiple real-robot tasks, it also demonstrates strong downstream performance after fine-tuning with limited downstream data, supporting generalization and rapid adaptation.

summary.en: The paper presents Magic-W0, a world-action foundation model that jointly represents structured physical-state changes and continuous actions. Interaction is modeled through current state, 3D action-induced motion, and future task-relevant semantics. Its architecture lets action hypotheses condition transition prediction and feeds predicted representations back into action generation. Pretraining uses human manipulation, real-robot, and simulation data. The authors report that interventions make structured representations respond to candidate actions, and that Magic-W0 has the highest average score among compared world-action models on RoboDojo-Sim. Fine-tuned real-robot tasks are presented as evidence of performance with limited downstream data.
summary.zh: 论文提出 Magic-W0，一种联合建模结构化物理状态变化与连续动作的世界-动作基础模型。它将交互表示为当前状态、三维动作引起的变化和未来任务相关语义，并通过共享表示让动作假设影响世界转移预测、预测结果反馈动作生成。模型使用人类操作、真实机器人及仿真等数据预训练。作者报告，干预实验显示结构化表示会随候选动作变化；在 RoboDojo-Sim 上，其平均得分在比较的世界-动作模型中最高。多个真实机器人任务的微调结果被用于说明有限下游数据下的表现与适应能力。

items.title: Magic-W0: A Structured World-Action Foundation Model for Physical Intelligence

items.intro: arXiv:2610.04366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliable safety evaluation of autonomous vehicles (AVs) is essential to improving road safety, yet it depends critically on realistic simulation of rare crashes. Existing crash scenario generation methods can increase collision occurrence, but often fail to realistically reproduce how crashes evolve before impact or the distribution of crash types observed in the real world. Here, we present CrashSim, a human behavior-informed crash scenario generation framework that uses real-world crash priors to guide generative

sections.text:
Reliable safety evaluation of autonomous vehicles (AVs) is essential to improving road safety, yet it depends critically on realistic simulation of rare crashes.

Existing crash scenario generation methods can increase collision occurrence, but often fail to realistically reproduce how crashes evolve before impact or the distribution of crash types observed in the real world.

Here, we present CrashSim, a human behavior-informed crash scenario generation framework that uses real-world crash priors to guide generative multi-agent traffic simulation for more reliable AV safety evaluation.

These priors capture how real-world crashes evolve before impact and how different crash types are distributed, allowing limited crash data to guide realistic and scalable scenario generation across naturalistic driving contexts.

We evaluate CrashSim against competing methods, showing that it more closely reproduces real-world pre-impact behavior, collision dynamics, collision geometry and crash-type distributions. We further use CrashSim to construct nuCrash dataset, containing over 4,000 crash and near-crash scenarios.

Closed-loop evaluation of five AV planners shows that nuCrash more effectively exposes differences in planner safety capabilities than nuScenes. An LLM-assisted evaluation agent further analyzes planner failures to provide capability-level diagnoses and targeted improvement guidance.

Together, CrashSim enables realistic and scalable crash generation for more informative AV safety evaluation.

summary.en: The paper presents CrashSim, which uses real-world crash priors and human behavior to generate multi-agent traffic simulation scenarios that reflect pre-impact evolution and crash-type distributions. The authors report closer reproduction of real-world pre-impact behavior, collision dynamics, geometry, and crash-type distributions than competing methods. They use the framework to construct nuCrash, with over 4,000 crash and near-crash scenarios. Closed-loop evaluation of five AV planners reportedly exposes safety differences more effectively with nuCrash than with nuScenes. An LLM-assisted agent analyzes planner failures and provides capability-level diagnoses and improvement guidance.
summary.zh: 论文提出 CrashSim，利用真实事故先验和人类行为信息生成多智能体交通仿真中的事故场景，以再现碰撞前行为及现实事故类型分布。作者报告，与对比方法相比，CrashSim 更接近真实世界的碰撞前行为、碰撞动态、几何特征和事故类型分布，并据此构建包含 4,000 多个事故与险情场景的 nuCrash 数据集。对五种自动驾驶规划器的闭环评估显示，nuCrash 比 nuScenes 更能揭示规划器安全能力差异；另有一个 LLM 辅助评估代理分析失败并提供改进指导。

items.title: Human Behavior-Informed Crash Scenario Generation with Real-World Crash Priors for Autonomous Vehicle Safety Evaluation

sections.text:
Quadruped robots entering hospitals, care homes, and quiet offices must be context-appropriate not only in where they move but in how loudly they move: a legged robot's locomotion noise, dominated by foot-ground impacts, is itself a social variable.

Prior social navigation respects human space but treats the robot as acoustically uniform, while quiet-locomotion methods reduce noise to an operator-specified, context-blind level.

We present TACET, a context-appropriate acoustic-social navigation method that infers social context from the robot's egocentric view and decides both where it walks and how loudly, coupling a slow fine-tuned vision-language reasoner to a fast reactive controller through a single compact behavior token, .

The same token conditions both a social costmap (where to go) and a quiet locomotion policy (how loudly to move), while a structured out-of-view memory keeps recently seen people in the reasoner's context after they leave the camera view.

On a real quadruped, context-conditioned locomotion lowers locomotion noise by up to 9.3 dBA at matched speed, and across our scenarios the full method keeps personal-space compliance at 100% with low acoustic intrusion ( < =2.9 dBA), jointly improving spatial and acoustic performance in the evaluated scenarios.

The project page is available at https://rcilab.khu.ac.kr/tacet/.

summary.en: The paper presents TACET, an acoustic-social navigation method for quadrupeds that infers social context from an egocentric view and chooses both where and how loudly to move. A behavior token connects a slow fine-tuned vision-language reasoner with a fast controller, conditioning both a social costmap and a quiet locomotion policy. Out-of-view memory retains recently seen people after they leave the camera. On a real quadruped, the authors report up to 9.3 dBA lower locomotion noise at matched speed; across evaluated scenarios, the full method maintains 100% personal-space compliance with acoustic intrusion at or below 2.9 dBA.
summary.zh: 论文提出 TACET，一种面向四足机器人的声学-社交导航方法，根据机器人第一人称视角推断社交情境，同时决定行走位置和运动音量。慢速微调视觉语言推理器通过行为令牌连接快速控制器；该令牌共同调节社交代价地图与安静行走策略，并由视野外记忆保留刚离开镜头的人物信息。在真实四足机器人实验中，匹配速度时情境条件运动噪声最多降低 9.3 dBA；在所评估场景中，完整方法保持 100% 个人空间合规，声学侵入不高于 2.9 dBA。

items.title: TACET: Context-Appropriate Acoustic-Social Navigation for Quadrupeds

We move the localization stack entirely off the aerial platform onto a quadruped robot with a 7-degree-of-freedom (DOF) arm, which supplies the micro-UAV (27 g bare, 42 g with fiducial markers) its full 6-DOF pose. A camera at the arm's end-effector detects

sections.text:
Micro unmanned aerial vehicles (micro-UAVs) are small enough to reach confined spaces that larger robots cannot access, but too small to carry the sensing and computing power required for autonomous flight.

We move the localization stack entirely off the aerial platform onto a quadruped robot with a 7-degree-of-freedom (DOF) arm, which supplies the micro-UAV (27 g bare, 42 g with fiducial markers) its full 6-DOF pose.

A camera at the arm's end-effector detects AprilTag fiducial markers on the drone and composes that observation with the quadruped's own self-localization to place the drone in a shared map frame, so the ground robot localizes its partner, rather than only tracking it relative to the camera.

The arm acts as an actively-controlled observer, repositioning to keep the drone in view as both robots move; the drone carries only an inertial measurement unit and fuses the external pose to fly commanded setpoints. In lab flights the external pose is accurate to 12-16 mm, enough to fly the drone autonomously within 2-5 cm of motion-capture-fed control.

Having the quadruped actively follow the drone reduces the tracking error from 11.0 cm to 6.9 cm by holding the camera in the close range, where the markers are most accurate.

summary.en: The paper presents a system in which a quadruped provides localization and active tracking for a micro-UAV. A camera on its seven-degree-of-freedom arm detects AprilTags on the drone and combines those observations with the quadruped’s self-localization to estimate the drone’s pose in a shared map frame. In lab flights, external pose accuracy was 12–16 mm. The authors report autonomous flight within 2–5 cm of motion-capture-fed control and a reduction in tracking error from 11.0 cm to 6.9 cm when the quadruped actively follows the drone.
summary.zh: 本文提出由四足机器人为微型无人机提供定位与主动跟踪的方案。四足机器人搭载七自由度机械臂，末端相机识别无人机上的 AprilTag，并结合四足机器人的自定位，将无人机位姿置于共享地图坐标系；机械臂还会调整位置以持续观测移动中的无人机。实验室飞行中，外部位姿精度为 12–16 毫米。作者称，该精度支持无人机在自主飞行时与动作捕捉控制保持 2–5 厘米距离；主动跟随使跟踪误差从 11.0 厘米降至 6.9 厘米。

items.title: Towards Quadruped-Provided Localization and Active Tracking for Micro-UAVs

They can see and act, but they do not imagine the future before acting.
