Unified models bring these modalities into one architecture, but they either decode autoregressively, one token

sections.text:
Vision-language-action models (VLAs) inherit strong semantic grounding from pretrained vision-language backbones but are typically optimized for predicting actions rather than future observations. They can see and act, but they do not imagine the future before acting.

World action models (WAMs) built on video diffusion backbones can imagine but treat language as frozen conditioning on a continuous latent space. Unified models bring these modalities into one architecture, but they either decode autoregressively, one token at a time, or keep video continuous with an auxiliary action head.

In this work, we present SUAVE, a Single vocabulary Unified Action-Video modEl in which a masked diffusion transformer generates video and actions conditioned on language, with all three modalities represented as discrete tokens in a shared sequence.

Choosing which tokens to mask at inference turns the same network into a world model, a robot policy, or a video-action model. For action-free co-training, the action positions of unlabeled video are filled with mask tokens and excluded from the loss. Simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate two findings.

First, a single SUAVE model predicts long-horizon video and acts as a policy, competitive with dedicated world models and specialized action policies on static and dynamic manipulation tasks.

On a real robot, our model generates subgoal images and an action chunk spanning one second of motion in 1,030 ms on an RTX 5090 GPU, sustaining closed-loop control at 2.5 actions per second. Second, pretraining on robot video and co-training on human video substantially improves policy performance and zero-shot robustness to distribution shift.

Together, these results show that masked diffusion is a practical and versatile foundation for unified video-action modeling.

summary.en: The paper introduces SUAVE, a masked-diffusion transformer that represents language, video, and actions as discrete tokens in one sequence. By choosing which tokens to mask at inference, the same model can serve as a world model, robot policy, or video-action model. Simulation and real-world experiments show long-horizon video prediction and manipulation performance competitive with dedicated models. On a real robot, it generated subgoal images and a one-second action chunk in 1,030 ms on an RTX 5090. The authors also report improved policy performance and zero-shot robustness to distribution shifts from robot-video pretraining and human-video co-training.
summary.zh: 本文提出 SUAVE，一种以掩码扩散 Transformer 统一生成视频与动作的模型。语言、视频和动作均表示为离散 token；推理时选择不同的掩码位置，可将同一网络用于世界模型、机器人策略或视频动作模型。仿真与真实世界实验显示，该模型可预测长时程视频并执行操作任务，表现可与专用世界模型和动作策略竞争。真实机器人实验中，模型在 RTX 5090 上以 1,030 毫秒生成子目标图像和一秒动作片段。作者还报告，机器人视频预训练及人类视频协同训练提升了策略表现与零样本分布偏移鲁棒性。

items.title: SUAVE: Unified Video-Action Models via Masked Diffusion

items.intro: arXiv:2610.05997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Early development unfolds in caregiver-infant dyads, where infants' sensorimotor streams are shaped by physical contact and face-to-face interaction. Yet developmental robotics simulators commonly model infants in isolation, limiting the study of caregiver-mediated experience. We present a caregiver-enabled extension of the Multi-Modal Infant Model (MIMo) in MuJoCo that turns MIMo into a controllable platform for replaying dyadic interaction and generating dense infant-perspective observations. The system provides (i) an articulated caregiver model compatible with MIMo

sections.text:
Early development unfolds in caregiver-infant dyads, where infants' sensorimotor streams are shaped by physical contact and face-to-face interaction. Yet developmental robotics simulators commonly model infants in isolation, limiting the study of caregiver-mediated experience.

We present a caregiver-enabled extension of the Multi-Modal Infant Model (MIMo) in MuJoCo that turns MIMo into a controllable platform for replaying dyadic interaction and generating dense infant-perspective observations.

The system provides (i) an articulated caregiver model compatible with MIMo morphologies, parameterized from anthropometrics and optionally resized to a recorded caregiver; (ii) a workflow to replay naturalistic caregiver-infant holding and soothing interactions; and (iii) logging and visualizing the infant's first-person multimodal experience (we show touch and vision).

We showcase the tool on touch by introducing origin-aware contact logging that disambiguates self-, caregiver-, and environment-generated contact and supports aggregation into touch-rate statistics comparable to manual coding.

While we showcase tactile analysis, the platform is intended more broadly as a generator of multimodal dyadic datasets (touch and egocentric vision) for modeling the development of social interaction.

summary.en: The paper presents a caregiver-enabled extension of the Multi-Modal Infant Model in MuJoCo for replaying caregiver-infant interactions and generating infant-perspective observations. It includes an articulated caregiver model parameterized from anthropometrics, a workflow for replaying holding and soothing interactions, and tools to log and visualize touch and vision. The demonstrated tactile analysis uses origin-aware contact logs to distinguish self-generated, caregiver-generated, and environment-generated contact, supporting touch-rate statistics. The authors describe the broader platform as a generator of multimodal dyadic datasets for modeling social-interaction development.
summary.zh: 本文介绍在 MuJoCo 中扩展的多模态婴儿模型 MIMo，使其能与具身照护者共同模拟互动，并生成婴儿视角的触觉和视觉观察。系统包含可适配 MIMo 身体形态、依据人体测量参数化的照护者模型，可重放自然的抱持与安抚互动，并记录和可视化婴儿的多模态体验。作者展示了触觉分析功能：具备来源识别的接触日志可区分自我、照护者及环境接触，并支持汇总触摸率。平台更广泛的目标是生成用于研究社会互动发展的双人多模态数据集。

items.title: Infant simulator with an embodied caregiver: Generating infant-perspective touch and vision during social interaction

Radar-lidar localization combines the complementary strengths of the two sensing modalities: radar is robust to adverse weather and precipitation, while lidar provides high-fidelity 3D maps in favourable conditions. However, existing radar-lidar localization methods are restricted to planar $SE(2)$ localization and have generally fallen short of the accuracy achieved by lidar-lidar

sections.text:
This paper introduces Dr-LiSA, a first-of-its-kind direct method for localizing 2D spinning radar intensity measurements in $SE（3）$ against 3D lidar maps.

Radar-lidar localization combines the complementary strengths of the two sensing modalities: radar is robust to adverse weather and precipitation, while lidar provides high-fidelity 3D maps in favourable conditions.

However, existing radar-lidar localization methods are restricted to planar $SE（2）$ localization and have generally fallen short of the accuracy achieved by lidar-lidar and even radar-radar systems. A key challenge is the substantial sensing-modality gap between radar and lidar, which observe and represent scene structure in fundamentally different ways.

Dr-LiSA bridges this gap using a learned forward model that predicts radar measurements from a lidar submap at a candidate pose, enabling direct photometric alignment of predicted and observed radar scans in $SE（3）$.

Dr-LiSA outperforms prior radar-lidar approaches in $SE（2）$ while achieving planar accuracy competitive with state-of-the-art radar-radar localization across more than 90 km of on-road data.

summary.en: The paper introduces Dr-LiSA, a direct method for localizing 2D spinning radar intensity scans in SE(3) against 3D lidar maps. To address the difference between radar and lidar scene representations, a learned forward model predicts radar measurements from a lidar submap at a candidate pose. The method then directly aligns predicted and observed scans photometrically. The authors report that Dr-LiSA outperforms prior radar-lidar approaches in SE(2), with planar accuracy competitive with state-of-the-art radar-radar localization across more than 90 km of on-road data.
summary.zh: 本文提出 Dr-LiSA，一种将二维旋转雷达强度扫描与三维激光雷达地图直接对齐、在 SE(3) 中定位的方法。为应对雷达与激光雷达在场景表示上的差异，该方法使用学习得到的前向模型，根据候选位姿下的激光雷达子地图预测雷达测量，再对预测扫描与观测扫描进行光度对齐。作者称，Dr-LiSA 在 SE(2) 中优于既有雷达—激光雷达方法；在超过 90 公里的道路数据上，其平面定位精度与先进雷达—雷达定位方法相当。摘要未报告其 SE(3) 定位精度结果。

items.title: Dr-LiSA: Direct Radar-Lidar Scan Alignment for SE(3) Localization

sections.text:
Powered neck exoskeletons are developed to restore head-neck motions for those with neck muscle weakness. Current methods using hand-held input devices to control these robotic systems are unintuitive or non-viable for these populations. Alternatively, the eyes coordinate with the head to accomplish many daily tasks.

Therefore, movements of the eyes can be a useful signal to control the neck exoskeletons without needing to use the hands. However, previous control models lack biobehavioral basis as well as means to personalize the control behavior, causing unnatural head-neck movements.

This paper presents a novel eye-tracking controller design leveraging the vestibulo-ocular reflex to emulate natural eyehead coordination. Personalization tools were also designed, consisting of sliders to allow users to adjust the parameters of this controller. Here, we present the technical design and validation of this system in human users.

Compared to the previous eye-tracking model, the new controller provides natural head motions personalized to the user through more natural velocity profiles and a 24 percent average increase of accurate motion intent detection.

This system provides a powerful platform for studying eye-tracking controllers in the context of personalization and preference, and ultimately restoring the lost head-neck mobility in patient populations.

summary.en: The paper presents an eye-tracking controller for neck exoskeletons that uses the vestibulo-ocular reflex to model natural eye-head coordination. Sliders let users personalize controller parameters. In validation with human users, the authors report more natural velocity profiles and a 24% average increase in accurate motion-intent detection compared with a previous eye-tracking model. They describe the system as a platform for studying personalization and preference, with the longer-term aim of restoring head-neck mobility in patient populations.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种用于颈部外骨骼的眼动控制器，借鉴前庭眼反射来模拟自然的眼头协调，并提供滑块供用户个性化调整参数。作者报告，该系统在人类用户验证中，相较既有眼动模型产生更自然的速度曲线，并使准确动作意图检测平均提升24%。论文将其定位为研究个性化与偏好的平台，并提出其最终可用于帮助恢复患者头颈活动能力。

items.title: A Biomimetic Gaze Control to Restore Head-Neck Movements

sections.text:
Benchmarks expose vision-language-action (VLA) policies to few canonical instructions, while exhaustive deployment testing is impossible.

We introduce Object-Grounded Attention Monitoring (OGAM), connecting systematic testing to runtime assurance: testing reveals attention divergence between successful and failed executions, and OGAM uses this signal to stop failures beyond the finite suite.

We generate scene-grounded instructions through pairwise combinations of action templates and objects, and separately test meaning-preserving paraphrases.

All 87 out-of-benchmark cases reveal problematic behavior across OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, UniVLA, and $\pi_{0.5}$: none completes any of the 24 feasible instructions, while infeasible or hazardous requests also trigger behavior substitution.

At each action query, we project gradient-weighted visual attention through object masks and group it by instruction role for comparison across tasks and policies.

Dynamic time warping aligns this course with a successful reference despite speed differences; conformal calibration on successful episodes sets the early-stopping threshold for sustained deviations, with a nominal false-stop target of $\alpha=0.05$.

Across four policies, OGAM stops 87-100% of failed episodes at median times of 5-12s within a 20s budget, with observed false-stop rates of 3-5%, without failure-labeled training. Finite testing thus identifies attention patterns that support online intervention before failure fully unfolds.

summary.en: The paper introduces Object-Grounded Attention Monitoring (OGAM), which uses attention differences between successful and failed executions in finite testing to intervene at runtime. It groups gradient-weighted visual attention by instruction role, aligns it with a successful reference using dynamic time warping, and calibrates an early-stopping threshold on successful episodes. Across four VLA policies, the authors report stopping 87–100% of failed episodes within a 20-second budget, with median times of 5–12 seconds and observed false-stop rates of 3–5%, without failure-labeled training.
summary.zh: 论文提出物体接地注意力监测方法OGAM，将有限场景测试中成功与失败执行的注意力差异用于运行时干预。方法按指令角色汇总经物体掩码投影的梯度加权视觉注意力，用动态时间规整与成功参考对齐，并依据成功回合校准提前停止阈值。在四种VLA策略上，作者报告OGAM在20秒预算内停止87%至100%的失败回合，中位停止时间为5至12秒，观测误停率为3%至5%，且无需失败标注训练。

items.title: OGAM: Connecting Systematic Testing to Runtime Assurance through Object-Grounded Attention Monitoring for VLA Policies

sections.text:
Long-horizon planning with latent world models requires reasoning across timescales and levels of abstraction. Existing task-agnostic JEPA world models predict and plan at a single timescale or with multiple horizons in one shared latent space.

We introduce H-JEPA, an end-to-end recipe for training a hierarchy of action-conditioned JEPAs in which each level predicts farther ahead in its own learned latent space. Planning proceeds top-down: the top level optimizes progress toward the goal, and each level's predictions become subgoals for the planner below it.

When factors in the data evolve at separated timescales, higher levels discard fast, unpredictable detail and retain slower task-relevant state. Across four simulated navigation and manipulation environments, hierarchical planning improves over a flat JEPA; on Visual AntMaze, a three-level hierarchy raises success from 18% to 73% using less planner compute.

Ablations attribute these gains to both temporal decomposition and higher-level goal representations. With inverse-dynamics supervision, the approach extends to diverse real-robot videos from DROID, where hierarchy improves offline planning fidelity at lower planner compute.

summary.en: The paper presents H-JEPA, an end-to-end method for training hierarchical, action-conditioned JEPA world models. Each level predicts farther ahead in its own learned latent space, and planning proceeds top-down, turning higher-level predictions into subgoals for lower levels. In four simulated navigation and manipulation environments, hierarchical planning outperforms a flat JEPA. On Visual AntMaze, success rises from 18% to 73% with less planner compute. With inverse-dynamics supervision, the method also improves offline planning fidelity on real-robot DROID videos at lower planner compute.
summary.zh: 论文提出H-JEPA，一种端到端训练分层、动作条件化JEPA世界模型的方法，各层在各自学习的潜在空间预测不同时间跨度，规划则自顶向下将高层预测转为低层子目标。在四种仿真导航与操作环境中，分层规划优于平坦JEPA；Visual AntMaze成功率从18%升至73%，且规划计算量更低。消融实验将收益归因于时间分解和高层目标表征。结合逆动力学监督后，该方法在DROID真实机器人视频上提升离线规划保真度并降低规划计算量。

items.title: H-JEPA: End-to-End Learning of Hierarchical World Models for Visual Planning

items.intro: arXiv:2610.05639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous robots operating over long periods must keep their environmental memory up to date as the world changes between visits. In semi-static environments, an object may be replaced in place by a different but geometrically and semantically similar instance, making the identity change difficult to detect from geometry or coarse semantics alone. We present FOCUS, an uncertainty-aware framework for object-level change detection and map maintenance. We formulate semi-static memory maintenance as probabilistic inference

sections.text:
Autonomous robots operating over long periods must keep their environmental memory up to date as the world changes between visits. In semi-static environments, an object may be replaced in place by a different but geometrically and semantically similar instance, making the identity change difficult to detect from geometry or coarse semantics alone.

We present FOCUS, an uncertainty-aware framework for object-level change detection and map maintenance. We formulate semi-static memory maintenance as probabilistic inference that fuses geometric likelihood with appearance likelihood rendered from a 3D Gaussian map.

A recursive three-state estimator maintains whether each mapped object is PERSISTED, REPLACED, or REMOVED.

To account for imperfect 3DGS rendering, we model the rendered appearance evidence probabilistically rather than using it as a direct change score, with the model parameters automatically calibrated from a change-free replay of the initial mapping session.

We evaluate our method on a new Isaac Sim warehouse benchmark with ambiguous in-place replacements and on the real-world TorWIC dataset. It improves object-level replacement F1 from 0.20 to 0.84 over a probabilistic baseline and transfers to real-world data without manual parameter retuning.

summary.en: The paper presents FOCUS, a framework for object-level change detection and map maintenance in semi-static environments. It uses probabilistic inference to combine geometric likelihood with appearance likelihood rendered from a 3D Gaussian map, and a recursive three-state estimator labels objects as persisted, replaced, or removed. Appearance evidence is modeled probabilistically to account for imperfect rendering, with parameters calibrated from a change-free replay of the initial mapping session. On an Isaac Sim warehouse benchmark and the real-world TorWIC dataset, the authors report replacement F1 improving from 0.20 to 0.84 over a probabilistic baseline, with transfer to real data without manual retuning.
summary.zh: 论文提出FOCUS，用于半静态环境中的物体级变化检测与地图维护。该框架以概率推断融合几何似然和由3D高斯地图渲染的外观似然，并通过递归三状态估计器标记物体为持续存在、被替换或已移除。为应对渲染不完美，外观证据按概率建模，参数由初次建图阶段无变化的回放自动校准。在Isaac Sim仓库基准和真实TorWIC数据集上的评估中，作者报告替换F1由概率基线的0.20提升至0.84，并迁移至真实数据而无需人工重新调参。

items.title: FOCUS: Fine-Grained Open-Vocabulary Change Detection for Uncertainty-Aware Semi-Static Scenes

Deterministic nonlinear MPC can explicitly incorporate constraints, but its real-time safety and performance depends strongly

sections.text:
Safe robot control often requires combining long-horizon performance optimization with hard state and input constraints, but existing approaches tend to address this tradeoff partially.

Sampling-based model predictive control (MPC) methods such as model predictive path integral (MPPI) are effective in handling nonlinear and nonconvex environments, yet their finite-sample rollouts and unconstrained weighted-average update can return an unsafe control.

Deterministic nonlinear MPC can explicitly incorporate constraints, but its real-time safety and performance depends strongly on warm starts and local convergence. Hamilton--Jacobi reachability (HJR) provides rigorous safety certificates, but offline value-function computation remains practical only for reduced-order models.

We propose ReSQ-MPPI, a reachability-informed generation--refinement architecture that combines these complementary strengths. An HJR value function computed offline for a reduced-order model guides online MPPI sampling toward safe, promising trajectory candidates.

The MPPI solution is then refined by a small number of sequential quadratic programming (SQP) iterations in a full-order MPC problem.

A key observation is that the standard MPPI inference step is an unconstrained weighted least-squares problem; ReSQ-MPPI replaces it with a constrained MPC refinement that recovers the MPPI update when it is feasible and minimally modifies it otherwise.

Simulations in cluttered navigation and autonomous racing environments demonstrate that ReSQ-MPPI improves safety and performance over standalone MPPI, MPC, and reachability-filtered sampling-based control baselines.

summary.en: The paper proposes ReSQ-MPPI, a generation-and-refinement architecture for safe nonlinear predictive control. An offline Hamilton–Jacobi reachability value function for a reduced-order model guides online MPPI sampling, and a few sequential quadratic programming iterations refine the candidate in a full-order MPC problem. The constrained refinement recovers the MPPI update when feasible and minimally modifies it otherwise. Simulations in cluttered navigation and autonomous racing show improved safety and performance over the reported baselines.
summary.zh: 论文提出 ReSQ-MPPI，一种面向安全非线性预测控制的生成与细化架构。它使用针对降阶模型离线计算的 Hamilton–Jacobi 可达性价值函数，引导在线 MPPI 采样，再通过全阶模型预测控制中的少量序列二次规划迭代细化结果。约束细化在可行时恢复 MPPI 更新，否则尽量小幅修改。拥挤导航和自动赛车仿真显示，该方法相较文中所列基线提升了安全性和性能。

items.title: Reachability-Guided Sequential Quadratic Programming-Guarded Model Predictive Path Integral for Safe Nonlinear Predictive Control

How far these native capabilities support embodied generalism across diverse tasks remains unclear. The arena contains 1,000 cases drawn from 32 established sources and GeoProbe, our new benchmark for geometric estimation on Blender renders and real-scene images. A minimal harness

sections.text:
Frontier vision-language models (VLMs) increasingly estimate scenes, ground interactions, and generate executable actions. How far these native capabilities support embodied generalism across diverse tasks remains unclear.

We introduce Embodied Agent Arena to assess seven VLM agents across Geometry, Spatial Reasoning, Affordance, Task Planning, and Manipulation. The arena contains 1,000 cases drawn from 32 established sources and GeoProbe, our new benchmark for geometric estimation on Blender renders and real-scene images.

A minimal harness preserves source observations and operations while leaving perception, reasoning, and action selection to the model. Separate measures of metric precision, functional grounding, and native goal completion connect local competence to complete task outcomes.

Astra's strengths in precise estimation and usable-contact localization coexist with endpoint errors in tracing and low household-task completion. Supplementary comparisons of richer observations and multi-round review show model- and task-dependent effects.

Current VLM agents thus fall short of embodied generalism: they often make partial progress without satisfying all task goals within allotted time and interaction budgets.

summary.en: The paper introduces Embodied Agent Arena to evaluate seven vision-language model agents on geometry, spatial reasoning, affordance, task planning, and manipulation. Its cases draw on established sources and GeoProbe, a benchmark for geometric estimation using Blender renders and real-scene images. Evaluation separates metric precision, functional grounding, and native goal completion. The authors report that current agents often make partial progress but fail to satisfy all goals within allotted time and interaction budgets, and conclude that they fall short of embodied generalism.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 Embodied Agent Arena，用于评估七种视觉语言模型智能体在几何、空间推理、可供性、任务规划和操作方面的表现。测试集含来自既有来源及 GeoProbe 基准的案例，后者涵盖 Blender 渲染图和真实场景图像中的几何估计。评估分别考察度量精度、功能性接地和原生目标完成。作者报告，当前智能体常能取得部分进展，却未能在规定时间和交互预算内完成全部目标，因此尚未达到具身通用能力。

items.title: Are Frontier VLM Agents Ready to Be Robot Generalists? An Empirical Study with the Embodied Agent Arena

sections.text:
The enduring vision of general-purpose robots serving humanity hinges fundamentally on policy steerability. However, prevailing paradigms of learning from expert demonstrations demand massive real-world data even on simplified grippers, rendering them prohibitively expensive for high-dimensional, data-scarce dexterous hands.

To overcome this bottleneck, we present a full-stack system that scales dexterous VLA pre-training from egocentric human videos and enables data-efficient real-robot post-training.

It integrates EgoSmith, a data pipeline that curates in-the-wild egocentric videos into 9,606 hours of pre-training data with 8.3x higher throughput and better accuracy than prior SOTA; a unified Robot Stack for teleoperation and human-in-the-loop correction tailored for dexterous hands; and EgoSteer, a world-model-enhanced VLA operating on a morphology-aligned action space.

Human data pre-training equips EgoSteer with language-guided manipulation priors, which are grounded through robot post-training and further refined via DAgger. Empirically, EgoSteer robustly executes free-form instructions across 45 diverse tasks, demonstrating adherence to user intent amid multiple candidate tasks and generalization.

The pre-trained model also few-shot adapts to five complex long-horizon tasks, including box folding, on two embodiments with 79% average progress. All system code, datasets, model checkpoints, and an evaluation gallery are publicly available at https://egosteer.github.io/.

summary.en: The paper presents EgoSteer, a full-stack system for dexterous manipulation that pre-trains on egocentric human videos and supports data-efficient real-robot post-training. It combines a video curation pipeline, a robot stack for dexterous-hand teleoperation and human-in-the-loop correction, and a world-model-enhanced vision-language-action model with a morphology-aligned action space. The authors report execution of free-form instructions across 45 tasks and few-shot adaptation to five complex long-horizon tasks on two embodiments, with 79% average progress.
summary.zh: 论文提出 EgoSteer，一个利用第一人称人类视频进行灵巧操作预训练、并支持真实机器人高效后训练的全栈系统。系统包含视频数据整理流程、面向灵巧手遥操作和人在环纠正的机器人平台，以及采用形态对齐动作空间的世界模型增强型视觉语言动作模型。作者报告，该系统能在 45 项多样任务中执行自由形式指令，并能在两种机器人形态上对五项复杂长时程任务进行少样本适配，平均进度为 79%。

items.title: EgoSteer: An Open-Source Full-Stack System Towards Steerable Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos

sections.text:
Inter-robot communication is a key enabling technology in cooperative robotics applications.

While wireless communication is ubiquitous, simple, and effective, it has inherent limitations: the receiving robot cannot easily localise the source of an incoming signal, clock synchronisation is challenging, and signals are broadcast to all nearby devices rather than targeted recipients.

Optical communication provides a complementary channel that is inherently directional and spatially localised, directly addressing these limitations.

Event cameras are bio-inspired dynamic vision sensors that respond to changes in image intensity with high temporal resolution, high dynamic range, and low latency, making them well-suited as receivers for high-rate optical communication in cooperative robotic systems.

In this paper, we propose the Asynchronous Tracking and Optical Communication (ATOC) system, which integrates LED smart-beacon modulation, event-based detection, optical tracking, and event-data demodulation in a single pipeline.

By simultaneously tracking and demodulating multiple LED smart beacons, ATOC transforms a conventional visual marker into a robust communication channel suitable for a wide range of high-impact robotics applications. We validate ATOC in a suite of laboratory studies and two 'applications': a smart-city demonstration and a 3D motion-capture system.

summary.en: The paper proposes ATOC, an Asynchronous Tracking and Optical Communication system that combines LED smart-beacon modulation, event-based detection, optical tracking, and event-data demodulation in one pipeline. The authors describe optical communication as a directional, spatially localized complement to wireless communication, addressing challenges in source localization, clock synchronization, and targeted reception. ATOC tracks and demodulates multiple LED beacons simultaneously. The system is validated in laboratory studies, a smart-city demonstration, and a 3D motion-capture application.
summary.zh: 论文提出异步跟踪与光学通信系统 ATOC，将 LED 智能信标调制、事件相机检测、光学跟踪和事件数据解调整合进单一流程。作者指出，光学通信可提供方向性和空间定位特征，补充无线通信在信号源定位、时钟同步及定向接收方面的局限。ATOC 可同时跟踪并解调多个 LED 信标。实验室研究以及智慧城市演示和三维动作捕捉应用验证了该系统；摘要未说明超出这些验证场景的结果。

items.title: Asynchronous Tracking, Optical Communication and 3D Motion Capture using Event-based Sensors

sections.text:
Visual imitation policies must learn which image regions matter for action, whether applying the same operation to different objects or selecting a language-specified target. We introduce ResCue (Residual Spatial Cueing), which converts language-derived target information into a spatial condition for visual policy learning.

Pretrained grounding produces a target mask; an independent cue encoder adds its features to spatial RGB features before further visual processing and pooling. This retains scene context while making the target explicit.

With Diffusion Policy (DP), ResCue achieves 56.5% average success across 15 simulated tasks, versus 33.1% for DP and 40.% for the strongest baseline, $\pi_0$, with gains in both ordinary manipulation and instruction-dependent object selection. On three real-world bimanual tasks, it reaches 60.0%, compared with 31.7% for $\pi_0$.

Matched-mask ablations favor residual fusion over input-level and pooled alternatives, while test-time interventions show that target-correct guidance matters for execution.

summary.en: The paper introduces ResCue, which turns language-specified target information into a spatial condition. A pretrained grounding model produces a target mask, and an independent cue encoder adds its features to spatial RGB features before further processing and pooling, preserving scene context while making the target explicit. With Diffusion Policy, the authors report a 56.5% average success rate across 15 simulated tasks and higher success on three real-world bimanual tasks than the compared baseline. Ablations favor residual fusion, and test-time interventions indicate that target-correct guidance matters.
summary.zh: 论文提出 ResCue，将语言指定的目标信息转化为空间条件：预训练定位模型生成目标掩码，独立提示编码器将其特征加到空间 RGB 特征中，再进行视觉处理与池化，以保留场景上下文并突出目标。使用 Diffusion Policy 时，作者报告其在 15 项仿真任务上平均成功率为 56.5%，高于所比较的基线；在三项真实世界双臂任务上也报告了更高成功率。消融比较支持残差融合优于输入级和池化替代方案，测试时干预则显示目标正确的引导对执行很重要。

items.title: ResCue: Residual Spatial Cueing for Language-Conditioned Imitation Learning

To address this limitation, we introduce a tracker-guided self-training framework that

sections.text:
Efficient and robust tracking of surgical robotic instruments is important for robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery, yet remains challenging due to the complexity of surgical scenes and the unconventional geometry of surgical instruments. Keypoint-based approaches are efficient, but their performance depends on reliable feature detection.

Improving these detectors with real-world supervision is difficult because accurate real-world annotations are costly to obtain at scale. To address this limitation, we introduce a tracker-guided self-training framework that adapts a model pretrained on synthetic images to unlabeled real-world videos.

Given measured robot joint states, an uncertainty-aware EKF recursively corrects the instrument pose and the observable joint angles by comparing projected model features with detected keypoints, shaft boundaries, and mask-derived cues.

An RTS smoother subsequently refines the resulting trajectory, which is projected into pseudo-labels for fine-tuning the feature detector without laborious pose annotations.

Experiments on real-world videos demonstrate consistent improvements from self-training across all evaluated keypoint metrics, and the resulting model outperforms prior approaches in both accuracy and runtime. The code and data will be released upon publication.

summary.en: The paper presents a tracker-guided self-training framework that adapts a model pretrained on synthetic images to unlabeled real-world videos, reducing the need for costly pose annotations. Using measured robot joint states, an uncertainty-aware EKF recursively corrects instrument pose and observable joint angles by comparing projected model features with detected keypoints, shaft boundaries, and mask cues. An RTS smoother refines the trajectory, which is projected into pseudo-labels for detector fine-tuning. Experiments on real-world videos show consistent self-training gains across evaluated keypoint metrics, with the resulting model outperforming prior approaches in accuracy and runtime.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种由跟踪器引导的自训练框架，将在合成图像上预训练的模型适配到无标注真实视频，以减少获取真实姿态标注的需求。方法利用机器人关节状态，通过不确定性感知 EKF 比较投影模型特征与检测到的关键点、器械轴边界及掩码线索，递归校正器械姿态和可观测关节角；随后用 RTS 平滑器细化轨迹，并投影为伪标签以微调特征检测器。作者报告，真实视频实验中自训练在所有评估关键点指标上均带来稳定提升，所得模型在准确率和运行时间上优于先前方法。

items.title: Robust Surgical Robotic Instrument Tracking via Sequential Multi-Cue Fusion and Sim-to-Real Self-Training

However, physical deployment can deviate from nominal assumptions, and additional disturbances may arise even when the model itself is accurate. sections.text:
Robotic controllers increasingly rely on analytical models, simulators, cost-query interfaces, and learned world models. However, physical deployment can deviate from nominal assumptions, and additional disturbances may arise even when the model itself is accurate.

In control systems, disturbance observers (DOB) are widely used to estimate such unmeasured effects from nominal models and measured feedback. Classical DOB formulations are generally built around explicit plant models.

This paper develops the sampling-based disturbance observer (SDOB), extending the DOB principle to a broader range of models, including simulators and learned world models, through state-rollout or cost-query interfaces.

SDOB separates two observable channels: state-effect disturbances, for which the feedback state differs from its prediction, and cost disturbances, for which the same query state receives different costs as the perceived environment changes.

Diverse simulation and real-robot experiments across traditional and learned models demonstrate the effectiveness of SDOB in compensating for sim-to-real mismatch and improving control performance.

summary.en: The paper develops the sampling-based disturbance observer (SDOB), extending the disturbance-observer principle to models such as simulators and learned world models that provide state-rollout or cost-query interfaces. It distinguishes state-effect disturbances, where feedback differs from predicted state, from cost disturbances, where the same query state receives different costs as the perceived environment changes. The authors note that physical deployment can introduce disturbances even when a model is accurate. Diverse simulation and real-robot experiments across traditional and learned models demonstrate SDOB’s effectiveness in compensating for sim-to-real mismatch and improving control performance.
summary.zh: 论文提出采样式扰动观测器 SDOB，将传统扰动观测器原理扩展到仿真器和学习式世界模型等可通过状态滚动或成本查询访问的模型。SDOB 区分两类可观测通道：状态效应扰动表现为反馈状态与预测状态不同；成本扰动表现为环境感知变化时，同一查询状态得到不同成本。作者指出，物理部署可能偏离名义假设，即使模型本身准确也会出现额外扰动。传统 DOB 通常依赖显式对象模型；论文报告了在传统与学习模型上的多种仿真和真实机器人实验，显示该方法可补偿仿真到现实的偏差并改善控制性能。

items.title: Tackling Sim-to-Real Mismatch Through Sampling-Based Disturbance Observers: From Analytical Models to Learned World Models

As episodes grow longer, however, retaining the full history becomes increasingly costly, creating a fundamental scalability challenge for memory-augmented policies. sections.text:
Memory is essential for long-horizon robotic manipulation, where successful actions may depend on past events that are no longer recoverable from the current observation. As episodes grow longer, however, retaining the full history becomes increasingly costly, creating a fundamental scalability challenge for memory-augmented policies.

Existing approaches address this challenge by either storing selected past observations in a bounded memory bank or compressing interaction history into a fixed-size parametric state through Test-Time Training (TTT).

Yet these formulations do not explicitly distinguish between historical information that can already be recovered from the policy's current context and information that must persist beyond it.

We introduce TTT-RM, which repurposes TTT as Residual Memory, using fast weights not to generically compress history but to complement a bounded memory bank by preserving task-relevant historical information that cannot be recovered from the policy's current context.

Concretely, TTT-RM learns a history decoder that reconstructs historical representations from the current observation and retrieved memory. The resulting reconstruction residual captures what this context fails to explain and serves as the learning target for TTT.

The TTT slow weights are optimized against this residual target so that online fast-weight updates learn to encode complementary historical information over time. The fast-weight state is then queried to produce a residual memory representation that conditions action generation.

Extensive experiments on memory-intensive simulation benchmarks and real-world tasks show that TTT-RM consistently improves across multiple memory designs, outperforms diverse baselines, and supports sustained execution on a three-minute, eight-stage stowing task.

summary.en: The paper proposes TTT-RM, using test-time training as residual memory to complement a bounded memory bank with task-relevant history that cannot be recovered from current context. A history decoder reconstructs historical representations from the current observation and retrieved memory; the reconstruction residual becomes the TTT learning target. Online fast weights then encode complementary historical information and produce a residual memory representation for conditioning actions. The authors report consistent improvements across memory-intensive simulation benchmarks and real-world tasks, gains over diverse baselines, and sustained execution on a three-minute, eight-stage stowing task.
summary.zh: 论文提出 TTT-RM，将测试时训练用作残差记忆，以补充有界记忆库中无法从当前上下文恢复的任务相关历史信息。方法训练历史解码器，根据当前观测和检索到的记忆重建历史表示，并以重建残差作为 TTT 的学习目标；在线快速权重由此编码互补历史信息，生成用于动作条件化的残差记忆表示。作者报告，该方法在依赖记忆的仿真基准和真实任务中持续改善表现，优于多种基线，并支持在一项三分钟、八阶段的收纳任务中持续执行。

items.title: Test-Time Training as Residual Memory for Robot Policies

items.intro: arXiv:2610.05180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning dexterous manipulation benefits from human demonstration datasets that capture diverse and natural hand-object interactions. In particular, contact points and forces provide supervision on where and how strongly to interact, which cannot be fully captured by motion trajectories alone. However, methods for jointly capturing hand and object motion, contact points, and forces remain limited. Moreover, severe occlusion from hand-object interaction challenges accurate tracking of both hands and objects. To address these limitations, we

sections.text:
Learning dexterous manipulation benefits from human demonstration datasets that capture diverse and natural hand-object interactions. In particular, contact points and forces provide supervision on where and how strongly to interact, which cannot be fully captured by motion trajectories alone.

However, methods for jointly capturing hand and object motion, contact points, and forces remain limited. Moreover, severe occlusion from hand-object interaction challenges accurate tracking of both hands and objects. To address these limitations, we present a Visual-Inertial-CONtact based hand-object tracking (VICON) framework.

It holistically captures both hand and object motion along with contact information during manipulation, even under severe occlusion. First, we adopt a visual-inertial glove and an RGB-D camera for accurate hand tracking, and redesign the glove to incorporate contact sensing.

Specifically, force-sensitive resistors (FSRs) are placed on the glove based on human grasp frequency to synchronously record contact states and calibrated normal forces. Second, without requiring pre-existing CAD models, we estimate object poses using RGB-D images and a mesh reconstructed from a monocular video.

We propose factor-graph-based object trajectory estimation that fuses object-pose estimates weighted by visibility under hand-object occlusion, FSR measurements, and a hand-motion prior.

Across 40 motion-capture sessions with five objects, VICON achieves a 2.5% failed-frame rate compared with 50.9-64.6% for the baselines, with median errors of 3.9 mm and 3.0 degrees under occlusion.

Using VICON, we construct a dataset containing synchronized hand-object motion, contact points, and normal forces, and will publicly release an expanded dataset covering 10 object categories at https://github.com/VICON-dataset/dataset.

summary.en: The paper presents VICON, a hand-object tracking framework designed to capture motion, contact points, and normal forces during manipulation, including under severe occlusion. It combines a visual-inertial glove, an RGB-D camera, glove-mounted force sensors, and object pose estimates based on RGB-D images and a mesh reconstructed from monocular video, without requiring existing CAD models. A factor graph fuses visibility-weighted pose estimates, sensor measurements, and a hand-motion prior. The authors report results from motion-capture sessions involving five objects and describe a synchronized dataset.
summary.zh: 论文提出 VICON，一种用于操作数据集的手部与物体跟踪框架，旨在严重遮挡下同步捕获手物运动、接触点和法向力。系统结合视觉惯性手套、RGB-D 相机及基于抓握频率布置的力敏电阻，并通过单目视频重建网格估计物体位姿，无需已有 CAD 模型。因子图融合按可见度加权的位姿估计、传感器测量和手部运动先验。作者报告，在 40 次、涉及五种物体的动捕会话中，失败帧率及遮挡条件下的中位误差优于基线，并据此构建同步数据集。

items.title: VICON: Visual-Inertial-Contact based Hand-Object Tracking for Manipulation Datasets

However, completing the joint video-action denoising process at each replanning cycle incurs substantial latency, delaying action updates and limiting closed-loop responsiveness. We present Rolling-WAM, a formulation that distributes joint denoising across successive replanning cycles. Our method maintains a sliding window of video-action chunks at staggered noise levels. At each step, a rolling noise schedule fully denoises the imminent action

sections.text:
World Action Models (WAMs) couple action generation with future visual prediction for robotic manipulation. However, completing the joint video-action denoising process at each replanning cycle incurs substantial latency, delaying action updates and limiting closed-loop responsiveness.

We present Rolling-WAM, a formulation that distributes joint denoising across successive replanning cycles. Our method maintains a sliding window of video-action chunks at staggered noise levels. At each step, a rolling noise schedule fully denoises the imminent action chunk for execution, while partially refining farther-future chunks.

As the window advances with new camera observations, the retained future chunks continue their denoising process. This distributes the computational cost over time while carrying an evolving visual-action context across chunk boundaries.

Evaluations on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and a real-world Unitree G1 humanoid show that Rolling-WAM achieves competitive manipulation performance. By removing the need to denoise the entire prediction horizon from scratch, it delivers a 4.5x steady-state replanning speedup over standard joint WAMs.

summary.en: Rolling-WAM distributes joint video-action denoising across successive replanning cycles to reduce the latency of denoising an entire prediction horizon anew at every cycle. It maintains a sliding window of chunks at staggered noise levels: the imminent action chunk is fully denoised for execution, while farther-future chunks are partially refined. As new camera observations arrive, retained chunks continue to be refined. Evaluations on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and a real Unitree G1 humanoid show competitive manipulation performance and a reported 4.5-fold steady-state replanning speedup over standard joint WAMs.
summary.zh: 论文提出 Rolling-WAM，通过在连续重规划周期中分配联合视频与动作去噪，降低每轮从头完成整个预测时域去噪造成的延迟。方法维护处于不同噪声水平的滑动窗口：当前动作片段被完全去噪以供执行，较远未来片段则逐步细化；窗口随新相机观测推进，并保留片段间演进的视觉动作上下文。作者在 LIBERO、RoboTwin 和 Unitree G1 实机上评估，报告其操作表现具有竞争力，稳态重规划速度较标准联合 WAM 提升 4.5 倍。

items.title: Rolling-WAM: World Action Models with Rolling Imagination

This paper investigates the dependence of maneuver performance and odometric error on approach speed for a differential-drive robot. A footprint-clearance analysis and a normalized wheel-motion index provide a kinematic description of five braking and turning maneuvers. The principal experiment comprises 540 block-randomized trials on tile, of which 539 are retained, at commanded approach speeds of 45

sections.text:
Emergency obstacle avoidance requires a mobile robot to brake or change its heading within the available distance. This paper investigates the dependence of maneuver performance and odometric error on approach speed for a differential-drive robot.

A footprint-clearance analysis and a normalized wheel-motion index provide a kinematic description of five braking and turning maneuvers. The principal experiment comprises 540 block-randomized trials on tile, of which 539 are retained, at commanded approach speeds of 45, 55, and 65 cm/s. An overhead camera provides an independent pose reference.

When encoder, gyro, and camera heading changes are evaluated over complete motion records, the mean encoder discrepancy increases by 4.7-5.1 degrees for the two reverse-spin maneuvers between the lowest and highest speeds; the arc and brake-assisted pivot change by less than 0.4 degrees.

Larger encoder discrepancy is associated with lower avoidance success after adjustment for distance, speed, maneuver, day, and turn direction. Gyro discrepancies remain approximately 3 degrees for the reverse spins. Estimated reaction distances for 90% success and their uncertainty quantify the maneuver trade-offs.

The results support speed-specific empirical characterization of emergency maneuvers and distinguish encoder error from recovery motion and measurement-window mismatch.

summary.en: This paper studies how approach speed relates to emergency avoidance performance and odometric error in a differential-drive robot. It describes five braking and turning maneuvers using footprint clearance and a normalized wheel-motion index. The main experiment retained 539 randomized trials on tile at commanded speeds of 45, 55, and 65 cm/s, with an overhead camera as an independent pose reference. Encoder discrepancies increased with speed for two reverse-spin maneuvers but changed little for the arc and brake-assisted pivot. Larger discrepancies were associated with lower avoidance success after adjustment for specified factors.
summary.zh: 论文研究差速移动机器人在不同接近速度下的紧急避障表现与里程计误差，并以占地间隙分析和归一化轮运动指标描述五种制动、转向动作。主要实验在瓷砖地面进行，共保留 539 次随机区组试验，速度为 45、55 和 65 cm/s，并用俯视相机提供独立位姿参考。完整运动记录显示，两种反向旋转动作的编码器角度差异随速度增加，而弧线和制动辅助枢转变化较小；较大编码器差异与较低避障成功率相关。作者据此支持按速度进行经验表征，并区分编码器误差、恢复运动和测量窗口不匹配。

items.title: Emergency Obstacle Avoidance Maneuvers in Differential-Drive Mobile Robots

items.intro: arXiv:2610.04364v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Designing effective reward functions in RL typically requires substantial expertise and trial and error. Recent work automates this process with LLM-based systems that generate and iteratively improve reward code using policy feedback. However, these methods are often hard to compare because they differ in implementation details, feedback assumptions, and evaluation environments. To address this, we introduce a Benchmark for Iterative Reward Design (BIRD) that expresses existing methods in a unified configuration and evaluation

sections.text:
Designing effective reward functions in RL typically requires substantial expertise and trial and error. Recent work automates this process with LLM-based systems that generate and iteratively improve reward code using policy feedback.

However, these methods are often hard to compare because they differ in implementation details, feedback assumptions, and evaluation environments. To address this, we introduce a Benchmark for Iterative Reward Design (BIRD) that expresses existing methods in a unified configuration and evaluation space.

This lets us compare algorithms directly, ablate individual design choices, and prototype new components under matched feedback conditions and policy-training budgets. Across MuJoCo, Meta-World, Assistax, and HumanoidBench, we identify a small set of simple design choices that consistently improve performance.

Combining these choices yields significantly better performance than the evaluated methods from prior work. Our results highlight the strength of simple baselines and motivate further study of when additional algorithmic complexity improves iterative reward design. Code is available at https://github.com/safety-research/bird.

summary.en: The paper introduces BIRD, a benchmark that places iterative reward-design methods in a unified configuration and evaluation space. These methods use policy feedback to generate and improve reward code, but differences in implementation, feedback assumptions, and environments make comparisons difficult. BIRD supports direct comparisons, ablations, and component prototyping under matched feedback conditions and policy-training budgets. Across MuJoCo, Meta-World, Assistax, and HumanoidBench, the authors report that a small set of simple design choices consistently improves performance, and that combining them outperforms the evaluated prior methods.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 BIRD 基准，用统一的配置与评估空间比较基于大语言模型的迭代奖励设计方法。这些方法通过策略反馈生成并改进强化学习奖励代码，但实现细节、反馈假设和评测环境差异使比较困难。BIRD 支持在匹配的反馈条件和策略训练预算下直接比较算法、消融设计选择及试验新组件。作者在 MuJoCo、Meta-World、Assistax 和 HumanoidBench 上发现，一组简单设计选择能稳定提升表现；组合这些选择后，结果显著优于所评估的既有方法，并强调简单基线的价值。

items.title: A Bird's-Eye View of Iterative Reward Design

items.intro: arXiv:2610.05230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most vision-language-action models represent future motion as fixed-rate action chunks, tying temporal resolution and prediction horizon to a fixed output budget. This pointwise representation wastes capacity on highly correlated neighboring actions, leaves temporal continuity and smoothness to be learned implicitly, and forces a tradeoff between long-horizon coverage and the local precision required for contact-rich manipulation. To address these limitations, we introduce Vela, a vision-language-action foundation model that represents future robot behavior as continuous

sections.text:
Most vision-language-action models represent future motion as fixed-rate action chunks, tying temporal resolution and prediction horizon to a fixed output budget.

This pointwise representation wastes capacity on highly correlated neighboring actions, leaves temporal continuity and smoothness to be learned implicitly, and forces a tradeoff between long-horizon coverage and the local precision required for contact-rich manipulation.

To address these limitations, we introduce Vela, a vision-language-action foundation model that represents future robot behavior as continuous trajectories.

Vela combines a compact spline-based action representation with motion-dependent temporal support and a shared action interface for heterogeneous embodiments, allowing a fixed output budget to adapt its temporal resolution across motions.

We pretrain Vela on large-scale multi-embodiment robot data and evaluate it on LIBERO-X, EBench, and two real-world long-horizon tasks, egg-cake cooking and potato shredding, obtaining promising results across simulation and physical manipulation.

These results highlight the potential of continuous action representations as a foundation for future embodied foundation models. Project page and more results: https://clementine24.github.io/Vela/ .

summary.en: The paper introduces Vela, a vision-language-action foundation model that represents future robot behavior as continuous trajectories. It combines compact spline-based actions, motion-dependent temporal support, and a shared interface for heterogeneous embodiments so a fixed output budget can vary temporal resolution across motions. The authors pretrain on multi-embodiment robot data and report promising results in simulation and physical manipulation on LIBERO-X, EBench, and two real-world long-horizon tasks: egg-cake cooking and potato shredding.
summary.zh: 论文提出 Vela，一种将机器人未来行为表示为连续轨迹的视觉—语言—动作基础模型。它结合紧凑的样条动作表示、依运动变化的时间支撑，以及面向异构具身的共享动作接口，使固定输出预算能够随运动调整时间分辨率。作者使用多具身机器人数据预训练，并在 LIBERO-X、EBench 和两个真实世界长时任务（鸡蛋糕烹制、土豆切丝）中评估，报告了仿真与实体操作中的有希望结果。

items.title: Vela: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with Adaptive Action Curve Parametrization

Each robot uses local force measurements, a preassigned force weight, and a locally expressed desired transport direction, without requiring an object model, contact locations, a CoM estimate, or moment arm magnitudes online. DNPush regulates nonparallel force magnitudes from local force direction misalignments through a reciprocal-sine law. Under the stated contact conditions, Lyapunov analysis with LaSalle's invariance

sections.text:
This letter proposes DNPush, a Distributed Nonparallel Pushing force controller for cooperative object transport without inter-robot communication.

Each robot uses local force measurements, a preassigned force weight, and a locally expressed desired transport direction, without requiring an object model, contact locations, a CoM estimate, or moment arm magnitudes online. DNPush regulates nonparallel force magnitudes from local force direction misalignments through a reciprocal-sine law.

Under the stated contact conditions, Lyapunov analysis with LaSalle's invariance principle proves convergence to a unique rotational equilibrium, where perpendicular force contributions cancel and the net torque from normal forces is zero. Object velocity converges to the desired transport direction, and suitable contact regions exist for convex polygons.

Simulations isolate the reciprocal-sine scaling mechanism, five-robot coordination, and active rotational damping. Hardware experiments with soft tactile differential-drive robots achieve a velocity direction error of 0.61 deg +/- 0.79 deg over five trials with a fixed transport direction and demonstrate object transport through waypoints with three robots.

summary.en: The paper proposes DNPush, a distributed nonparallel pushing force controller for cooperative object transport without inter-robot communication. Robots regulate force magnitudes using local force measurements, assigned weights, and locally expressed desired directions; online control does not require an object model, contact locations, a center-of-mass estimate, or moment-arm magnitudes. Under stated contact conditions, Lyapunov analysis establishes convergence to a unique rotational equilibrium and alignment of object velocity with the desired direction. Simulations examine the mechanism, while hardware experiments demonstrate transport with tactile differential-drive robots.
summary.zh: 论文提出 DNPush，一种无需机器人间通信的分布式非平行推力控制器，用于多机器人协同搬运物体。各机器人依据本地力测量、预设力权重和局部期望运输方向调节非平行力大小；在线控制不需要物体模型、接触位置、质心估计或力臂大小。在所述接触条件下，李雅普诺夫分析证明系统收敛到唯一旋转平衡，物体速度方向趋近期望方向。仿真分析控制机制；硬件实验使用软触觉差速机器人，报告了五次试验的方向误差，并展示三机器人经路径点搬运物体。

items.title: DNPush: Distributed Nonparallel Pushing Force Control of Multi-Robot Systems for Object Transportation

We characterize this gap through end-to-end latency measurements of model inference and the robot execution chain. Repeated Flow Matching denoising contributes substantially to inference cost, while robot-side delays mainly arise from perception acquisition, communication scheduling, and physical response. Analysis of the velocity field shows relatively stable magnitude and direction in early integration, followed by stronger directional correction near the

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models face a timing gap between low-rate inference and high-rate robot execution. We characterize this gap through end-to-end latency measurements of model inference and the robot execution chain.

Repeated Flow Matching denoising contributes substantially to inference cost, while robot-side delays mainly arise from perception acquisition, communication scheduling, and physical response.

Analysis of the velocity field shows relatively stable magnitude and direction in early integration, followed by stronger directional correction near the terminal steps. Based on this stage heterogeneity, we propose two-stage non-uniform denoising, reducing the number of steps from 10 to 2 and model-inference time from 61.557 ms to 21.956 ms.

We also develop a distributed real-time VLA framework with independent inference, action-publication, and robot-control rates, modular observation acquisition, and action-provenance logging. Using {\pi}0.5 as the baseline, we evaluate six real-time execution methods on a long-horizon physical garment-folding task.

Legato performs best overall among training-based methods, while Temporal Smoothing leads among training-free methods; both perform strongly in task success, completion time, action continuity, and acceleration smoothness.

Combining two-step denoising with representative execution methods substantially reduces inference cost with a small reduction in task performance. These results motivate joint optimization of model-inference efficiency and robot-system timing.

summary.en: The paper studies the timing gap between vision-language-action inference and robot execution, attributing substantial inference cost to repeated Flow Matching denoising and robot-side delays mainly to perception, communication scheduling, and physical response. Based on observed variation in the velocity field across integration stages, it proposes two-stage non-uniform denoising, reducing steps from 10 to 2 and inference time from 61.557 ms to 21.956 ms. With π0.5 as baseline, six execution methods are evaluated on a physical long-horizon garment-folding task. Combining two-step denoising with representative methods lowers inference cost with a small performance reduction.
summary.zh: 论文分析视觉—语言—动作模型推理与机器人执行之间的时延，并指出重复 Flow Matching 去噪是推理成本的重要来源，机器人侧延迟主要来自感知获取、通信调度和物理响应。作者根据速度场在积分早期较稳定、末步方向修正较强的特点，提出两阶段非均匀去噪，将步数从 10 降至 2，模型推理时间从 61.557 毫秒降至 21.956 毫秒。以 π0.5 为基线，作者在实体长时服装折叠任务中比较六种执行方法；结合两步去噪后，推理成本下降而任务表现略有降低。

items.title: Toward Real-Time VLAs: Stage-Aware Two-Step Flow Denoising and System-Level Evaluation

sections.text:
Partnered human-humanoid interaction couples locomotion with continuous physical contact. A humanoid needs to coordinate with a person's motion while responding to interaction forces and maintaining stable and natural movement. We present CoDance, a framework for learning reactive and compliant human-humanoid interaction from video.

We study partnered dancing as a challenging instantiation, where a humanoid coordinates its footsteps with a moving partner and maintains continuous two-hand contact. Given a single video of two human dancers, CoDance retargets their motions into a robot reference and a moving partner.

We introduce a multi-link compliance augmentation that transforms the kinematic demonstration into force-aware training data by adapting the robot reference under structured forces at both hands. Policies trained on this data follow the observed partner while preserving the demonstrated locomotion style and responding compliantly to physical interaction.

In simulation, the policies adapt their footsteps to changes in the partner and reproduce approximately 80% of the wrist displacement encoded by the augmented demonstrations. On a physical humanoid, CoDance enables sustained two-hand dancing with a human partner including repeated transitions between forward and backward motions.

summary.en: The paper presents CoDance, a framework for learning reactive and compliant human-humanoid interaction from video, studied through partnered dancing. From one video of two human dancers, it retargets motion into a robot reference and a moving partner. A multi-link compliance augmentation adapts the reference under structured forces at both hands to create force-aware training data. In simulation, policies adjust footsteps to partner changes and reproduce approximately 80% of the wrist displacement in the augmented demonstrations. A physical humanoid demonstrates sustained two-hand dancing with a human, including repeated transitions between forward and backward motion.
summary.zh: 论文提出 CoDance，从视频学习具反应性和柔顺性的人形机器人交互，并以双人舞为研究场景。给定一段两名人类舞者的视频，方法将动作重定向为机器人参考动作和移动伙伴，并通过多连杆柔顺性增强，在双手结构化受力下调整机器人参考动作，生成力感知训练数据。仿真中，策略能根据伙伴变化调整步伐，并复现增强示范中约 80% 的腕部位移。实体人形机器人实验展示了与人类持续双手接触跳舞，并反复完成前进与后退转换。

items.title: CoDance: Learning Reactive and Compliant Human-Humanoid Interaction from Video

sections.text:
Video planning has emerged as a flexible framework for robot manipulation, in which a generative model predicts a video of task completion, and a downstream module translates the predicted frames into actions.

However, existing methods typically ignore information from past interactions, limiting their ability to adapt to latent physical properties that can only be revealed through trial and error, such as whether a door should be pushed or pulled, or how friction affects object dynamics.

When a plan fails, these methods usually replan from scratch without leveraging the information revealed by the failure. To address this limitation, we introduce RELIC, REplanning with Latent embedding refInement and Candidate rejection, a video planning framework that adapts to hidden physical properties from test-time failures.

RELIC optimizes a latent embedding that captures the environment's hidden physical properties from interaction videos and introduces a rejection-based sampling mechanism that filters out hypotheses inconsistent with prior failures.

Across eight tasks in two simulation suites, RELIC consistently reduces the number of replanning steps required for success, and linear probes show that its embedding captures the hidden parameters from the interaction itself rather than from scene appearance.

Across four challenging real-world robotic manipulation tasks involving hidden interaction modes, e.g., friction, center of mass, and object mass, RELIC raises the one-shot replanning success rate of a video planning baseline from 30.0% to 63.8% after a single physical interaction.

summary.en: The paper presents RELIC, a video-planning framework that optimizes a latent embedding from interaction videos to capture hidden physical properties and uses rejection-based sampling to filter hypotheses inconsistent with prior failures. Across eight tasks in two simulation suites, RELIC reduces the replanning steps needed for success; linear probes indicate that its embedding captures parameters revealed by interaction. In four real-world manipulation tasks, one physical interaction raises a baseline’s one-shot replanning success rate from 30.0% to 63.8%.
summary.zh: 论文提出 RELIC 视频规划框架，通过交互视频优化潜在嵌入，以捕捉环境隐藏的物理属性，并用基于拒绝的采样排除与先前失败不一致的假设。在两套仿真环境的八项任务中，该方法减少了成功所需的重规划步骤；线性探针结果显示嵌入反映交互揭示的隐藏参数。在四项真实机器人操作任务中，单次物理交互后，视频规划基线的一次重规划成功率由30.0%升至63.8%。

items.title: Video Replanning via Latent Embedding Refinement and Rejection-Based Sampling

Our approach enables the efficient discovery of a wide range robust grasp configurations, which serve as reliable starting points for generating diverse prehensile manipulation trajectories on articulated objects. The resulting diversity in manipulation behaviors enhances generalization and adaptability, enabling effective deployment continuously evolving open-world settings.

sections.text:
We propose to use Quality-Diversity (QD) algorithms to solve robotic prehensile manipulation tasks in open-ended environments. Our approach enables the efficient discovery of a wide range robust grasp configurations, which serve as reliable starting points for generating diverse prehensile manipulation trajectories on articulated objects.

The resulting diversity in manipulation behaviors enhances generalization and adaptability, enabling effective deployment continuously evolving open-world settings.

summary.en: The paper proposes using Quality-Diversity (QD) algorithms for robotic prehensile manipulation in open-ended environments. The approach aims to efficiently discover a broad range of robust grasp configurations, which can serve as starting points for generating diverse manipulation trajectories on articulated objects. The authors state that diversity in manipulation behaviors enhances generalization and adaptability for deployment in continuously evolving open-world settings. The abstract does not report specific experimental results.
summary.zh: 论文提出使用质量多样性（QD）算法解决开放环境中的机器人抓取操作任务。该方法旨在高效发现多种稳健的抓取构型，并将其作为起点，为关节式物体生成多样的抓取操作轨迹。作者认为，操作行为的多样性能够增强泛化与适应能力，从而支持在持续演变的开放世界环境中部署。摘要未报告具体实验结果。

items.title: Towards Robust Prehensile Manipulation in Open-Ended Environments

items.intro: arXiv:2610.06331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human demonstrations offer rich examples of precise dexterous manipulation and a promising source of robot training data. However, high-fidelity reproduction of demonstrated motions and hand-object interactions across robot embodiments remains challenging under physical constraints. We present DexForge, a differentiable physics-grounded framework for converting human video demonstrations into high-fidelity robot trajectories. We reconstruct spherical-Gaussian object models and hand-object motion from visual observations, then build a differentiable simulator combining efficient Gaussian collision detection with existing

sections.text:
Human demonstrations offer rich examples of precise dexterous manipulation and a promising source of robot training data. However, high-fidelity reproduction of demonstrated motions and hand-object interactions across robot embodiments remains challenging under physical constraints.

We present DexForge, a differentiable physics-grounded framework for converting human video demonstrations into high-fidelity robot trajectories.

We reconstruct spherical-Gaussian object models and hand-object motion from visual observations, then build a differentiable simulator combining efficient Gaussian collision detection with existing differentiable dynamics.

Based on this simulator, DexForge combines contact-aware kinematic retargeting with force-aware dynamics retargeting: robot-adapted stable contacts guide kinematic reference construction and subsequent gradient-based control refinement for precise physical motion reproduction.

Experiments on 130 DexYCB and HOT3D demonstrations across seven dexterous hands show success-rate gains of approximately 35-53 percentage points over the baseline, with object position and orientation tracking errors on successful trajectories reduced by approximately 34-67% and 71-78%, respectively.

Further experiments demonstrate open-loop transfer to MuJoCo and real-robot execution. Our project page is available at https://wmz1226.github.io/DexForge/

summary.en: The paper presents DexForge, a differentiable physics-grounded framework for converting human video demonstrations into robot trajectories. It reconstructs object models and hand-object motion, then combines contact-aware kinematic retargeting with force-aware dynamics retargeting for control refinement. Experiments covering 130 demonstrations and seven dexterous hands report success-rate gains of about 35–53 percentage points over a baseline. On successful trajectories, position and orientation tracking errors fall by about 34–67% and 71–78%, respectively. The paper also reports open-loop transfer to MuJoCo and real-robot execution.
summary.zh: 论文提出 DexForge，一种基于可微物理的框架，可将人类视频演示转换为机器人轨迹。方法重建物体模型及手物运动，并结合接触感知的运动学重定向和力感知的动力学重定向进行控制优化。在涵盖130段演示和七种灵巧手的实验中，相较基线，成功率提高约35至53个百分点；成功轨迹的位置与姿态跟踪误差分别降低约34%至67%和71%至78%。论文还报告了向 MuJoCo 的开环迁移及真实机器人执行。

items.title: DexForge: High-Fidelity Physics-Informed Dexterous Retargeting

sections.text:
We present RAGrasp, a retrieval-augmented pipeline for planar parallel-jaw grasping from a compact set of locally collected, grasp-annotated RGB-D (color and depth) templates.

Unlike task-specific predictors trained primarily on large public or synthetic grasp datasets, RAGrasp requires no end-to-end retraining for a new deployment.Its template memory is constructed from observations collected with the deployment camera, robot, and gripper in the target workspace, thereby aligning stored examples with the local sensing and embodiment conditions.

The system uses self-supervised DINOv2 visual fea- tures together with appearance and depth cues to prompt the Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2), which isolates the query object. A two-stage geometry-semantic retrieval cascade then selects a template, and a confidence gate chooses one of two grasp- transfer estimators.

The transferred grasp is refined using mask- support and silhouette-contact constraints before calibrated 2D- to-3D conversion. In real-world trials, RAGrasp achieves 20/20 successful grasps on seen objects and 19/20 on unseen objects.

Within the evaluated setting, the results demonstrate deployment- specific grasp adaptation from limited local annotation and tolerance to the tested viewpoint and illumination changes.

summary.en: The paper presents RAGrasp, a pipeline for planar parallel-jaw grasping using a compact set of locally collected RGB-D templates annotated with grasps. It segments query objects using visual features, appearance, and depth cues, retrieves a template through a two-stage geometry-semantic cascade, and selects a grasp-transfer estimator based on confidence. The transferred grasp is refined and converted to 3D. In real-world trials, it succeeds on 20/20 seen objects and 19/20 unseen objects. Within the evaluated setting, the authors report adaptation from limited local annotation and tolerance to tested viewpoint and illumination changes.
summary.zh: 论文提出 RAGrasp，通过少量本地采集并标注抓取信息的 RGB-D 模板，实现平行夹爪的平面抓取。系统结合视觉特征、外观与深度线索分割查询物体，再以两阶段几何和语义检索选择模板，并依据置信度选择抓取迁移估计器；迁移结果经过约束细化并转换为三维坐标。真实场景试验中，已见物体抓取成功20/20，未见物体19/20。作者称，在评估设置内，该方法可利用有限本地标注适配部署，并能容忍所测试的视角和光照变化。

items.title: RAGrasp: Geometry-Semantic Template Retrieval and Grasp Transfer

items.intro: arXiv:2610.05792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robotic minimally invasive surgery offers well-documented clinical benefits, but the cost and infrastructure requirements of purpose-built platforms limit access in rural and lower-resourced facilities. Recent work has teleoperated general-purpose robots for laparoscopic tasks and in vivo procedures, but relied on handheld instruments coupled through passive linkages rather than native robotic actuation. Instead, we adapt da Vinci Classic and Xi instruments onto general-purpose robots that can integrate in clinical workflows. We present DASH, a

sections.text:
Robotic minimally invasive surgery offers well-documented clinical benefits, but the cost and infrastructure requirements of purpose-built platforms limit access in rural and lower-resourced facilities.

Recent work has teleoperated general-purpose robots for laparoscopic tasks and in vivo procedures, but relied on handheld instruments coupled through passive linkages rather than native robotic actuation. Instead, we adapt da Vinci Classic and Xi instruments onto general-purpose robots that can integrate in clinical workflows.

We present DASH, a da Vinci Adapter for Serial-link and Humanoid platforms, consisting of two types of adapters that require no modification to the instruments themselves.

Each adapter is compatible with many robotic platform load capacities, engages the instrument's native latch, and wirelessly identifies inserted tools to load instrument-specific kinematics and coupling matrices. Teleoperated experiments demonstrate the efficacy of DASH and its benefits for enabling research access to surgical robotic platforms.

summary.en: The paper presents DASH, an adapter platform for mounting da Vinci Classic and Xi instruments on general-purpose serial-link and humanoid robots without modifying the instruments. Its adapters accommodate a range of robot load capacities, engage the instruments’ native latch, and wirelessly identify inserted tools to load instrument-specific kinematics and coupling matrices. Teleoperated experiments demonstrate DASH’s efficacy and its potential to broaden research access to surgical robotic platforms.
summary.zh: 论文提出 DASH，一种将 da Vinci Classic 和 Xi 手术器械安装到通用串联机器人及人形机器人上的适配器平台，无需改动器械本身。适配器可适配多种机器人负载能力，接合器械原有锁扣，并通过无线方式识别器械，以载入相应运动学和耦合矩阵。遥操作实验展示了该平台的有效性及其对手术机器人研究的支持作用。

items.title: DASH: A da Vinci Adapter for Serial-link and Humanoid Robots as an Accessible Platform for Surgical Robotics Research

items.intro: arXiv:2608.17129v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have shown promising spatial reasoning capabilities from static visual inputs, where the evidence needed to answer a question is available in the provided views. However, in cluttered environments, answer-relevant evidence may be occluded rather than absent: an object may lie beneath a pile, be covered by another object, or have identifying information facing away from the camera. Answering such questions requires physical interaction to reveal the hidden evidence. We formalize

sections.text:
Vision-language models (VLMs) have shown promising spatial reasoning capabilities from static visual inputs, where the evidence needed to answer a question is available in the provided views.

However, in cluttered environments, answer-relevant evidence may be occluded rather than absent: an object may lie beneath a pile, be covered by another object, or have identifying information facing away from the camera. Answering such questions requires physical interaction to reveal the hidden evidence.

We formalize this setting as Manipulation-Grounded Visual Question Answering (MG-VQA), where an agent answers a question about an initially cluttered scene by using manipulation as an intermediate evidence-gathering operation.

We introduce MG-VQA-Bench, comprising 600 human-verified questions across four spatial reasoning tasks, and evaluate it in a cluttered tabletop interactive environment.

Eight VLMs are evaluated under three levels of environment access: Direct (image only), Perception (pointing, segmentation, and scene graphs), and Manipulation (perception, grasping, and pushing).

Across all models, Direct and Perception achieve average success rates of 36.2% and 37.6%, respectively, only slightly above an image-blind chance baseline of 32.7%.In contrast, Manipulation raises average success to 56.8% (40.8-83.0% across models).

Stronger tool-calling VLMs, GPT~6~Astra (83.0%) and Gemini~3.8~Flash (69.3%), search persistently and re-ground after unsuccessful interactions, while weaker models often answer without gathering sufficient evidence or stop prematurely after failed actions.

Our results highlight the need for VLM agents that use manipulation for persistent, physically grounded evidence gathering and recovery. Code and benchmark is available here: https://github.com/vineet2104/MG-VQA

summary.en: The paper defines manipulation-grounded visual question answering (MG-VQA), in which an agent manipulates a cluttered scene to reveal evidence needed to answer a question. The authors introduce a benchmark of 600 human-verified questions across four spatial reasoning tasks and evaluate eight vision-language models in an interactive tabletop environment. In these evaluations, adding grasping and pushing yields higher average success than image-only or perception-level access. The authors emphasize persistent physical evidence gathering and recovery after unsuccessful actions.
summary.zh: 论文将操作接地视觉问答（MG-VQA）定义为：智能体通过操作场景来显露被遮挡的证据，从而回答初始杂乱场景中的问题。作者提出包含四类空间推理任务、经人工验证的 600 个问题的基准，并在桌面交互环境中评测八种视觉语言模型。实验显示，加入抓取和推动能力后，模型平均成功率高于仅使用图像或感知信息；作者指出，持续收集物理证据并在失败后恢复仍是关键能力。

items.title: MG-VQA: Manipulation Grounded Visual Question Answering with VLMs

items.intro: arXiv:2610.05796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimisation-based parking planners usually impose collision constraints only at the time samples, so a vehicle corner can cut an obstacle between samples, and no executable trajectory exists until the solver converges. We present a planner for car-like vehicles with reverse gear in which every iterate of the optimisation phase satisfies the discretised dynamics exactly and keeps the whole vehicle rectangle clear of obstacles between the samples. Each time interval receives one convex corridor

sections.text:
Optimisation-based parking planners usually impose collision constraints only at the time samples, so a vehicle corner can cut an obstacle between samples, and no executable trajectory exists until the solver converges.

We present a planner for car-like vehicles with reverse gear in which every iterate of the optimisation phase satisfies the discretised dynamics exactly and keeps the whole vehicle rectangle clear of obstacles between the samples.

Each time interval receives one convex corridor that holds all vehicle corners at both ends and is shrunk by a sweep margin bounding how far the corner paths leave their chords.

Separating half-planes give the corridors a direction out of obstacles when the initial guess is in collision; later, heading-aligned boxes are grown from the speed, curvature and step of the current iterate and rebuilt after accepted steps.

A feasibility-perturbed trust-region sequential quadratic programming method projects each step onto the dynamics by feedback and verifies it exactly; the cost decreases monotonically, and once the corridors stop changing, limit points are Karush-Kuhn-Tucker points of the corridor-constrained problem or violate a constraint qualification.

On 820 benchmark cases the planner succeeds in 818 without penetration (797 from the first initial guess), none of the 7103 evaluated optimisation-phase iterates is unusable, and it succeeds in 96.5% of the cases when 99% of the initial guesses intersect an obstacle.

Its maneuvers take 0.7% longer in the median than those of a similarly certified exact-collision baseline. The guarantees hold for the planning model, not for a physical vehicle.

summary.en: The paper presents a motion planner for car-like vehicles with reverse gear. Its optimization iterates satisfy discretized dynamics and use convex corridors with sweep margins to keep the full vehicle clear of obstacles between time samples. A trust-region sequential quadratic programming method projects steps back onto the dynamics. In benchmark evaluations, the planner succeeds in 818 of 820 cases. The authors clarify that the guarantees apply to the planning model and do not establish equivalent guarantees for a physical vehicle.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种面向可倒车类汽车的非完整运动规划器。优化过程中，每次迭代都满足离散动力学，并通过凸走廊和扫掠裕量约束车辆整体在采样点之间避开障碍；信赖域序列二次规划方法则将迭代投影回动力学约束。基准测试中，规划器在 820 个案例中成功处理 818 个。作者强调，这些保证针对规划模型成立，不代表真实车辆也获得相同保证。

items.title: Dynamics-Aware Adaptive Corridors with Feasibility-Perturbed Trust-Region SQP for Certified Nonholonomic Motion Planning

In real interactions, however, entering an instruction can take several seconds, leaving the policy idle for a substantial fraction of the interaction.
